docs.text:
Document Adding a New Operator — Checklist Version 1.0 Status Living Document Audience Anyone deploying a new Helm chart, operator, or internal tool onto the cluster Purpose The ordered, cross-repo checklist so nothing gets silently skipped (namespace, RBAC, netpol, mTLS...). Last Updated July 2026

Worked examples referenced throughout: Reflector (cross-namespace ConfigMap replication, apps/platform/cfg/reflector), VPA (apps/foundation/auto-scale/vpa), and Goldilocks (apps/foundation/auto-scale/goldilocks) — added together in one pass, so they cover most of the variation you'll hit (single-component vs multi-component chart, inbound-serving vs controller-only, needs kube-apiserver access, needs external ingress).

docs.title: 0. Research before writing anything
docs.text:
• Check the chart's actual latest version and repo. Don't trust a version a teammate remembers — helm repo add <name> <url> && helm search repo <name>/<chart> --versions and use the top result. Prefer the chart maintained by the upstream project itself over third-party repackagings when both exist (e.g. VPA: kubernetes.github.io/autoscaler, the official kubernetes-sig-autoscaling chart, not a third-party mirror — check for one before assuming the first Helm repo you find is canonical).
  • Read the chart's own RBAC template, not just its values.yaml prose. Chart-bundled ClusterRoles are often broader than the workload actually needs (e.g. Reflector's chart grants configmaps and secrets with no values.yaml toggle to split them). If it's too broad and there's no values-level way to scope it down, plan on rbac.enabled: false + a hand-written ClusterRole in k8s-security (§3).
  • helm template your actual values before committing them. This catches real bugs — chart-level validation errors, wrong key names, mutually-exclusive options set together — that pure YAML linting won't. Do this for every profile (base + each of dev/stage/prod), not just one.
  • Figure out what the workload's pods actually need to reach, and what needs to reach them. This drives §5 (netpol) and is much easier to get right before deploying than to reverse-engineer from a mysteriously-hanging pod afterward. In particular: does it need kube-apiserver access (most controllers do)? Does anything outside the mesh call into it directly (e.g. an admission webhook, called by kube-apiserver itself, which has no sidecar)?

docs.title: 1. budy-cloud-management — create the namespace
docs.text: Add an entry to v2/stacks/shared-infra/k8s/v1/namespaces.tf (ob1-tf-eks-<name>-ns-1). If the workload has an opt-in-per-namespace pattern (see §7), this is also where those labels get added to other namespaces, not the new one.

docs.title: 2. argocd-critical-stack — AppProject
docs.text:
• Prefer reusing an existing project. Check whether the tier's project already has the namespace pre-staged as a commented-out destination (a sign someone planned for this).
  • If reusing: add the chart's Helm repo URL to sourceRepos (if not already present) and the new namespace to destinations.
  • If a genuinely new access pattern (e.g. governance-scoped, like pfm-cfg-sources-acd-proj-1 which only allows ConfigMap into one namespace): create a new project, tightly scoped — don't default to namespaceResourceWhitelist: [{group: '*', kind: '*'}] unless the workload genuinely needs broad object creation.

docs.title: 3. argocd-eks-stack — the app itself
docs.text:
• app.yaml + values/base.values.yaml + one values file per profile (dev/stage/prod), following the exact structure in Repos & the App Model.
  • Pin the chart version with ~x.y.z.
  • Set deployedReleaseName to <name>-1.
  • Always keep the real defaults beside the values files that override them: values/default.values.yaml, unmodified and never referenced by app.yaml. Fetch the exact pinned chart version with helm pull <repo-or-oci-chart> --version <x> --untar and copy the extracted chart's values.yaml; alternatively, filter OCI transport lines from helm show values <repo-or-oci-chart> --version <x> before writing the file. Refresh this reference in the same PR whenever the chart version changes. Never hand-type it from memory or include Helm transport output such as Pulled:/Digest: lines.
  • If the chart's default RBAC is broader than needed: rbac.enabled: false here, then write the narrower ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding in k8s-security (§4).
  • Add budybot.io/netpol to every Pod template the chart creates (podLabels: {"budybot.io/netpol": <name>-1}, or the chart's equivalent — some charts call it additionalLabels under a deployment: block; check the rendered output, do not assume the field name). This is required for the k8s-security netpol convention (§5) to select the workload. For multi-component charts, give each component a distinct value (<name>-1-<component>) when they have different network requirements. Add every value to the namespace-scoped, deny-mode BudyNetpolIdentity allow-list in k8s-security. Plain app labels are legacy and must not be used for new selectors.
  • helm template the final base+profile-layered values against the real chart one more time after adding labels, to confirm nothing broke.

docs.title: 4. k8s-security — RBAC (only if you disabled the chart's own)
docs.text: v1/objects/rbac/cluster/manifests/<name>-ns-1/: a ClusterRole scoped to exactly the verbs/resources needed, a ClusterRoleBinding to the workload's ServiceAccount (name must match serviceAccount.name set in the app's values), and wire the new directory into rbac/cluster/manifests/kustomization.yaml's resources: list. No new ArgoCD app needed — this rides on the existing apps/foundation/rbac/cluster app.

docs.title: 5. k8s-security — NetworkPolicy / CiliumNetworkPolicy
docs.text:
Every new namespace needs its own netpol directory, even if it feels like overkill for a single controller pod. See Network Policy & mTLS for the full pattern; summary:

  • <name>-ns-1/ingress/namespace-wide.default-deny.yaml — always. Deny-by-default, matched on k8s:budybot.io/netpol Exists.
  • <name>-ns-1/ingress/<workload>.{netpol,ciliumnetpol}.yaml — only for components that actually receive inbound traffic (a dashboard behind the gateway, an admission webhook). Most controller-only workloads need zero positive ingress rules.
  • <name>-ns-1/egress/namespace-wide.allow-required.yaml — DNS (CoreDNS) + istiod (15012). Copy verbatim from any existing namespace.
  • <name>-ns-1/egress/namespace-wide.deny-missing-netpol-label.yaml — catch-all deny for anything that lacks budybot.io/netpol. Check Helm-hook Jobs (cert-gen jobs, migration jobs): give them an approved network-policy label and narrow allow when they need traffic, or a deliberate reviewed exclusion when bootstrap-only.
  • <name>-ns-1/egress/<workload>.allow-required.yaml — whatever the workload actually needs: DB access, kube-apiserver (controllers almost always need this — use Cilium's kube-apiserver entity, not a static CIDR, since the EKS control plane isn't a cluster pod), other internal services.
  • Wire the new namespace directory into netpol/manifests/kustomization.yaml's top-level resources: list.

docs.title: 6. k8s-security — mTLS (PeerAuthentication)
docs.text:
The mesh has sidecar injection on cluster-wide, but not every namespace has explicit PeerAuthentication set — check current state before assuming STRICT is already enforced elsewhere. When adding one:

  • <name>-1-strict-mtls.peerauthentication.yaml, spec.mtls.mode: STRICT, alongside the ingress/egress dirs (not inside either — it's neither).
  • If anything outside the mesh calls the workload directly (most commonly: kube-apiserver calling an admission/conversion webhook), add a portLevelMtls PERMISSIVE exception for just that port. Forgetting this silently breaks the webhook the moment STRICT mTLS is applied — the caller has no sidecar and no cert, so the plaintext connection gets rejected. Everything else in the namespace stays STRICT.
  • portLevelMtls port keys must be quoted strings in YAML ("8000":, not 8000:) — Istio's API represents them as map<uint32, ...>, which the JSON/YAML conversion kustomize build performs requires as string keys. An unquoted integer key fails the build with a cryptic unsupported type error.
  • Confirm the project (fnd-network-policy-acd-proj-1 today) whitelists security.istio.io/PeerAuthentication in namespaceResourceWhitelist — it may not, if this is the first namespace to use it.

docs.title: 7. If the workload dashboards/UIs need external access
docs.text: Follow the existing OIDC-protected ingress pattern rather than inventing a new one: apps/foundation/gtw/ingress/manifests/oidc-protected/<name>.ingress.yaml — a networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress (ALB, routes to istio-gateway-1:443) plus an Istio VirtualService (routes from the gateway to the workload's actual Service), host <name>.ENV.orangebox.ai. The ENV placeholder is substituted per-environment automatically by the existing Kustomize replacements transform in env/<environment>/apps/foundation/gtw/ingress/manifests/kustomization.yaml — don't hardcode an environment name into the shared manifest, and don't create a new per-environment ingress file; the substitution mechanism already handles it. Add the new file to oidc-protected/kustomization.yaml's resources: list.

docs.title: 8. If the workload has an opt-in-per-namespace pattern
docs.text: Some tools (Goldilocks, Reflector) don't act on every namespace by default — they require a namespace-level label or annotation to opt in. If you're adding such a tool: document what the label/annotation is in the app's base.values.yaml as a comment, and don't flip any global "watch everything" flag as a shortcut — label the specific namespaces you actually want covered, in budy-cloud-management's namespaces.tf (§1).

docs.title: 9. Verify before opening PRs
docs.text:
• helm template (or kubectl kustomize for type: git apps) every layer combination you touched. This is cheap and catches real errors — mutually exclusive chart options, bad label selectors, broken relative Kustomize paths — before they hit a live cluster.
  • For netpol changes specifically: kubectl kustomize v1/objects/netpol/manifests should build the entire tree cleanly, not just your new namespace's subtree — a bad relative path or duplicate resource name elsewhere can break the whole app.
  • Cross-check that every resource name your new ClusterRoleBinding/CiliumNetworkPolicy/Ingress references (ServiceAccount name, Service name, app label value) actually matches what the Helm chart renders — don't guess these, render the chart and read them off the output.

docs.title: Common Mistakes (from real PRs)
docs.text:
• Writing an app.yaml values file that assumes a chart field exists without rendering the chart to confirm — chart schemas change between major versions and third-party repackagings diverge from upstream.
  • Applying STRICT mTLS without checking whether anything outside the mesh (control plane webhooks, external health checkers) talks to the workload in plaintext.
  • Forgetting that Helm-hook Jobs (cert-gen, DB migrations) often don't inherit the same pod labels as the main Deployment/StatefulSet — they need their own netpol carve-out.
  • Using a static CIDR block for kube-apiserver egress/ingress instead of Cilium's kube-apiserver entity — CIDRs drift, the entity doesn't.
  • Skipping the namespace's NetworkPolicy/CiliumNetworkPolicy entirely because "it's just a controller pod with no inbound traffic" — it still needs an explicit ingress default-deny and an egress allow-list; leaving it unmanaged means it's implicitly allow-all, not deny-all.

docs.title: Application Cluster CI/CD Standard
docs.text:
Document Application Cluster CI/CD Standard Version 0.1 Status Draft target standard — current applications should converge incrementally Audience Application engineers, platform engineers, release approvers, and Kargo operators Purpose Define efficient validation, versioning, image/module/chart release, GitOps update, tags, approvals, and rollback. Last Updated July 2026

This document standardizes CI/CD for self-contained application clusters containing approximately 6–10 releasable units: one Nexus Go contract module, one parent Helm chart, and normally 5–7 component images in a single application ECR image repository.

The current Context Cluster pipeline is the functional reference. The common Go modules repository is the structural reference for dynamic change detection, JSON matrices, and reusable validation/release workflows.

docs.title: 1. Artifact and version model
docs.text:
Artifact Count per application cluster Version/tag rule Registry/repository Container image repository Exactly one All components share it Application image ECR repo in ecr-1 Component image One per deployable component <component>-<component-version>-<short-sha> Shared application image repo Parent Helm chart Exactly one published chart Chart.yaml version and appVersion are identical Application Helm ECR repo Local Helm subchart One per component where useful Bundled into parent; not published independently Application source repo Nexus Go contract module Normally one public contract module SemVer plus module-directory-prefixed Git tag Application Git repository Component Git release tag One per released image component <component>/v<component-version> Application Git repository Parent chart Git tag One per published chart charts/<parent-chart>/v<chart-version> Application Git repository

Image tags and Git tags are immutable. Never move an existing tag to another commit or digest.

For Go modules below the repository root, Go requires the relative module directory to prefix the semantic version tag. A module at shared/contract version v1.4.0 therefore uses shared/contract/v1.4.0. This is required for consumers to resolve the Nexus contract correctly, not merely a naming preference. See the Go multi-module repository guidance.

docs.title: 2. Required GitHub variables and secrets
docs.text:
Use the Context Cluster names as the current organization contract.

Name Type Used for GLOBAL_REFPACKAGE_APP_1_ID Organization/repository variable GitHub App client ID for private Go modules/contracts GLOBAL_REFPACKAGE_APP_1_PEM Organization/repository secret GitHub App private key for private Go modules/contracts GLOBAL_GITOPS_APP_1_ID Organization/repository variable GitHub App client ID for GitOps PRs GLOBAL_GITOPS_APP_1_PEM Organization/repository secret GitHub App private key for GitOps PRs AWS_ECR_1 Variable Central ECR account ID AWS_REGION_MAIN Variable ECR region GLOBAL_VAR_AWS_ECR_IMAGE_BUILDER_2_ROLE_1_ARN Variable AWS OIDC role for image/chart publication GLOBAL_ECR_HELM_REPO_V1 Variable Helm OCI root/prefix; append the parent chart name

Generate a short-lived token with actions/create-github-app-token from the REF PACKAGE App. Pass it into Docker only as BuildKit secret github_token. Consume it in RUN --mount=type=secret,id=github_token; never persist it through ARG, ENV, copied credential files, final image layers, logs, or exported cache.

docs.title: 3. Component manifest: one source of release metadata
docs.text:
Do not repeat component names and paths across every workflow. Keep a machine-readable component catalog in the application repository, for example .github/components.json:

{
  "components": [
    {
      "name": "gateway",
      "path": "components/gateway",
      "packageFile": "components/gateway/package.json",
      "dockerTarget": "components/gateway",
      "imageValuesPath": ".gateway.image.tag",
      "goModule": false
    },
    {
      "name": "file",
      "path": "components/file",
      "packageFile": "components/file/package.json",
      "dockerTarget": "components/file",
      "imageValuesPath": ".\"file\".image.tag",
      "goModule": false
    },
    {
      "name": "nexus-contract",
      "path": "shared/contract",
      "packageFile": "shared/contract/package.json",
      "goModule": true,
      "publishImage": false
    }
  ],
  "parentChart": {
    "path": "charts/context-cluster",
    "name": "context-cluster-1-repo-1"
  }
}

A detector reads this catalog plus the PR/main diff and Changesets, then emits JSON matrices for validation, image publication, Go module tags, and chart-value updates. Adding component 8 should normally require one catalog entry—not edits to six workflow files.

docs.title: 4. Pull request validation
docs.text: Every PR targeting main proves the eventual release is buildable before approval.

docs.title: Detect once
docs.text:
Create one detect-changes job that outputs:

  • changed_components: component matrix selected by changed paths;
  • release_components: components named by Changesets;
  • changed_go_modules and changed_contract_modules;
  • chart_changed: parent or local subchart/chart-library changes;
  • workflow_changed: forces validation of all components;
  • requires_changeset: application/module changes that need a version bump.

Use the PR merge base, not only the previous commit. Workflow/catalog changes validate all components because they can break the entire release mechanism.

docs.title: Validate selected components
docs.text:
Use a matrix job or a matrix calling a reusable workflow. Each selected component performs the checks relevant to it:

  • private dependency resolution using the REF PACKAGE GitHub App;
  • go mod download, build, vet/lint, unit tests, workflow replay/contract tests;
  • Docker build with push: false and the real Dockerfile/target/platform;
  • generated-code/schema consistency checks;
  • changeset-to-component validation.

Validate the parent chart once after component jobs:

  • Helm dependencies resolve;
  • helm lint and helm template succeed with CI-safe values;
  • all image values paths in the component catalog exist;
  • Chart.yaml version == appVersion;
  • no subchart is configured for independent publication;
  • rendered Temporal/VSO/RBAC labels and references are internally consistent.

The required branch-protection check should be a stable aggregate job such as ci-required, which depends on detection, matrix validation, chart validation, and consistency checks. Individual matrix job names can evolve without constantly rewriting branch protection.

docs.title: 5. Release state machine
docs.text:
Release workflows run only from main or from temporary automation branches created by the workflow. Do not use release/ in ephemeral branch names because those branches match protected long-lived release rules and may not be deleted after merge.

Use names such as:

  • automation/version-packages;
  • automation/chart-release/<chart-name>;
  • automation/gitops-chart-bump/<application>.

docs.title: Application-code release
docs.text:
Feature PR approved and merged
  → version-packages PR created/updated from Changesets
  → version-packages PR approved and merged
  → detect released components
  → matrix builds/pushes only released component images
  → publish only changed Nexus Go module tags/releases
  → create component Git tags/releases
  → chart-release PR updates released image tags
     and bumps parent chart version + appVersion together
  → chart-release PR approved and merged
  → publish parent chart + chart Git tag/release
  → create GitOps chart-version PR
  → GitOps PR approved and merged

Publication runs from main after the version-packages / chart-release PR merges; that merge is the human gate. A component that has no consumed Changeset is not rebuilt or republished.

docs.title: Chart-only release
docs.text:
Chart PR approved and merged
  → chart-release PR generates a Git-style chart-file changelog
     and bumps parent chart version + appVersion together
  → chart-release PR approved and merged
  → publish parent chart + chart Git tag/release
  → create GitOps chart-version PR
  → GitOps PR approved and merged

No component image or Go module is published. This path has one application-repository chart-release PR plus the GitOps PR.

docs.title: Avoid release loops
docs.text:
Classify the merge before acting:

  • ordinary merge with Changesets → create/update version-packages PR;
  • version-packages PR merge → application publication;
  • ordinary chart-only merge → create/update chart-release PR;
  • chart-release PR merge → chart publication and GitOps PR;
  • workflow-generated metadata/tag commits → no new version PR.

Use explicit PR labels or a machine-readable release marker, plus changed-file validation, instead of guessing solely from commit-message text.

docs.title: 6. Efficient matrix architecture
docs.text:
Use three layers:

  1. Thin event workflows: pr-ci.yml, main-version.yml, publish-application.yml, publish-chart.yml.
  2. The organization shared library Budybot/ob1_mn_github_platform-actions_repo_1: validate-go-module.yml, build-image.yml, publish-go-module.yml, publish-chart.yml, and gitops-update.yml; retain a same-repository wrapper only when it expresses application-specific release state.
  3. Component catalog and detector script/action that emit matrices.

GitHub supports a matrix job calling a reusable workflow. This is the right fit for 5–7 similar images: the top-level workflow remains readable, components run in parallel, and each receives explicit catalog inputs. Pin third-party actions to immutable SHAs or reviewed release tags, and pin the organization's platform-actions library to its moving major tag @v1 (@v1.x.y only to freeze a caller deliberately). The organization setting lets GitHub fetch private reusable workflow YAML with its scoped ephemeral token; the REF PACKAGE App is only for private Go source/module access. Pass the GitOps App key only to the GitOps update call. GitHub recommends reusable workflows to avoid duplication.

For Go multi-module repositories, enable actions/setup-go cache with a cache-dependency-path covering every **/go.sum and **/go.work.sum file. Do not rely on the default root-only lookup, which produces warnings or stale cache keys when go.mod files are below the repository root. A module-specific override is allowed only when that module has no workspace or cross-module dependency input.

Recommended matrix controls:

  • fail-fast: false on PR validation so all failing components are visible;
  • max-parallel tuned to runner/ECR capacity;
  • image publish matrix includes only consumed Changeset packages;
  • separate contract-module and image matrices because tag semantics differ;
  • one chart-update aggregation job after all image builds, because concurrent matrix jobs must not each edit the same values file/branch.

docs.title: 7. Approvals, concurrency, and permissions
docs.text:
There are no per-release approval environments. The human gate is merging the version-packages PR and the chart-release PR; promotion between environments is gated by Kargo bake checks; and the platform-actions release-PR sweeper auto-merges the automation PRs. The only protected GitHub Environment in the flow is release-automation (limited to main), which holds the sweeper's GitHub App key. GitOps write credentials remain isolated to the GitOps PR job/App.

GitHub environment jobs cannot access environment secrets until protection rules pass. Use least-privilege job-level permissions and OIDC for AWS rather than stored AWS keys. See GitHub deployment environments.

Concurrency:

  • cancel stale PR CI for the same PR;
  • serialize version-PR mutation per repository;
  • serialize application publication per application cluster without canceling an in-progress publish;
  • serialize chart publication per parent chart;
  • serialize GitOps PR updates per application path.

Do not reuse the exact same concurrency group in caller and called reusable workflows; GitHub warns this can cancel the caller. GitHub concurrency groups allow matrix and needs contexts.

docs.title: 8. Tags and Kargo discovery
docs.text:
Create tags only after the artifact exists and its digest/version has been verified.

Signal Format Consumer Component image <component>-<version>-<short-sha> Helm values and Kargo image subscription Component Git tag <component>/v<version> Audit/release history Nexus module Git tag <module-dir>/v<version> Other Go applications importing the contract Parent chart version/tag SemVer and charts/<parent>/v<version> ArgoCD/Kargo chart subscription

Because prefixed component image tags are not pure SemVer, Kargo configuration must use one image subscription per component with an anchored allow-regex and a strategy compatible with immutable build tags. Do not let one subscription select another component's tags from the shared image repository. The concrete Kargo strategy, regex, and discovery limit will be added during Kargo implementation in Kargo Promotion Design.

The parent chart remains SemVer and is the preferred aggregate release signal after all selected component image tags are written into chart values.

docs.title: 9. Idempotency and rollback
docs.text:
Every publication job must be rerun-safe:

  • if an image tag exists, verify it points to the expected digest or fail;
  • if a Go/chart/component Git tag exists, verify its commit or fail;
  • if a chart version exists, compare expected metadata and skip or fail safely;
  • update an existing automation PR rather than opening duplicates;
  • use immutable prior chart versions for rollback;
  • never overwrite ECR tags or Git tags.

The GitOps PR is the deployment handoff. Publishing an artifact does not deploy it.

docs.title: Reviewer PR handoff
docs.text:
For every generated or human release PR, put the release sequence directly in the PR description. Use [release N/M] in the title and include Prerequisites, Next approval, Reviewer action, and Rollback/hold point. Name the precise next state: for example, version-packages PR #12 in <application repo>, chart-release PR #123 in <application repo>, or GitOps PR #456 in <group GitOps repo>. A reviewer should never need to infer whether to approve now, wait for a workflow, or move to another repository.

When the next PR does not yet exist, say which workflow creates it and the condition that triggers it; replace that text with its link as soon as it is opened. For a chart-only release this produces one application-repository chart-release PR followed by one GitOps PR. For an application release it produces the version-packages PR, the chart-release PR, then the GitOps PR, with only changed components in the matrix.

docs.title: 10. Target workflow inventory
docs.text:
Workflow Trigger Responsibility pr-ci.yml PR to main Detect, matrix validate/build without push, chart render, aggregate required check main-version.yml Ordinary merge to main Create/update version-packages PR or chart-release PR publish-application.yml Version-packages PR merge Approval, matrix image/module publication, tags, then chart-release PR publish-chart.yml Chart-release PR merge Approval, parent chart publication/tag/release, then GitOps PR reusable-validate-component.yml workflow_call Validate one catalog component reusable-build-image.yml workflow_call Build/push/verify one selected image reusable-publish-go-module.yml workflow_call Test and tag/release one selected Go module gitops-update.yml workflow_call Update pinned chart version and open/update GitOps PR

The exact filenames may vary, but the state boundaries and responsibilities should remain recognizable.

docs.title: 11. Current reference gaps and adoption
docs.text:
Context Cluster currently proves the release mechanics but hand-wires gateway/file/k8scr/execution-system inputs and build jobs. Converging to this standard should first introduce the component catalog and detection matrix without changing artifact names or approval behavior, then replace repeated build jobs with reusable matrix calls.

Chart-only source changes do not require a Changeset. The chart-release workflow creates the patch version, derives a Git-style changelog from changed chart files, and opens the chart-release PR with that generated changelog. Component Git tags use <component>/v<version>.

The shared-workflow home is ob1_mn_github_platform-actions_repo_1, managed by github-infra and configured for organization-level reusable-workflow access. Kargo selection details belong in Kargo Promotion Design, where they will be decided with the implementation.

docs.title: Recommendation: centralize only proven reusable workflows
docs.text:
Use the dedicated private Actions repository ob1_mn_github_platform-actions_repo_1, managed by github-infra. Keep caller-specific event workflows and the component catalog in each application repository; centralize only tested workflow_call workflows and composite actions. Release that library with semver tags plus a moving major tag, pin callers to @v1, grant organization access explicitly, and keep permissions/credentials scoped to the caller job. GitHub requires a private reusable-workflow repository to be explicitly accessible to its callers; sharing also makes its workflow logs indirectly visible to callers, so it must contain no secrets. See GitHub's private workflow sharing guidance.

Do not use the REF PACKAGE GitHub App to retrieve reusable workflow YAML. GitHub Actions provides the caller runner a scoped, short-lived installation token when the called repository's Actions access level allows it. Retain the REF PACKAGE App only for private Go-module/source access. A separate GitHub App is needed only for explicit API automation outside workflow_call, such as a centrally owned cross-repository PR or release operation; grant it only the specific API permissions it needs.

docs.title: Primary references
docs.text:
• GitHub reusable workflows
  • GitHub workflow concurrency
  • GitHub deployment environments and approvals
  • GitHub protected branches
  • Go multi-module source and tags
  • Kargo Warehouses and image selection

docs.title: Component Authorization Module Standard
docs.text:
Document Component Authorization Module Standard Version 0.2 Status Draft for research and review. New standard for new repositories; no compatibility with context-cluster or dt-manager is planned. Audience Component engineers, platform engineers who approve authorization models, and k8s-security owners Purpose One shared Go module that every component inserts to ask "may subject S have relation R on object O?" against its own OpenFGA model. Last Updated November 2026

Authentication is already standard: an STS bearer token is verified at the gateway (go/capability/gateway/stsauth), and the tenant and user come only from that token. This document standardizes what happens next: authorization. It reflects the owner's decisions of October 2026 and the evidence listed in section 2.

docs.title: 1. Decisions
docs.text: # Decision 1 One shared Go module, go/authz in budy-common-modules. Any component, in any cluster, inserts it and tells it which relation to check on which object. 2 No policy decision service. The module calls the existing read-only OpenFGA proxy (openfga-1-readonly-proxy) over HTTP. It does not use Nexus and does not call sts-service. 3 No service identity and no token handling in the module. The proxy is unauthenticated by design; admission is by network policy. The subject comes from the identity the gateway already fixed (ComponentRequest), never from a payload. 4 One shared store with one OpenFGA module per service (the current model of auth-store-2). The platform team approves model changes. 5 The component's model lives in its own repository and is the single reference for the relations the component checks. 6 Authorization is strict. Every capability declares an authorize: block. There is no way to mark a capability public. The only operation without an authorization check is capability discovery (DescribeCapabilities), which still requires a valid token. 7 Checks run at the gateway (coarse, from the manifest) and in component activities (fine, per object). Both use this module. 8 OpenFGA will be locked down, so the read-only proxy becomes the only access path for readers. Models are moving out of argocd-eks-stack into a shared models repository in a parallel workstream; this standard targets "the models repository" and does not depend on which one. 9 OpenFGA module names end in -1, like every platform entity. The 12 existing modules are renamed (argocd-eks-stack PR 1365); nothing else references them. 10 Fail closed. A deny and an outage are different results, and neither is ever read as allow.

docs.title: 2. What exists today (verified in the repositories)
docs.text:
• One store, modular model. argocd-eks-stack, v2/apps/platform/authz/openfga-1/manifests/v2/models/fga.mod (schema 1.2) lists 12 modules: platform-roles, identity, tenant-roles, audience, conditions, context-cluster, infrastructure, credentials, service-access, connections, authz-manager, feature. stores/README.md states there is one OpenFGA store, auth-store-2; the folders under stores/ are tuple seeds, not stores.
  • A service model is a module that extends shared types. context-cluster.fga owns context_scope and context_type and extends platform, tenant and audience with its own relations. Object ids carry the scope, for example context_scope:tenant/acme/meeting.
  • Adding a module touches three hand-maintained lists: fga.mod, the openfga-1-model-v2 ConfigMap generator in v2/kustomization.yaml, and the explicit cp list in jobs/model-bootstrap.job.yaml. The Job also folds every tuple seed into its digest; a changed digest writes a new model and moves the environment's model binding. authz-config_gitops_repo-1 is currently a README only, so today the models are owned by argocd-eks-stack.
  • Read-only proxy. openfga-1-readonly-proxy.yaml is plain nginx. It forwards only POST /stores/<store>/check, /list-objects and /list-users for the one store (port 8080, used by sts-service and sts-service-external) and adds /read on port 8081 (authz-provider). Everything else, including writes, model reads and other stores, gets 403. OpenFGA itself runs with authn.method: none. Callers are admitted per listener by Cilium rules in k8s-security (authz-1-ns-1/ingress/openfga-1-readonly-proxy.allow-*.yaml, matching on namespace and the budybot.io/netpol pod label).
  • Tuples are written only by authz-manager-1. Components never write tuples.
  • The Go side. ComponentRequest carries ScopeType, TenantID, User and SessionBoundary, set by the gateway from the verified token. The manifest has no authorization field today (go/capability/manifest.go), and dispatch.ExecuteWorkflow has no authorization step.

docs.title: 3. Identity rule: no token in the module
docs.text:
The module never sees or forwards a bearer token. The gateway has already verified it. The module builds the subject from the verified identity:

  • Subject user:<User> from ComponentRequest.User (or dispatch.Command.User at the gateway).
  • Tenant objects use ComponentRequest.TenantID, built with authz.TenantObjectOf (which refuses a / in the tenant or the id, so two pairs never name one object).
  • The session fact is ComponentRequest.SessionBoundary, added to every check that reaches an active_* relation with CheckRequest.WithSession(tenant, user, boundary). An empty boundary adds nothing and the check denies.
  • A component that needs a non-user subject (for example tenant:acme against a service-access relation) passes it explicitly in code. It is never read from the request payload.

Consequence, accepted by the owner: the proxy does not authenticate callers, so any pod the network policy admits can ask about any subject. Subject discipline is enforced by the module's API shape, code review and per-component admission, not by the infrastructure. CallerToken is not needed for authorization and must not be passed to authorization calls.

docs.title: 4. The module (go/authz)
docs.text:
Signatures only. Names are a proposal.

package authz

type Subject string // "user:u1", "tenant:acme"
type Object string  // "deployment_1:acme/d1"; ObjectOf(type, id) validates both parts

type Tuple struct{ Subject Subject; Relation string; Object Object }

type CheckRequest struct {
    Subject     Subject          // required: build with UserSubject(identity)
    Relation    string
    Object      Object
    Contextual  []Tuple          // validated against the model, never persisted
    Context     map[string]any   // OpenFGA condition context
    Consistency Consistency      // Default | HigherConsistency
}
type Decision struct{ Allowed bool; ModelID string }

type ListRequest struct {
    Subject    Subject
    Relation   string
    ObjectType string
    Contextual []Tuple
    Context    map[string]any
}
type ListResult struct{ Objects []Object; Truncated bool }

type Checker interface {
    Check(ctx context.Context, r CheckRequest) (Decision, error)
    BatchCheck(ctx context.Context, rs []CheckRequest) ([]Decision, error) // same length and order as the input
    ListObjects(ctx context.Context, r ListRequest) (ListResult, error)
}

func UserSubject(userID string) (Subject, error) // from ComponentRequest.User; rejects an empty or malformed id
func ObjectOf(typ, id string) (Object, error)
func TenantObjectOf(typ, tenant, id string) (Object, error) // type:<tenant>/<id>; refuses '/' in tenant or id
func SessionTuples(tenant, user, boundary string) ([]Tuple, error) // the contextual session_<boundary> fact; none for an empty boundary
func (r CheckRequest) WithSession(tenant, user, boundary string) (CheckRequest, error) // replaces any session_* tuple the request carried
func Require(ctx context.Context, c Checker, r CheckRequest) error // nil, *DeniedError or ErrUnavailable
// package authztemporal:
func ToTemporalError(err error) error // denied: non-retryable PERMISSION_DENIED; invalid: non-retryable INTERNAL; unavailable: retryable UNAVAILABLE

var ErrUnavailable, ErrInvalid error

type Config struct { BaseURL, StoreID, ModelID string; Timeout time.Duration; Cache CacheConfig; HTTPClient *http.Client }
func New(cfg Config) (*Client, error)
func ConfigFromEnv(getenv func(string) string) Config // AUTHZ_OPENFGA_URL, AUTHZ_STORE_ID, AUTHZ_MODEL_ID, AUTHZ_TIMEOUT

Behaviour that is part of the standard:

  • Fail closed. The zero Decision is a deny. Empty relation, subject or object is ErrInvalid. There is no bypass switch in production code; tests inject a different Checker.
  • Deny is not an error; outage is. Check returns Decision{Allowed:false}, nil for a deny, and ErrUnavailable for timeouts, 5xx, an unknown model or any malformed answer. No method returns allow together with an error.
  • Retries belong to Temporal. The module does not retry; default timeout 2s per call. Activity retry policy handles ErrUnavailable.
  • Cache: off by default. Opt-in in-process cache, TTL capped at 30s, keyed on everything that can change the answer: subject, relation, object, the contextual tuples, the condition Context and the consistency level (plus the model id, fixed per client). A check evaluated with a different Context (a current_time before and after a conditional grant expires) never shares an entry. A time-based condition can still expire inside the TTL, which is another reason the TTL is short. Duplicate identical calls in flight are collapsed; a cancelled caller never receives a cached or joined decision. Errors are never cached. Revocation lag equals the TTL, which is why it is off by default.
  • ListObjects is a lower bound, never an exhaustive answer. OpenFGA stops a list at its result limit (default 1000) or its deadline and returns what it has, with no completion indicator. The module sets Truncated when the result reaches the limit, but a list cut short by the deadline looks complete, so Truncated == false does not prove completeness. A list can only miss objects the subject may access, never add one, so it is safe for showing a user their items; it must not be used to decide that an object is absent or that a decision is final. Decisions use Check or BatchCheck on candidate rows. Raising the server's limit and deadline is a platform setting.
  • Expand is not part of v1. No service in the evidence needs it.
  • Model and store come from the environment's binding. The model id is the one the bootstrap Job publishes to the versioned binding ConfigMap (the same source sts-service reads: OPENFGA_STORE_ID, OPENFGA_AUTHORIZATION_MODEL_ID). The chart exposes them to components as env.

docs.title: 5.1 Gateway (coarse), declared in the capability manifest
docs.text:
Every capability has an authorize: block. A manifest without one fails to load.

capabilities:
  getTransitionStatus:
    description: Read the status of a worker transition.
    authorize:
      relation: can_view                 # must exist on the object's type in the component's model
      object: "deployment_1:{tenant}"    # templates: {tenant}, {user}, {payload.<field>}
    schema: { ... }

Rules:

  • {payload.<field>} may name only a top-level string field that the capability's schema marks required. This is checked when the manifest loads.
  • {tenant} against a platform-scope token (no tenant) is rejected.
  • No public option, no expressions, one check per capability. Anything richer is a component-level check in code.
  • The gateway runs the check in a new activity after ValidateSchema and before the child workflow starts, using the identity from the token. A deny returns PERMISSION_DENIED; an outage returns UNAVAILABLE.
  • DescribeCapabilities stays authentication-only. It reveals capability names and schemas, not tenant data.

go/capability stays free of a dependency on go/authz: dispatch defines a small Authorizer interface, as it does for Authenticator, and the gateway wires authz.Client into it.

docs.title: 5.2 Component activity (fine)
docs.text:
Per-object decisions, ownership, negative checks and list filtering stay in component code. The check runs in the same activity that touches the data, immediately after the tenant assertion:

func (a *Activities) GetTransitionStatus(ctx context.Context, req dispatch.ComponentRequest) (contract.TransitionStatus, error) {
    if err := assertTenant(req); err != nil { return ..., err }
    subject, _ := authz.UserSubject(identityOf(req))
    object, _ := authz.TenantObjectOf(example.TransitionType, req.TenantID, in.TransitionID)
    check, _ := authz.CheckRequest{Subject: subject, Relation: example.RelCanViewTransition, Object: object}.
        WithSession(req.TenantID, req.User, req.SessionBoundary) // the token's live tier; empty means no tier
    if err := authz.Require(ctx, a.Authz, check); err != nil { return ..., authz.ToTemporalError(err) }
    ...
}

docs.title: 6.1 Layout
docs.text:
components/<component>-1/authz/       # <component>-1: every platform entity ends in -1
  <component>-1.fga         # OpenFGA module file; first line `module <component>-1`
  tests.store.fga.yaml      # fga model test fixtures: tuples + assertions
  relations.gen.go          # generated typed constants (types, relations)

docs.title: 6.2 Rules for modules in a shared store
docs.text:
• Module names end in -1, like every platform entity (owner decision, October 2026): module <component>-1, in a file of the same name. The 12 existing modules were renamed to follow it (context-cluster-1, tenant-roles-1, ...). The names inside the module carry the generation too (next bullet).
  • Names inside the module end in _1 (snake_case, like the existing types): every type the module owns (deployment_1) and every relation it adds to a shared type (can_view_deployment_1 on tenant). Types and added relations are global across the store, so this is what lets a -2 generation run beside -1 without colliding. Relations on a module's own types need no suffix, since the type already carries it. Shared types (tenant, platform, audience, user) are owned by the platform modules and are never suffixed. Object ids in tuples follow the type: deployment_1:acme/d1. The 12 existing modules keep their type names: unlike the module name, a type name is stored in every tuple and used by auth-service code, so renaming it is a data migration, not a rename.
  • Type names and any relation added to a shared type are global across the store. A module must not redeclare another module's names. CI composes the candidate module with the current fga.mod and runs fga model validate.
  • Service objects carry the tenant in the id (deployment_1:acme/d1) and relate to tenant, following context_scope.
  • A module never defines tenant membership or platform roles. It extends tenant-roles and platform-roles.
  • Models change additively. Pinned worker versions finish on the build they started on and keep asking the old relations. Publish the additive model first, ship the component after, remove a relation only after the last build that uses it is sunset. A removed relation is rejected by OpenFGA and the module returns ErrUnavailable (deny), never allow.

docs.title: 6.3 How a model reaches the store (proposed)
docs.text:
1. The component repo validates <module>.fga and tests.store.fga.yaml in CI (fga model validate, fga model test).
  2. On release, the platform-actions workflow authz-model-pr.yml (section 12) opens a PR against the repository that owns the models, adding the module file and its fga.mod entry. The platform team approves it. This is the existing review path for changes to auth-store-2.
  3. Argo CD syncs, the bootstrap Job writes a new model, and the binding ConfigMap moves to the new model id.

The bootstrap Job now copies *.fga (PR 1365), so a module is one new file, one fga.mod line and one entry in the ConfigMap generator's file list. Kustomize has no glob for generator files, so that list stays until the models move to the shared models repository. Which repository owns the models (argocd-eks-stack today, authz-config_gitops_repo-1 as intended) is open question 1.

docs.title: 6.4 One reference for code, manifest and tests
docs.text:
The model file is the reference for every relation a component checks:

  • authzgen reads the model with the openfga/language Go transformer (TransformModuleFilesToModel, the call authz-manager-1 already makes in internal/model/files.go). It is a separate tool, so go/authz keeps no OpenFGA dependency and writes relations.gen.go with type and relation constants. Code uses deployer.RelCanViewTransition, never a string literal.
  • capabilitytest.Verify takes the model path and fails if any manifest authorize.relation or the object type of authorize.object is not in the model.
  • A test fails if generated constants are stale.

docs.title: 7. Network
docs.text:
• Add a component listener to openfga-1-readonly-proxy (for example port 8082): check, list-objects, list-users and batch-check for the one store. /read stays on 8081 only. The current proxy has no batch-check route.
  • In k8s-security, admit each component and gateway pod label (budybot.io/netpol: <prefix>-<component>) to that listener, and add egress from those pods to the proxy.
  • The gateway needs the same rule. Its existing egress to sts-service is not used for authorization.
  • Helm: the platform-app-cluster WorkerDeployment helper (component pods) and platform-capability (gateway chart) gain env: AUTHZ_OPENFGA_URL, AUTHZ_STORE_ID, AUTHZ_MODEL_ID, sourced from the environment's model binding ConfigMap. This is not verified: the library chart repository was not available to review.

docs.title: 8. Temporal rules
docs.text:
• Checks run in activities, never in workflow code. A check inside the activity that reads the data is preferred. The module also ships authz.Activities (AuthzCheck, AuthzBatchCheck) for the rare workflow-level branch.
  • Checks are read-only and safe to retry.
  • Activity input carries subject, relation, object and the contextual tuples (the session fact included), never payloads or tokens. The result recorded in history is {allowed, modelId}.
  • Audit: structured log from the module with subject, relation, object, result and model id (no tokens). The proxy does not log decisions today; central decision audit is open question 4.
  • Right after a grant, use HigherConsistency if read-your-writes matters (GET /v1/requests/{id} on authz-manager reports converged).

docs.title: 9. Testing
docs.text:
• Interface-level tests with a real implementation. Module go/authzembedded (separate, so the core stays dependency-light) provides New(t, modelDSL, tuples...) and NewFromModules(t, schema, files, tuples...): a real OpenFGA v1.22.0 server with an in-memory datastore, the same client code path as production, plus Grant and Revoke. It is built and merged (common-modules PR 27, released with the next version PR) and passes the conformance suite below. The Postgres and OpenFGA containers that authz-manager-1 uses remain an alternative.
  • authztest.Static (package go/authz/authztest, in the core module) is an exact-tuple checker for flat relations. It rejects unknown relations, has no computed-relation semantics, and says so in its docs.
  • Conformance suite authztest.RunConformance(t, newChecker): deny versus unavailable, timeout and cancel, malformed object, contextual tuples, batch order, list truncation, cache behaviour, tenant isolation (a tuple in tenant A never grants in B), Require mapping. ToTemporalError is tested in authztemporal. The suite is built and passes against both Static and the real server.
  • Per-component: fga model test on tests.store.fga.yaml, plus Go tests with authzembedded.NewFromModules loading the component's own model.

docs.title: 10. Packaging
docs.text:
• go/authz (core client on the standard library; authztemporal adds the Temporal SDK; authztest is in the same module) and go/authzembedded (test-only, OpenFGA server dependency), each its own Go module, tagged go/authz/vX.Y.Z and go/authzembedded/vX.Y.Z, released with changesets like go/capability. authzembedded requires go/authz v0.1.0, the first version, and keeps a local replace for development.
  • go/capability changes: authorize in the manifest, load-time validation, the model check in capabilitytest.Verify, and the Authorizer step in dispatch.
  • A worked example: the first worker component added to the nainai-cluster-1_repo-1 reference (one capability, one relation on a tenant-scoped _1 type, one model module, one Checker in Activities). Section 12 lists what has to be built first.

docs.title: 11. Unverified or open
docs.text:
Verified by building it: OpenFGA v1.22.0 can be embedded in tests and serves /batch-check, /check and /list-objects; the model language transformer used by authz-manager-1 also compiles the renamed modules. Not verified: the server version openfga-1 actually runs (so whether its proxy-side /batch-check works), the publishing workflow on GitHub, and the exact platform-app-cluster and platform-capability helper changes.

Open questions:

  1. Which repository owns the shared models: argocd-eks-stack (today) or authz-config_gitops_repo-1 (intended)? Who reviews at the platform team?
  2. Are two admitted listeners enough, or do component pods in different clusters need per-cluster ingress rules?
  3. Should the 12 existing modules' type names also move to _1? That is a tuple migration plus auth-service code changes, so the proposal leaves them.
  4. Central decision audit: log at the module only, or add access logging to the proxy?
  5. Should authzgen be a go/authz subcommand or a separate tool?

docs.title: 12. What has to be built
docs.text:
# Where Work Depends on 1 budy-common-modules: go/authz Built, merged and released (common-modules PR 27, go/authz v0.1.0; v0.2.0 adds SessionTuples, CheckRequest.WithSession and TenantObjectOf, PR 31): client for the proxy, Checker, Require, UserSubject, ObjectOf, bounded cache, env config, authztemporal. First consumer: studio-services-cluster-1. none 2 budy-common-modules: go/authz/authztest, go/authzembedded Built and merged (common-modules PR 27; not yet tagged): Static, RunConformance, and the embedded real OpenFGA. 1 3 budy-common-modules: go/authz/authzgen Typed constants from a model; the check that manifest relations exist in the model. 1 4 budy-common-modules: go/capability authorize: on each capability, load-time validation (required, templates, payload fields), capabilitytest.Verify model check, dispatch.Authorizer and the gateway Authorize activity. Breaking: every existing manifest must add authorize: (changeset: minor while 0.x). 1, 3 5 platform-actions Built and merged (platform-actions PR 58; usable as @v1 after the next release, and authz-model-pr.yml has not run on GitHub yet): validate-authz-model, stage-authz-model and authz-model-pr.yml. Still to do: the catalog field and app-cluster-ci call. Original scope: authz-model-pr@v1: validate the module (fga model validate, fga model test), compose it with the current fga.mod, check the additive-only rule against the published model, then open the PR to the models repository. Plus a validation.kind or catalog field so validate-cluster-catalog knows a component ships a model (for example authz: {module: authz/<module>.fga, tests: authz/tests.store.fga.yaml}) and runs the checks in app-cluster-ci. 3 6 EKS stack (openfga-1) Component listener and batch-check on the proxy; replace the three hand-kept module lists with a glob. Moves with the models repository when that work lands. models repository plan 7 k8s-security Ingress rules on the component listener for each component and gateway label; egress rules from them. Revisit OpenFGA ingress when it is locked down. 6 8 ob1-mn-github-helm-charts-repo-1 platform-app-cluster and platform-capability: AUTHZ_* env from the model binding ConfigMap. 6 4a budy-common-modules: go/capability Built, merged and released (common-modules PR 31, go/capability v0.3.0): the session boundary. stsauth.Identity.SessionBoundary reads the token's sessionBoundary claim (viewer, editor or admin; absent is empty, anything else is rejected), dispatch carries it in ComponentRequest.SessionBoundary and in the gateway workflow id when present. A component sends it to go/authz with WithSession, which adds the contextual user:<u> session_<boundary> tenant:<t> tuple that the platform's active_* tiers need; every check that reaches an active_* relation must carry it, and an empty boundary means no tier (deny). 1 9 Wiki Update the scaffold-nexus-cluster-repo skill (authorize: required, authz/ folder in the layout tree, the nexus checklist) and application-cicd-standard.md (model release step); promote this page from draft. after the trial 10 Trial First worker component in nainai-cluster-1_repo-1, which has only gateway-1 today. 1 to 8

Trial plan (item 10):

  1. Add one tenant-scoped worker component with one read capability, a small model module extending tenant, and a Checker in its activities.
  2. In dev only: publish the model by hand-driven PR first, then through authz-model-pr to prove the action.
  3. Prove in tests, then in dev: an allowed user, a denied user, a user of another tenant, the proxy stopped (must deny with UNAVAILABLE, never allow), and a model PR that removes a relation (CI must fail).
  4. Fold what breaks into this page before promoting it.

Order: 1 and 2 first (nothing else needs infrastructure), 3 and 4 next, 6 to 8 in parallel with them, 5 once 3 exists, the trial last.

docs.title: 13. Conditional grants: pass current_time
docs.text:
A relation can be granted with an OpenFGA condition. The one in use is non_expired_grant(current_time, grant_time, grant_duration) (authz-config_gitops_repo-1, models/conditions.fga), which ends a grant by itself when it expires. Example, models/dt-consulting-services.fga:

define svcrole_dtcs_coder_1: [user, user with non_expired_grant]

A standing membership has no condition; a workload session (section 14) holds the role with one. The rule:

  • Every check that can reach such a relation must send current_time in the check context. That includes everything derived from it: here active_svcrole_dtcs_coder_1, service_role_holder, assumable_editor and whatever extends from them. When a check reaches a conditional tuple without the parameter, OpenFGA answers with an error (missing context parameters [current_time]), not a deny.
  • Format: the UTC time as RFC 3339, for example 2026-11-13T08:30:15Z. It is the form sts-service sends.
  • A check that cannot reach a conditional relation does not need it, but sending it is harmless. The reviewer and reader relations of the same model stay [user] only.
Caller How it passes the time Code Go components on go/authz (sandbox-manager-1) CheckRequest.Context carries {"current_time": <UTC, truncated to the second, RFC 3339>} on every check of the access gate. The second keeps repeated checks within it shareable in the opt-in cache (section 4), which keys on the context. karkhana-cluster-1, components/sandbox-manager-1/internal/access/access.go (currentTime) sts-service Its authorizer sets current_time from its own clock on every check, and replaces a caller-supplied value on the Check/List endpoint. auth-service-1, sts-service/internal/authorizer/authorizer.go (currentTime), authorize.go (conditionContext) gitjib token-broker-1 Its own minimal OpenFGA client (no go/authz dependency) puts current_time into the context of every check call. gitjib-cluster-1, components/token-broker-1/internal/openfga/client.go (Check)

Consequences for callers:

  • A deny is still a deny and an error is still an error (section 4). A missing parameter shows up as an invalid-request error; token-broker-1 turns it into a refusal with the OpenFGA message in its audit line, and sandbox-manager-1 counts a rejected request as a deny for that relation and logs it. Neither reads it as allow.
  • A positive result that is cached can outlive the grant by up to the cache TTL (token-broker-1: authz.cacheTtl, default 30s, at most 1m; go/authz: at most 30s). Keep the TTL below any grant lifetime.
  • A new component that checks a role relation should send the time from the first version, even if no conditional grant exists yet, because the model can add one without a change in the component.

docs.title: 14. Workload sessions and the glassboxId claim
docs.text: These are capabilities of authz-manager-1 and sts-service (auth-service repository). They are generic; the sandbox service is the first user. Other pages own the details: this section says what a component author needs to know.

docs.title: 14.1 Workload sessions
docs.text:
A workload session is a short-lived identity for one workload that a platform service runs on a tenant's behalf (the sandbox operator, for pods in a tenant namespace). It acts only in that tenant, only for as long as the work, and never with more than the requester holds. Design: docs/provisioning-service-design.md, section 8.2, in ob1_mn_gh_auth-service-1_repo-1; code: providers/authz-manager-1/internal/ops/workload_session.go and internal/api/workload_sessions.go.

Topic Behaviour API POST /v1/workload-sessions (kind, tenant, namespace, serviceAccount, requester, roles, glassboxId, expiresAt, reference); GET /v1/workload-sessions/{id} (state pending, active, released or expired); DELETE releases (twice is not an error). Identity Kind plus reference name the session. The same pair is one session while it is live (identical request: no-op; later expiresAt: extension, never past maxLifetime after creation; different parameters: conflict). After release or expiry the pair starts another session. Kinds are configuration config.workloadSessionKinds (env WORKLOAD_SESSION_KINDS, empty by default). One reviewed entry per kind: callers (the workload ServiceAccounts that may create, read and release), roles (the only roles a session may carry), maxLifetime, namespaces (names, or $tenant). Checks All fail closed: the caller is in the kind's callers; every role is in the kind's roles; the requester is active and holds each role on the tenant for at least until expiresAt; the expiry is within maxLifetime; the namespace is allowed; the ServiceAccount is bound to no other user. Expiry The role tuple carries non_expired_grant with the expiry, so OpenFGA ends it by itself; the 5-minute maintenance sweep also ends sessions that are over, or whose requester lost a role, and withdraws their tuples. Release The caller releases explicitly when the work stops. A released session frees the ServiceAccount, so a later session can use it. Billing entity Recorded as a glassbox tuple on the session user (below). Opt-in A RoleType lists the workload_session user class in allowedUserClasses and must be tenant-scope and gitops-tier.

Because the role is granted with a condition, every check a receiver makes for such a user needs current_time (section 13).

docs.title: 14.2 The glassboxId STS claim
docs.text:
Every tenant session carries glassboxId: the entity that pays for what the session does, either the tenant id or a digital teammate of that tenant. STS decides it (sts-service/internal/authorizer/glassbox.go, ResolveGlassboxID); a caller cannot set it. Contract: docs/v2-token-claims-contract.md, "Billing entity".

  • Fixed for a workload session. authz-manager-1 records the entity as a tuple that names the session user as its object: tenant:<t> glassbox user:<session user> or user:<teammate> glassbox user:<session user> (authz-config_gitops_repo-1, models/workload-sessions.fga, define glassbox: [tenant, user] on user). STS stamps that value, refuses a different budy_glassbox_id, re-checks at every mint that the entity still belongs to the tenant, and refuses a user with more than one record.
  • A model without user#glassbox (OpenFGA relation_not_found) means "no fixed entity" and the default applies; any other OpenFGA error fails closed (temporarily_unavailable).
  • Otherwise the default is the subject when it is a digital teammate of the tenant, else the tenant; a service may name one with budy_glassbox_id on the workload exchange and the user-delegation grant.

What a component does with it: record it, never derive it. How usage is recorded against it is in the Usage Metering Standard. A consumer that maps it to something else (token-broker-1 maps it to a DigitalTeammate by spec.name) says so in its own documentation.

Status: on de-v2 main no workload session kind is configured for authz-manager-1 (charts/apps/auth-cluster-1 values hold no workloadSessionKinds). The sandbox-1 kind (callers: the sandbox operator ServiceAccount; roles: svcrole-dtcs-coder-1; maxLifetime 8h5m; namespaces $tenant) is proposed for dev in de-v2 PR 2414, open on 13 November 2026. Stage and prod get the kind after the auth chart that accepts the workload_session class (0.1.100) and the workload-session UserType (platform-crs authz-types/profile/dev, dev only for now) reach them; authz-manager-1 refuses to start with a kind whose user type or roles the catalog does not accept.

docs.title: Kargo Implementation Plan
docs.text: Status Foundation merged; awaiting prod-2 reconciliation and UI-access validation — do not enable promotion yet Scope One prod-2-hosted Kargo control plane; visibility of one Temporal cluster and Context Cluster across dev, stage, and prod Goal Establish trustworthy release visibility first, then add narrowly scoped, human-approved GitOps promotion

docs.title: Decision: topology and ownership
docs.text:
Kargo is a promotion control plane, not a per-application controller. Install one Kargo control plane in the prod-2 EKS cluster in a dedicated system namespace. Its API/UI, CRDs, Projects, Warehouses, Stages, Freight, PromotionTasks, and promotion history are all Kubernetes resources in that central control plane. The sole user interface is https://kargo.prod-2.orangebox.ai, exposed through a direct ALB ingress using the established ArgoCD pattern; controller shards do not expose their own UI.

That does not mean only prod participates. To observe ArgoCD health and safely run promotions for all three independent ArgoCD installations, deploy one narrowly scoped Kargo controller shard in each of dev-1, stage-1, and prod-2. Each controller talks to the central control plane but is permitted to interact with at most its local ArgoCD control plane. The central control plane therefore has visibility without holding a multi-cluster administrator credential.

Concern Recommended location Kargo Helm release, central namespace, control-plane security, prod bootstrap argocd-critical-stack, prod-2 only Kargo control-plane AppProject argocd-critical-stack; owns the Helm release, CRDs, RBAC, admission webhooks, and only the Kargo system namespaces Kargo configuration AppProject argocd-critical-stack; source-restricted to kargo-config, allowed all Kargo CRDs across Project namespaces but no non-Kargo Kubernetes resources Dev/stage/prod controller shards and their local network/RBAC corresponding environment configuration, installed only after the control plane is healthy Kargo Projects, Warehouses, Stages, PromotionTasks, and verified Git credentials a dedicated kargo-config GitOps repository reconciled only by prod-2 ArgoCD Temporal and Context desired-state changes their existing GitOps repositories; Kargo changes only a pinned artifact/version reference

The dedicated configuration repository is ob1_mn_github_kargo-config_gitops_repo_1. It has one protected main branch, reconciled by prod-2 ArgoCD. Do not create a fake release/stage or release/prod lifecycle for Kargo configuration itself: it is one global prod-hosted control plane, and a protected reviewed main gives the intended extra PR gate without pretending Kargo has separate environment installations. Individual Kargo Stages still model dev, stage, and prod.

Keep two AppProjects rather than one. The control-plane chart necessarily creates CRDs, cluster RBAC, admission webhooks, and system resources; allowing the day-to-day Kargo configuration repository to do the same would make a release-train change a control-plane administration path. The configuration AppProject may allow all kargo.akuity.io CRDs across Project namespaces so new release trains do not require a project-policy change, but it must not permit non-Kargo Kubernetes resources such as RBAC, Ingress, NetworkPolicy, or arbitrary Kubernetes resources. Visibility-only is enforced by the reviewed Kargo configuration: no Git credentials or Git-mutating PromotionTasks are present until the rollout gates are approved.

Kargo promotions are not deployments. A Stage promotion updates the exact allowed desired-state reference in the application GitOps repository; that environment's ArgoCD then deploys it. This preserves Git history, normal reconciliation, and rollback.

docs.title: Current implementation state — July 2026
docs.text:
The following foundation changes are merged and awaiting observation in prod-2:

  • Kargo control-plane, shared-resources, and system-resources namespaces;
  • scoped Vault/VSO access, including the shared VSO global-auth namespace allow-list and the ALB OIDC destination Secret;
  • a namespace-local, resource-name-scoped Role and RoleBinding allowing only the AWS Load Balancer Controller ServiceAccount to get that OIDC Secret. The Secret stays in the Kargo namespace; it must not be copied to kube-system.
  • separate Kargo control-plane and Kargo-configuration AppProjects;
  • prod-2 ArgoCD Applications for the pinned 1.10.8 Kargo control-plane chart and kargo-config repository, ordered so configuration follows CRD installation;
  • the temporal-cluster-2 and context-cluster-1 Kargo Project baseline resources; and
  • Google SSO through bundled Dex, using the existing VSO-managed Google web-client Secret, with ALB OIDC retained as the outer access gate. Dex performs the confidential Google token exchange; Kargo consumes Dex's PKCE-compatible OIDC session. For AWS Load Balancer Controller, set api.ingress.pathType: Prefix; the chart default ImplementationSpecific can route / while returning 404 for UI assets and API paths.

These changes are not yet live-validated. No Warehouse, Stage, Git credential, or Git-mutating PromotionTask has been added.

docs.title: Immediate next step — reconcile and access checkpoint
docs.text:
Before adding any release-train resources, perform and record this prod-2 checkpoint:

  1. Confirm the kargo-control-plane-1 ArgoCD Application is Synced/Healthy and kargo-config-1 follows it successfully.
  2. Inspect the Kargo namespace for ready API, controller, management-controller, webhooks-server, and garbage-collector Pods. Confirm the expected Kargo CRDs and the Kargo Project namespaces exist.
  3. Confirm the Kargo OIDC VaultStaticSecret is Ready and its destination Secret exists; never print Secret data in terminal output or PR evidence. Confirm that kube-system/ob1-acd-eks-aws-alb-controller-irsa-1 can get only ob1-mn-eks-kargo-google-oidc-secret-1 in the Kargo namespace. An ALB OIDC Ingress fails to reconcile when this namespace-local RBAC is absent.
  4. Confirm the ALB target is healthy and open https://kargo.prod-2.orangebox.ai. Test Google login as ksamay@budy.bot or jae@budy.bot; separately confirm a system user has only the intended non-admin access.
  5. Record the ArgoCD application status, Pod readiness, VSO condition, ingress result, and login result in the implementation PR/runbook. Stop and diagnose any failed item before adding Warehouses or Stages.

docs.title: Target release trains
docs.text:
Use two deliberately different first visibility cases:

Release train Type Initial Freight signal Why temporal-cluster-2 Infrastructure Helm release immutable parent Helm chart version/digest Validates promotion of a platform chart with dev/stage/prod profiles and stricter operational gates Context Cluster Multi-component application cluster parent Helm chart version first; component image tags/digests recorded as supporting evidence Validates application release visibility without prematurely letting Kargo independently choose tags from a shared image repository

For Context Cluster, do not subscribe to all component image tags in the first phase. Its one shared image ECR repository contains prefixed tags for multiple components. Start with the parent chart as the release unit; add one anchored image subscription per component only after the discovery regex, tag strategy, and chart/image consistency checks are tested.

docs.title: Stage 0 — design and access decisions (foundation merged)
docs.text:
1. Record temporal-cluster-2 and Context Cluster's exact ArgoCD Application names and GitOps paths/branches in dev-1, stage-1, and prod-2.
  2. Expose only the central UI/API at kargo.prod-2.orangebox.ai through the existing direct ALB ingress pattern. The shared Google client needs both callbacks: ALB uses /oauth2/idpresponse; Kargo native PKCE uses /login. Provision the ALB client secret to the Kargo namespace through Vault/VSO. The built-in admin account is not acceptable for production operation.
  3. Create a dedicated Kargo GitHub App, separate from the REF PACKAGE App and GitOps App. Give it only Contents: read/write and Pull requests: read/write for the GitOps repositories it must update. Store its key through Vault/VSO; never place a personal token in Kargo configuration.
  4. Define retention, backup/restore, alerting, SLO, resource sizing, PodDisruptionBudget, NetworkPolicy/Cilium, STRICT mTLS, and incident ownership.

Exit: a reviewed design PR records all identities, application names, repository paths, artifact signals, and rollback owner.

docs.title: Stage 1 — install the secure central control plane
docs.text:
1. Create the prod-2 Kargo system namespace, dedicated AppProject, and argocd-critical-stack Helm application with an immutable Kargo chart version. Keep that exact chart's unmodified default.values.yaml beside Kargo's environment values and refresh it whenever the pinned version changes.
  2. Configure direct ALB TLS termination, bundled Dex with a Google connector, a disabled built-in admin account, and direct ALB ingress at kargo.prod-2.orangebox.ai. The Google web client must allow both ALB's /oauth2/idpresponse callback and Dex's /dex/callback; its VSO-provisioned clientSecret is mounted only into Dex. Initial system administrators are ksamay@budy.bot and jae@budy.bot; initial system users are prateik@budy.bot and lan@budy.bot. The external-webhook endpoint stays disabled until GitHub webhooks are explicitly approved.
  3. Add least-privilege security policies in k8s-security, including the dedicated budybot.io/netpol: kargo Pod label, VSO authentication, a namespace-scoped BudyNetpolIdentity constraint, and (where ALB OIDC reads a VSO Secret) a namespace-local Role/RoleBinding granting the AWS Load Balancer Controller only get on that exact Secret.
  4. Bootstrap the kargo-config repository through github-infra, then create its prod-2 ArgoCD Application. Its AppProject must allow only Kargo CRDs and secrets delivered through VSO in the Kargo project namespaces.

Exit: Kargo UI is reachable only through approved authentication, control-plane health is green, backup restore is rehearsed, and no promotion-capable Project exists yet.

docs.title: Stage 2 — connect environment-local controller shards
docs.text:
1. Deploy one controller shard in dev-1, stage-1, and prod-2 as part of the initial installation, with separate service accounts and a separate central-control-plane token for each shard.
  2. Limit each shard to one local ArgoCD instance and its approved applications; do not give it direct credentials to another EKS cluster.
  3. Verify central UI/CLI can see all controller shards and can report local ArgoCD health without any Git write credential.

Exit: loss of any one shard cannot grant cross-cluster access, and central Kargo remains the single record of Freight history.

docs.title: Stage 3 — visibility-only: Temporal Cluster
docs.text:
1. Create one Kargo Project namespace for the Temporal release train in kargo-config.
  2. Add a Warehouse that discovers only the approved immutable Temporal chart signal.
  3. Add dev, stage, and prod Stages: dev accepts Warehouse Freight; stage accepts only verified dev Freight; prod accepts only verified stage Freight.
  4. Seed each Stage with the chart revision already deployed in its corresponding Git branch so the first dashboard view is truthful.
  5. Configure health observation only. Do not add a PromotionTask that edits Git and do not add Git write credentials.

Exit: Kargo correctly shows the currently deployed Temporal Freight and health across all three environments for at least one ordinary release cycle.

docs.title: Stage 4 — visibility-only: Context Cluster
docs.text:
1. Create a separate Kargo Project namespace for Context Cluster; do not share Project RBAC or credentials with Temporal.
  2. Subscribe to the parent Helm chart release only; correlate its chart values with the published component image digests/tags.
  3. Create and seed dev/stage/prod Stages as above, then verify the visual Freight lineage matches Context Cluster's actual GitOps revisions.
  4. Document the future component-image subscriptions: one subscription per component, anchored to <component>-<version>-<short-sha>, with a bounded discovery limit and chart-version consistency test.

Exit: both pilot release trains are visible, but Kargo still has no ability to mutate Git.

docs.title: Stage 5 — manual, GitOps PR promotion
docs.text:
1. Add a PromotionTask that modifies only the approved chart-version/value path for the target application and creates a PR—never a broad branch merge or direct protected-branch push.
  2. Make dev promotion manually initiated and require ArgoCD health. Keep stage/prod promotion manually initiated: Kargo opens a narrow PR but never auto-merges it; one Platform/SRE CODEOWNER approves after the required evidence is attached.
  3. Require these first gates: Temporal needs ArgoCD Healthy/Synced, Temporal frontend/namespace reachability, and a non-destructive test workflow start/completion; Context needs ArgoCD Healthy/Synced, all entrypoint/worker readiness, one authorized Nexus contract call, and an agreed error-rate/availability check. Record the exact runnable checks before enabling each pilot.
  4. Preserve the numbered cross-repository PR handoff standard: Kargo-created PRs state prerequisites, next approval, reviewer action, and rollback point.
  5. Disable or scope existing broad main → release/stage / release/stage → release/prod automation for a pilot once Kargo owns that application's narrow version path, preventing races.

Exit: a successful and a rollback promotion are rehearsed for Temporal before Context Cluster is permitted to automate beyond visibility.

docs.title: Stage 6 — progressive verification and wider onboarding
docs.text:
1. Add Kargo verification steps: ArgoCD health first, then smoke tests, GitHub Actions evidence, SLO/metrics checks, and approved production change-control gates.
  2. Add Context Cluster component-image Freight only after each tag-selection regex and image-to-chart consistency check is proven.
  3. Onboard additional release trains one at a time using the same Project, Stage, credential, security, observability, and rollback checklist.

docs.title: PR sequence
docs.text:
Follow the numbered PR handoff standard. The initial installation sequence is:

  1. github-infra: create kargo-config and, if approved, the dedicated Kargo GitHub App integration declaration.
  2. budy-cloud-management: create the Kargo control-plane, shared-resources, and system-resources namespaces.
  3. vault-management-1: grant the Kargo namespace's VSO service account read-only access to its scoped Kargo Vault KV path.
  4. k8s-security: Kargo namespace VSO authentication and ALB-OIDC secret materialization. When using shared-vso-1, add ob1-tf-eks-kargo-ns-1 to shared-vso-1-global-vault-auth-1.spec.allowedNamespaces; without it, the namespace-local VaultAuth is rejected even when the Vault-side role and policy are correct. Also add the Kargo namespace to pfm-security-infra-acd-proj-1.spec.destinations in argocd-critical-stack; otherwise ArgoCD rejects the VaultStaticSecret before VSO can create the OIDC destination Secret. Network policy and mTLS enforcement must be merged before applying the Kargo ArgoCD Application.
  5. argocd-critical-stack: Kargo AppProject, pinned Kargo Helm Application, and prod-2 bootstrap wiring.
  6. kargo-config: control-plane Project configuration and visibility-only Temporal/Context resources.
  7. Existing Temporal/Context GitOps repositories: only after visibility is proven, add Kargo authorization annotations and narrowly scoped promotion paths.

Each PR links its prerequisites, the next PR, required checks, and the last safe hold point. Do not approve a Git-mutating PromotionTask until every visibility-only exit criterion is evidenced.

docs.title: Information required before visibility onboarding
docs.text:
The foundation is merged. These decisions are still required before adding Warehouses, Stages, or Git-mutating promotion:

  1. Confirm the exact ArgoCD Application names and GitOps paths for temporal-cluster-2 and Context Cluster in each environment.
  2. Confirm the Platform/SRE GitHub team that is the required CODEOWNER for Kargo-created stage/prod promotion PRs.
  3. Convert the approved Temporal and Context smoke-gate descriptions into runnable commands/workflows before Git mutation is enabled.
