docs.title: Janus Cluster — Nexus Contracts
docs.text:
How other clusters, the Janus console, intake-1 and Digital Teammates (DTs) call janus-cluster-1. This is the as-built contract of 2026-11-17. The authoritative sources are the capability manifests in charts/gateway-1/files/capabilities/*.yaml (request schemas) and the Go types in shared/contract (answers); this file records them for callers and marks what is not verified.

What is not covered: outbound enforcement. outbound-policy-1 is built as an Envoy external-authorization service, but the listener is off and its only Nexus capability is a phase 0 stub (see "Other components"). Outbound is owned separately and is not a contract here.

docs.title: Endpoint and operations
docs.text:
Nexus endpoint ob1-nexus-janus-cluster-1-endpoint-1 (never versioned; its server-assigned id is delivered to callers in a Secret, and the HTTP path uses that id, not the name) Service ConnectionServiceV1 Operations Execute and DescribeCapabilities STS audience urn:budy:nexus:ob1-nexus-janus-cluster-1-endpoint-1:ConnectionServiceV1 Temporal namespace ob1-temporal-janus-cluster-1-ns-1 Gateway worker gateway-1, task queue janus-cluster-1-gateway-1-tq, workflow GatewayExecuteWorkflow Components behind it connection-registry-1 (25 capabilities), publish-1 (3), outbound-policy-1 (1, stub), vault-manager-1 (1)

Execute takes the envelope below and returns {ok, data?, error?: {code, message}}. The caller's tenant, user, scope type and session boundary come only from the verified STS token; a payload never carries a tenant. DescribeCapabilities returns the capability list and, on request, each capability's JSON Schema; it needs a valid token and nothing else.

docs.title: Request envelope
docs.text:
{
  "component": "connection-registry-1",
  "capability": "requestConnection",
  "payload": { "typeCode": "google-calendar", "reason": "Book the sales calendar" },
  "idempotencyKey": "optional, see below",
  "auth": { "token": "<STS access token>" }
}

The gateway validates payload against the capability's JSON Schema (every schema is closed: additionalProperties: false), starts a GatewayExecuteWorkflow, and runs the component as a child workflow on its own task queue. Unknown capability: UNIMPLEMENTED.

docs.title: Result envelope and error codes
docs.text:
error.code Meaning Retry? UNAUTHORIZED The token is missing, expired or not accepted. Fetch a new token, then retry once. PERMISSION_DENIED The token is valid but the caller may not call this capability (wrong scope, session boundary too low, not an internal caller). Surfaced to Temporal as a non-retryable application failure. No. INVALID_ARGUMENT The request failed schema or business validation. The message starts with the field (reason: ..., name: ..., type_retired: ..., conflict: ...). No: fix the request. NOT_FOUND The connection, type or link does not exist for this caller (a tenant cannot see another tenant's connection). No. FAILED_PRECONDITION A stale expectedUpdatedAt (the row changed since it was read), or a concurrent write lost. Only the catalog editor capabilities. Reload, then retry with the new version. UNAVAILABLE A dependency is not ready or not configured (no database, CONNECT_BASE_URL unset, a name could not be chosen after 5 clashes). Yes, with backoff. INTERNAL Unexpected failure. Once, with backoff. UNIMPLEMENTED The capability is not offered by that component. No.

A failed gateway call can also surface as an HTTP 500 from Temporal's Nexus handler instead of a result envelope, for example Workflow execution is already running (see idempotency).

docs.title: Calling Execute: asynchronous, with a callback
docs.text:
Execute is a workflow-run operation. POST <temporal frontend>:7243/nexus/endpoints/<endpoint id>/services/ConnectionServiceV1/Execute?callback=<url> does not return the result:

  1. Temporal answers 201 with {"token": "<operation token>"} immediately (a 200 with the result is also valid and is used as is).
  2. When the operation finishes, Temporal POSTs the result to the callback URL with headers Nexus-Operation-Token (must equal the token from the 201) and Nexus-Operation-State (succeeded, failed or canceled). On succeeded the body is the result envelope above.
  3. The caller must register the callback before sending the request (the completion can arrive before the 201).

Requirements for a caller:

  • A callback listener, reachable from Temporal's history service, on its own port (the Janus callers use 3001) with a per-call signed URL so only a call this process started can be completed. One replica per callback Service, or a shared signing key.
  • The callback address must be in Temporal's component.callbacks.allowedAddresses (eks-stack, temporal-cluster-3 values). Janus callers already listed: console-1-callback, janus-intake-1-callback and janus-outbound-policy-1-callback, all in ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-janus-1-ns-1, port 3001.
  • Network policy: egress to the Temporal frontend on 7243 (and the STS for tokens), and ingress to the callback port from Temporal's history service. In an Istio namespace with an ALLOW AuthorizationPolicy on the caller, the policy must also admit Temporal's service account (ob1-acd-eks-temporal-cluster-3-sa-1) on the callback port, or Temporal gets a 403 and reports "handler error (UNAUTHORIZED)".
  • Send Operation-Timeout in whole seconds, and make the local wait no shorter than it. intake-1 waits 10 s per try (up to 3 tries) and the console 20 s for reads and longer for writes. The registry's default execution timeout is 30 s (defaults.executionTimeout in the manifests).
  • Callbacks are delivered at least once; a repeat or late callback for a finished call is acknowledged and dropped.

docs.title: Idempotency and workflow ids
docs.text:
The gateway derives the workflow id from the tenant, the user, the capability, the session boundary and either idempotencyKey or a hash of the payload. Consequences for callers:

  • Two identical calls in flight at once share a workflow id and the second fails with Workflow execution is already running (HTTP 500). This includes a retry after a timeout and a page that polls while it reads. Send a fresh idempotencyKey on every try of a call that is only a read (the console and intake-1 send a random one per try).
  • For a write that must land once, send the same key on every retry so the retry finds the same run (the key becomes the workflow id). The registry also keeps its own idempotency for writes (below).
  • The registry reads idempotencyKey from the call; for the catalog editor writes it is the audit's replay key, otherwise run:<workflow run id>. A key reused for a different request (caller, capability or payload) is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT idempotencyKey: ....

docs.title: Scope and session rules
docs.text:
Kind Token scope Session boundary Capabilities Type reads any valid token any describeConnectionTypes, listConnectionTypes, getConnectionType (tenant-shaped answers: no normaliser, updatedAt, links or activeProvider) Tenant Tenant (tenantId in the token) any listConnections, getConnection, listConnectionRevisions, listConnectionAudit, listPublications, createConnection, requestConnection, revokeConnection; describePublications System reads Platform any systemListConnectionTypes, systemListProviders, systemConnectionTypeUsage, systemCheckTypeProvider, systemListCatalogAudit, describeVaultState System writes (catalog editor) Platform editor or admin (checked by the registry itself) systemUpsertConnectionType, systemSetConnectionTypeState, systemDeleteConnectionType, systemSetTypeProvider, systemRemoveTypeProvider Internal Platform, caller's user id in the registry's INTERNAL_CALLERS (janus-intake-1, janus-outbound-policy-1) any completeConnection, inspectConnection, setConnectionMetadata, recordCredentialUse Publishing service the publishing service's identity any registerPublication, retirePublication

Session boundaries are viewer, editor and admin, ordered. Janus enforces editor on the catalog writes in the registry (not only in the console) and on the console's Connect action (console only, see "console-1").

docs.title: Capabilities: connection-registry-1
docs.text: Every call is Execute with component: "connection-registry-1". Ids: connection ids are conn_<ULID>. Timestamps are RFC 3339.

docs.title: Connection types (reads)
docs.text:
Capability Payload Result describeConnectionTypes, listConnectionTypes none {connectionTypes: ConnectionType[]} getConnectionType code (1-64) ConnectionType

ConnectionType (tenant shape): id, code, name, description, category, credentialKind (oauth2 | api_key | basic | bearer), host?, pathPrefix?, scopes?, defaultScopes[], placement {in: header\|query\|context, name?, format?}, state (active | retired). Platform-only fields: normaliser?, updatedAt, links[], activeProvider?. The provider behind a type is not shown to tenants. Retired types stay readable.

docs.title: Tenant reads
docs.text:
Capability Payload Result listConnections typeCode?, state? (pending | active | needs-reauth | revoked), limit? (1-200), cursor? {connections: Connection[], nextCursor?} getConnection connectionId Connection listConnectionRevisions connectionId {revisions: [{revision, vaultPath?, createdAt, createdBy}]}, newest first; versions and times, never values listConnectionAudit connectionId?, limit? (1-200) {entries: [{at, connectionId, actor, action, runId?, activity?, decision?}]}, newest first listPublications automation?, limit? (1-200) {publications: [{id, tenant, automation, activities{activityId: connectionId[]}, state, refusalReason?, publishedAt}]}

Connection: id, tenant, name, typeCode, providerCode, providerRef?, state, currentRevision, host?, pathPrefix? (generic types), createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt, lastUsedAt?, reason? (why it was requested; empty on older rows), metadata? (a string map for display, see setConnectionMetadata). No secret value is ever in an answer.

docs.title: Tenant writes
docs.text:
Capability Payload Result requestConnection typeCode (1-64), reason (required, 1-500, plain text, no control characters), idempotencyKey? (up to 128), host? (up to 253) and pathPrefix? (up to 200) for generic types, forceNew? (boolean, or the strings "true"/"false") {connection, link: {url, message, expiresAt}, reused, reusedFromRequestedAt?} createConnection typeCode, name (1-200, unused for the tenant and type in any state, else name: ...), host?, pathPrefix? {connection, collection: {mode: form\|redirect, intakeSession?, intakeUrl?, connectUrl?, expiresAt}} revokeConnection connectionId Connection (state revoked); queues destruction of the stored secret versions; idempotent

requestConnection is what callers use. It creates a pending connection and mints a link the user opens to finish it (a form for api_key, basic and bearer; the provider's redirect for oauth2). Rules:

  • There is no name: the registry names and numbers connections per tenant and type. Types with a fixed host: Google Calendar, Google Calendar 2. Generic types (no fixed host): <Type name> – <host><path> (the path only when it is not empty or /), for example API key – welcomehome.com, with a number only on a repeat of the same type, host and path. A number is never reused, even after a revoke. A request that still sends name is refused (name: not accepted).
  • Reuse. If the same user already has a connection of that type (and host and path prefix) still pending from the last 60 minutes, the answer is a fresh link for that same connection with reused: true and reusedFromRequestedAt, and link.message begins by saying so. Tell the user it is the same pending connection. Older links to it stay valid until they expire.
  • forceNew: true starts another connection and leaves the pending one as it is; use it only when the user explicitly asks for another.
  • The same idempotencyKey for the same type always finds the same connection again (a retry), even with forceNew, and mints a fresh link; it is not reported as a reuse.
  • The link lives 60 minutes, its session is single use, and it only lets the holder store a credential into this one pending connection. Pass link.message and link.url to the user unchanged, including the # fragment. A refused type is INVALID_ARGUMENT type_retired: ....
  • reason is kept on the connection and in the audit.
  • Fails UNAVAILABLE while the registry has no CONNECT_BASE_URL; UNAVAILABLE could not pick a free connection name; try again after 5 name clashes.

docs.title: Internal capabilities
docs.text:
Capability Caller Payload Result completeConnection intake-1, oauth-provider-1 connectionId, providerRef?, vaultPath? (up to 512) with vaultVersion? (>= 1), actor? Connection (now active). A connection that is not pending is refused (that makes a session single use); repeating the same completion is harmless. inspectConnection intake-1 connectionId {connection, type, provider: {code, kind, integrationKey?}} (metadata only; never a provider reference) setConnectionMetadata INTERNAL_CALLERS, platform scope connectionId, set? (1-20 keys), remove? (up to 20 keys); at least one, no key in both {connectionId, metadata} after the change recordCredentialUse outbound-policy-1 events[] (1-100): tenant, connectionId?, runId?, activity?, host?, method?, path? (no query string), decision (allow | deny), code?, at {recorded}; all or nothing; never a credential, header or token

setConnectionMetadata: keys match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$; a value is plain text of 1-500 characters without control characters; at most 20 keys per connection; repeating a call changes nothing; the change is audited with key names only. Metadata is shown to tenants and platform alike and is never a place for a secret. Nothing writes it yet (for example an account_label from a provider is the intended later use).

docs.title: System and catalog editor (platform scope)
docs.text:
Reads (any session boundary): systemListConnectionTypes ({connectionTypes} with links, normaliser, updatedAt, activeProvider), systemListProviders ({providers: [{id, code, kind, credentialKinds[], state, name, configRef, updatedAt?}]}; configRef is a Vault path, never a value), systemConnectionTypeUsage ({usage: [{typeCode, tenants, connections, active, providers[{providerId, connections, active}]}]}).

Writes (session boundary editor or admin; each is audited, with the row before and after, and replays by its idempotency key). Providers are not editable through Nexus: a provider is added in code through a registry migration.

Capability Payload Result systemUpsertConnectionType id (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$), name (1-120), description (required, 1-1000, plain text, newlines allowed), credentialKind, placement {in: header\|query, name, format} (format holds exactly the kind's placeholder: {token} for oauth2 and bearer, {key} for api_key, {base64(username:password)} for basic), category?, defaultScopes? (up to 50), normaliser?, host? + pathPrefix? (both or neither), expectedUpdatedAt? the type as stored, with its links. credentialKind cannot change once a connection of the type exists. A type with no description is refused on edit until one is given. systemSetConnectionTypeState id, state (active | retired), expectedUpdatedAt? the type with its links. A retired type is refused for new connections; existing ones keep working. systemDeleteConnectionType id, expectedUpdatedAt (required) {id, deleted}. Refused (id: ...) if any connection of the type exists in any state: retire it instead. Deletes its links. systemSetTypeProvider connectionTypeId, providerId, state (active | available | deprecated | retired), settings? {integrationKey} (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]*$, up to 128), expectedUpdatedAt? the link as stored. active demotes the type's other active link in the same transaction; only new connections use the new provider. integrationKey is required for nango-1 and refused for any other provider. systemRemoveTypeProvider connectionTypeId, providerId, expectedUpdatedAt? {connectionTypeId, providerId, removed}. A link any connection uses cannot be removed: retire it. systemCheckTypeProvider (read only, any boundary) connectionTypeId, providerId, integrationKey? (checks that key before the link is saved) {ok, checks: [{name, ok, detail}]}; for a Nango link: the integration exists, is for this type, and allows the type's default scopes. Details are fixed sentences, never Nango's text. systemListCatalogAudit (read only, any boundary) limit? (1-200, default 50), cursor? {entries: [{id, at, actor, action, subject, before?, after?, requestId?}], nextCursor?}, newest first

expectedUpdatedAt: when sent it must equal the stored updatedAt, else FAILED_PRECONDITION.

docs.title: Other components
docs.text:
Component Capability Caller Notes publish-1 describePublications Tenant scope Same answer as listPublications. publish-1 registerPublication The publishing service only publicationId, tenant, dt, automation (required), activities (activity id to connection ids, up to 500 activities, 50 connections each), hosts[] (up to 200), rules. Validates that every connection belongs to the tenant and is active, records the publication and writes its tuples to Janus's OpenFGA. Idempotent per publicationId. A request naming a missing or inactive connection is recorded as refused with the reason and writes nothing. publish-1 retirePublication The publishing service only publicationId. Marks it retired and deletes the tuples no other live publication of the automation needs; idempotent. vault-manager-1 describeVaultState Platform scope What it keeps in the Janus Vault (KV mounts, fixed policies), the queued destroy requests and the last reconcile; never a secret value. outbound-policy-1 describePolicy any Phase 0 stub: answers stub: true. Outbound decisions are not made through Nexus.

Not published and not callable by tenants or DTs: createConnection, completeConnection, registerPublication, retirePublication and every system* capability (the catalog lint fails the build if a DT tool names any of them).

docs.title: DT tools and skills (catalog path /janus, audience global)
docs.text:
Published by janus-catalog-1 as Tool and Skill resources. Every tool calls Execute on this endpoint as the signed-in user, so the gateway fixes tenant and user from the token; no tool has a tenant argument. Parameters are strict and every parameter is required (a tool template can only send strings).

Tool Capability Parameters list_connection_types listConnectionTypes none get_connection_type getConnectionType code list_connections listConnections none list_connections_by_type listConnections typeCode list_connections_by_state listConnections state get_connection getConnection connectionId list_connection_revisions listConnectionRevisions connectionId list_connection_audit listConnectionAudit connectionId list_publications listPublications none list_publications_for_automation listPublications automation revoke_connection revokeConnection connectionId (only on an explicit user request for that exact connection) request_connection requestConnection typeCode, reason (one concrete sentence on why; required), forceNew ("true" or "false"; "false" unless the user explicitly asked for another connection)

request_connection sends idempotencyKey from the runtime placeholder {{runtime.workflowToolCallIdempotencyKey}}, so a retried tool call lands on the same connection. Its answer is requestConnection's: the DT shows link.message and link.url to the user unchanged and, when reused is true, says it is the same pending connection from earlier.

Skills: janus-using-connections (plan around the user's connections, request the missing ones, hand over the link, read back), janus-diagnosing-connections and janus-publishing-with-connections.

docs.title: intake-1 public HTTP (the connect page)
docs.text:
Routes under /v1/connections on the public API host, routed to intake-1 by api-gateway-1 without an app bearer token: the credential is the signed intake session in the body (capability auth), except the webhook. All are POST with Content-Type: application/json; each answers Cache-Control: no-store and a closed Content-Security-Policy. Errors are {"error": {"code", "message"}}; a link that is not valid, expired (410) or already completed (409) says so without revealing why a forged one failed.

Route Request Success session/inspect {session} 200 {connection: {id, name, state}, type: {code, name, credentialKind, host?, pathPrefix?}, provider: {code, kind}, mode: form\|redirect, fields: [{name, label, input: secret\|text, required}], expiresAt} credentials {session, fields} (the exact field set of the kind: key; username + password; token; each up to 4 KiB, no control characters) 201 {state: "active"} session/connect {session} 200 {connectUrl, expiresAt} (the provider's hosted connect page, created now so it is fresh) session/status {session} 200 {state, completed, typeName, completedAt?} webhooks/nango Nango's event verified by the X-Nango-Hmac-Sha256 header: hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with the environment's webhook signing key (a key of its own, not the API key); a good event completes the connection

Errors seen by the page: session_invalid (401), session_expired (410), already_completed (409), connection_not_found (404), invalid_request and unsupported_kind (400), not_a_redirect_connection (400), provider_not_configured (503), provider_unavailable (502), registry_unavailable (503), vault_unavailable (502), origin_not_allowed (403), unsupported_media_type (415) and rate_limited (429, with Retry-After).

docs.title: console-1 HTTP API (platform console)
docs.text:
The console's own browser API, behind the console-kit session cookie. It calls this endpoint as the signed-in user with that user's token. A tenant session gets 403 from /api/system/*, a platform session gets 403 from every tenant route; neither reaches the gateway. A gateway failure reaches the browser as a status class only (401, 403, 404, 503), never the gateway's text.

Route Scope Boundary Capability GET /api/connection-types, /:typeCode tenant any listConnectionTypes, getConnectionType GET /api/connections, /:connectionId tenant any listConnections, getConnection GET /api/audit, GET /api/publications tenant any listConnectionAudit, listPublications POST /api/connections/request (Idempotency-Key required; body {typeCode, reason, host?, pathPrefix?, forceNew?}) tenant editor requestConnection GET /api/system/types, /providers, /usage system any systemListConnectionTypes, systemListProviders, systemConnectionTypeUsage GET /api/system/audit system viewer systemListCatalogAudit PUT /api/system/types/:id, /:id/state; DELETE /api/system/types/:id system editor systemUpsertConnectionType, systemSetConnectionTypeState, systemDeleteConnectionType PUT and DELETE /api/system/types/:id/providers/:providerId; POST .../check system editor systemSetTypeProvider, systemRemoveTypeProvider, systemCheckTypeProvider

Every console write requires an Idempotency-Key that it forwards as the gateway's idempotencyKey; the catalog editor's writes are also optimistic (expectedUpdatedAt, 409 on a stale edit).

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text: Where Value Capability execution timeout 30 s (defaults.executionTimeout in each manifest) Operation-Timeout header whole seconds, never shorter than the caller's local wait Link / intake session lifetime 60 minutes (requestConnection) Reuse window for a pending connection the same 60 minutes

docs.title: Caller guidance
docs.text:
// Go: a read that may be retried. A new idempotency key per try, so a retry never collides with a run still going.
body := Execute{Component: "connection-registry-1", Capability: "inspectConnection",
    Payload: json.RawMessage(`{"connectionId":"conn_..."}`),
    IdempotencyKey: randomKey(), Auth: Auth{Token: token}}
cbURL, wait, release := callbacks.Register()        // before the request
defer release()
resp := post(endpoint + "?callback=" + url.QueryEscape(cbURL), body, "Operation-Timeout: 10s")
if resp.StatusCode == 201 { result = wait(ctx, resp.Body) }  // the completion arrives at cbURL
// result is {ok, data | error{code, message}}
  • A write that must land once (a catalog edit, requestConnection): send one key per intended action and reuse it on retries; do not retry INVALID_ARGUMENT or PERMISSION_DENIED.
  • FAILED_PRECONDITION: reload the row and retry with its new updatedAt.
  • Never log link.url, link.message, an intake session, a token or a credential: the link's fragment is a one-time bearer for entering a secret.

docs.title: Versioning policy
docs.text:
• The endpoint (ob1-nexus-janus-cluster-1-endpoint-1) is never versioned; the service is ConnectionServiceV1. A breaking change is a new service version, not an edited one.
  • Capability schemas are closed: an added optional field is non-breaking, a removed or renamed field is refused by the gateway for old callers. Example: requestConnection dropped name and made reason required on 2026-11-17; the console, the DT tool and the skills changed in the same release.
  • shared/contract (Go) carries the types; the manifests carry the schemas; a component's own test (capabilitytest.Verify) fails if its manifest and worker drift.
  • Component and chart versions follow changesets (connection-registry-1, contract, gateway-1, intake-1, console-1, the Janus chart).

docs.title: Not verified
docs.text:
• The gateway's exact workflow-id derivation and the maximum length of the envelope's idempotencyKey (only requestConnection's key is bounded, at 128) were read from the registry's documentation and callers, not from the gateway's source.
  • Which of the error codes Temporal treats as non-retryable beyond PERMISSION_DENIED (observed in a failed workflow) was not checked.
  • describePublications is listed as a tenant read from its manifest text and the publish-1 source comment; its scope check in code was not read line by line. The type reads (describeConnectionTypes, listConnectionTypes, getConnectionType) were read: they need a valid token and no particular scope.

docs.title: Janus Cluster — Product Requirements
docs.text: In review. This describes what Janus does today in dev. Outbound enforcement (checking and limiting the calls Digital Teammate workers make) is designed but not built; the owner is taking it over, and it is listed under Deferred Scope, not specified here.

docs.title: Why This Exists
docs.text: Digital Teammates (DTs) and the workflows that run for them need to act in customers' systems: read a calendar, call a business API. That takes credentials, and a credential must never sit in a prompt, a log, a workflow or a screen where the wrong person or a model could read it. Without a service that owns connections, each team collects secrets its own way, nobody can say who connected what or why, and a DT cannot tell what a tenant has already connected. Janus is that service: it collects credentials safely, keeps them out of reach, and tells DTs and people which connections exist.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: People and DTs ask Janus which kinds of connection are available, request a new connection with a reason, and finish it through a one-time link opened in a separate tab. Janus keeps the connection's details (which type, who made it, why, its state) and the credential itself in a separate, locked-down store that no screen or tool ever shows. Platform staff manage the catalogue of connection types in the console and see how they are used; tenants see their own connections.

docs.title: Who Uses It
docs.text: User What they do Digital Teammates See which connection types exist and which connections the tenant has, request a missing one for the user, and tell the user to open the link. A DT never sees a credential. Tenant users Connect a service for their organisation from the console (or by following a link a DT gave them), and see their connections. Platform staff Manage the catalogue of connection types and see usage; read-only unless they hold an editor session. Workflows Will use connections when they run (see Deferred Scope).

docs.title: Connection types
docs.text:
Type How it is connected Named after Google Calendar Sign in at the provider (hosted by Nango, with the platform's own verified Google app) the type ("Google Calendar", "Google Calendar 2") API key, Basic auth, Bearer token (any service) A form: the user enters the credential and says which website it is for the type and the website ("API key – welcomehome.com")

Platform staff can add more types, give each a description, retire one that should take no new connections, and delete one nothing uses.

docs.title: What a user experiences
docs.text:
• Choosing a type. A list of connection types, each with a plain description of what it gives access to. A DT sees the same list.
  • Requesting a connection. The user (or the DT for the user) names the type and gives one sentence on why the connection is needed. For a type with no fixed website, the website is part of the request. The answer is a link and a message to pass on, valid for about an hour, usable once.
  • Finishing it. The user opens the link in another tab. For an API key, basic or bearer connection they fill in a form; for Google Calendar they sign in with Google. A confirmation page says when it is done and they can close the tab; the connection then shows as active in the console.
  • Several connections of one type. Connections are named automatically and numbered, so a tenant can hold two Google calendars or API keys for different websites and tell them apart. The reason is kept with each one.
  • Asking twice. If the same user asks again within an hour for the same type (and website) while the first request is still waiting, they get the same pending connection with a message saying so, not a second one. They can explicitly ask for another connection of the same type, which leaves the pending one as it is.
  • Details that arrive later. A connection can carry extra labels for display, for example the account it belongs to, shown in the console. They are never secrets.
  • The console. Tenants see their connection types and connections, with when each was created, rotated and last used. Platform staff see every type, which provider serves it, how many connections use it, and an audit of every catalogue change. The console has a sign out button and sends people back to the platform when their session ends.
  • Connect from the console. A user with an editor session can request a connection directly from the console, exactly as a DT would. A user with a view-only session sees the button disabled with the reason.

docs.title: What platform staff control
docs.text:
• Types. Create, edit, retire and delete connection types; give each a description; link a type to a provider and choose which provider serves new connections. Changing the provider affects new connections only and moves nothing; the console says so and asks the person to confirm.
  • Providers. Visible but fixed: a new provider is a software change, not a console action.
  • Audit. Every change to the catalogue is recorded with who made it and what changed.

docs.title: What Janus Is NOT Responsible For
docs.text:
• Showing or exporting a credential: nothing in Janus ever displays or returns a secret; credentials are write-only.
  • Signing people in and tenant roles: the platform's authentication service owns it.
  • The external systems themselves: their availability and their API limits.
  • Building and running the Digital Teammates' workers: the nainai cluster and the build services own it.
  • Limiting how often the platform's public API is called: the public API gateway owns inbound limits.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text: Metric Target A user can request a connection and finish it in another tab without help Yes, for every supported type No credential ever appears on a screen, in a log, in a DT's context or in a link Zero occurrences (checked by tests of every route and log line) A request made twice within an hour never leaves two waiting connections 0 duplicates Every connection says who created it and why 100% of connections created after launch Every catalogue change is attributable 100% recorded with the person and the change Connect page responds to the user's click Proposed: within a few seconds at the 95th percentile; to be confirmed with product

docs.title: Phase 1 UAT Acceptance Criteria
docs.text: # Scenario Pass condition 1 A user lists connection types in the console Every active type shows its name and a description; retired types are marked and cannot be connected 2 A user requests an API key connection for a website with a reason They receive a link; opening it shows a form; after saving, the connection is active and named "API key – " 3 The same user requests the same type and website again within an hour, while the first is pending They get the same pending connection with a message saying it already exists; no second connection appears 4 The same user asks for another connection of that type explicitly A second pending connection is created and numbered ("… 2"); the first stays pending 5 A user requests two API keys for different websites Both connections exist with different names showing each website 6 A user requests Google Calendar and completes the sign-in The connection becomes active and shows as "Google Calendar" in the console 7 A request is made without a reason It is refused with a message asking for one 8 A link is opened a second time, or after an hour The page says the link is no longer valid and does not accept a credential 9 A DT is asked for a connection the tenant does not have It requests one, passes the link and message to the user unchanged, and does not see any credential 10 A view-only user opens the connection types page The Connect button is disabled with an explanation 11 A platform editor creates a type without a description The save is refused with a message 12 A platform editor changes which provider serves a type A warning explains that only new connections are affected and requires a confirmation 13 A platform editor deletes a type that has connections It is refused and retiring is offered; deleting a type with none succeeds 14 Two editors change the same type at the same time The second is told it changed and must reload; nothing is silently overwritten 15 A tenant user views their connections They see only their organisation's connections, with created, rotated and last-used times and no secret 16 A user's session ends while the console is open They get a two-minute notice, then are sent back to the platform; sign out does the same at once 17 Platform staff open the audit page Every catalogue change shows who, when and what 18 The connection service is briefly unavailable The user sees a clear "try again" message and no half-created connection is shown as active

docs.title: Phase 2 / Deferred Scope
docs.text:
• Outbound enforcement: checking each call a DT worker makes against what it is allowed to do, injecting credentials and limiting rates. Designed; the owner is taking it over.
  • Renaming a connection and who fills in details such as the account label: connections can carry them; nothing writes them yet.
  • Refreshing and re-authorising connections (rotation, "needs sign-in again") and deleting the provider-side connection when one is revoked: not built.
  • Janus's own Google sign-in as an alternative to the hosted provider: later.
  • Moving connections between providers: deliberately not built; new connections use the active provider.
  • Sharing a connection beyond the creator and the DT it serves (and its manager): out of scope.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• Outbound enforcement scope and timing (owner).
  • Whether a view-only user may ever request a connection (today an editor session is required).
  • Targets for connect-page responsiveness and how many connections per tenant to plan for.

docs.title: Janus Cluster — TRD
docs.text:
How janus-cluster-1 is built, as built on 2026-11-17: the code layout, configuration, schema, capability shapes, wiring and operations. Product intent is in the PRD, architecture and decisions in the HLD, the caller contract in nexus-contracts, the service summary in info. The repository's own docs/content/ keeps the deeper per-component notes this document points at.

Scope. Everything that is built and running in dev: the gateway, the connection registry, the connect page backend (intake-1), the console, the catalog editor, the Nango provider, the Janus Vault and OpenFGA wiring. Outbound enforcement is not described here: outbound-policy-1 and the Envoy gateway are listed as built-not-enforcing (their configuration surface only) because that work is owner-led and open.

Status of verification. Facts below were read from the code, charts and GitOps repositories at the dates in each section. Items that could only be inferred are collected under Not verified.

docs.title: Implementation Stack
docs.text: Concern Choice Rationale Language (cluster) Go 1.26 (one module per component, go.work for local dev) Nexus-first clusters are Go; consistent with the platform's shared kit Console TypeScript on Node 26 (>=26.13 <27), Fastify 5, React 19, Vite 8, @budybot/console-kit 0.6.0 The platform console standard; the kit supplies session, STS verification, adapters and the write routes Orchestration Temporal (Worker Deployment Versioning, Pinned); one workflow per component, <Component>WorkflowV1, one activity (Execute) A component is only reached through the gateway as a child workflow; behaviour changes by shipping a new build Gateway Shared kit budy-common-modules go/capability/gateway/{stsauth,dispatch}, version capability v0.3.0 No business logic in gateway-1; it loads capability manifests and validates payloads Database PostgreSQL (ob1-janus-db-1), pgx, goose migrations embedded in the registry image, run by a chart Job One schema owner (the registry); publish-1 and vault-manager-1 read and write their own tables Secrets Janus Vault (janus-vault-cluster-1, KV v2 mount janus-connections); platform Vault for service secrets via VSO Tenant credentials are isolated from the platform Vault Authorization OpenFGA (janus-openfga-1), model components/publish-1/authz/janus.fga A dedicated instance; the bootstrap Job owns the store and model Third-party credentials Nango (hosted, api.nango.dev) for OAuth Nango holds the OAuth tokens; Janus holds ids only Packaging One parameterized Dockerfile for every Go component (COMPONENT, BINARY_TARGET); the console has its own Non-root, read-only root filesystem, emptyDir on /tmp Release changesets, the shared app-cluster-ci / app-cluster-release workflows (@v1), Kargo promotion See CI/CD and release

docs.title: Types and constants (shared/contract)
docs.text:
The contract module is the only module tagged for external use. Cross-reference: field documentation is in the HLD; these are the names an implementer needs.

States: pending, active, needs-reauth, revoked. docs.title: ID and key construction
docs.text:
// Connection id: "conn_" + 26 Crockford base32 characters from 16 random bytes (ULID-length, not ordered).
//   components/connection-registry-1/internal/activities/activities.go (`newID`)

// Vault path of a connection's secret fields (under the KV mount janus-connections):
func ConnectionVaultPath(tenant, connectionID string) string { return "tenants/" + tenant + "/connections/" + connectionID }

// Intake session ("link" payload): base64url(json(IntakeSession)) + "." + base64url(hmac-sha256(key, that json)).
//   IntakeSession{c: connection id, t: tenant, y: type code, k: credential kind, p: provider, a: actor, n: nonce, e: expiry}
//   TTL 60 minutes (activities.DefaultLinkTTL). Key: INTAKE_SESSION_KEY_FILE, shared by the registry (signs) and intake-1 (verifies).

// Nexus callback URL: <origin>/internal/nexus/callback/<id>.<sig>
//   id  = base64url(32 random bytes)  (43 characters), sig = base64url(hmac-sha256(per-process random key, id))

Connection naming (request_connection.go, connectionBaseName, nextName):

  • A type with a fixed host (ConnectionType.Host != "") is named by the type's name: Google Calendar.
  • A generic type (no fixed host) is named <type name> – <host><path> with an en dash and spaces; the path is included only when it is not empty and not /: API key – welcomehome.com, Bearer token – api.example.com/v2.
  • The first connection of that base name keeps it; later ones get the number after the highest in use for that tenant, type and base: ... 2, ... 3. Every state counts, so a revoked connection keeps its number and numbers are never reused.
  • The whole name is at most 200 runes: the base is cut to leave room for a space and five digits (nameNumberRoom = 6) and a long host/path is cut with ….
  • Uniqueness is enforced by the unique index connection_name_idx (tenant_id, connection_type_id, lower(name)). On a unique violation the name is picked again (maxNameTries = 5), then the capability fails UNAVAILABLE ("could not pick a free connection name; try again").

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: PostgreSQL database ob1-janus-db-1. The registry owns the schema; migrations are goose SQL files embedded in the registry image (internal/store/migrations), applied by the chart's migration Job (<release>-connection-registry-1-migrate, Helm hook pre-install,pre-upgrade which ArgoCD runs as a PreSync hook, weight -5, the registry binary with the argument migrate, database admin credentials from VSO). Enabled by migration.enabled: true in the GitOps base values, so every environment applies pending migrations when its chart upgrades.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text: # File What it does 00001 schema connection_type, connection_provider, type_provider (+ one-active index), connection, connection_revision (+ immutability trigger), publication, audit 00002 layers_and_seed credential_kind, provider_credential_kind; connection_type.credential_kind replaces auth_scheme; connection.{name,host,path_prefix,last_used_at}; connection_revision.vault_version; vault_destroy_request; publication_grant; the seed 00003 request_key connection.request_key + the unique request-key index (an idempotent requestConnection) 00004 publication_fga_tuples publication.fga_tuples (widened before an OpenFGA write, narrowed after, so a failed write is reconcilable) 00005 catalog_editor connection_type.state; catalog_audit (+ immutability trigger, unique replay index); connection_type_provider_idx 00006 type_description connection_type.description: seeds real sentences, sets description = name for editor-made rows, adds CHECK (btrim(description, E' \t\r\n') <> ''), drops the default 00007 connection_names_and_reason connection.request_reason; renumbers existing duplicate names (oldest keeps its name, later get the smallest free number from 2); unique connection_name_idx 00008 reset_connections_names_and_metadata Destructive on purpose (nothing was in use). In order: (1) queue every stored secret version in vault_destroy_request (grouped by connection and path, only vault_version > 0) so nothing is orphaned in the Janus Vault; (2) one audit row registry.connections_reset with counts; (3) delete publication_grant; (4) disable the connection_revision_immutable trigger, delete connection_revision, re-enable it (inside the migration transaction, the only way to delete them); (5) delete connection; (6) rename the three generic types to API key, Basic auth, Bearer token (only if still named as seeded); (7) create connection_metadata. Keeps audit and the publication rows. Does not delete Nango-side connections or the OpenFGA tuples publish-1 wrote. The Down restores the type names and drops the table; deleted rows are not restored. It runs once per database in every environment the chart reaches.

docs.title: Capabilities of connection-registry-1
docs.text:
Every capability is a Nexus Execute call {component, capability, payload, auth:{token}} answered {ok, data | error:{code, message}}. The gateway validates payload against the manifest schema (charts/gateway-1/files/capabilities/connection-registry-1.yaml, additionalProperties: false everywhere) before the registry sees it. The registry additionally decodes strictly and re-asserts identity. Error codes are the kit's dispatch.Code: INVALID_ARGUMENT, PERMISSION_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, FAILED_PRECONDITION (a stale expectedUpdatedAt or lost concurrent write; the console maps it to 409), UNAVAILABLE, UNIMPLEMENTED, INTERNAL. A refusal message starts with the field or reason (reason:, name:, type_retired:, id:, conflict:).

Capability Caller Request Answer describeConnectionTypes, listConnectionTypes tenant {} types (tenant view; no normaliser, links, activeProvider) getConnectionType tenant {code} one type listConnections tenant {typeCode?, state?, limit?≤200, cursor?} the tenant's connections, metadata only getConnection, listConnectionRevisions, listConnectionAudit tenant {connectionId} / {connectionId?, limit?} the connection (with reason, metadata); revisions (versions and times, never values); audit createConnection tenant {typeCode, name, host?, pathPrefix?} pending connection with mode: form (intakeUrl, intakeSession) or mode: redirect (connectUrl). The name must be unused for tenant+type in any state (name:). Normally replaced by requestConnection requestConnection tenant below {connection, link:{url, message, expiresAt}, reused, reusedFromRequestedAt?} revokeConnection tenant {connectionId} revokes, queues the secret versions in vault_destroy_request; idempotent listPublications tenant {automation?, limit?} publications and which connections each activity uses completeConnection internal {connectionId, providerRef?, vaultPath?, vaultVersion?, actor?} pending → active; a non-pending connection is refused (this is what makes a link single use) inspectConnection internal (intake-1) {connectionId} the connection, its type and provider (code, kind, non-secret integration key); never a provider reference or Vault path setConnectionMetadata internal {connectionId, set?{k:v}, remove?[k]} the connection's metadata after the change recordCredentialUse internal (outbound-policy-1) {events[1..100]} all-or-nothing credential.use audit rows (no credential, header or token in an event) systemListConnectionTypes, systemListProviders, systemConnectionTypeUsage platform {} full types with links, providers with credential kinds, per-type tenant/connection counts systemUpsertConnectionType platform, boundary editor/admin {id, name, description, credentialKind, placement{in,name,format}, defaultScopes?, normaliser?, host?, pathPrefix?, category?, expectedUpdatedAt?} the type as stored, with links systemSetConnectionTypeState platform, editor/admin {id, state: active\|retired, expectedUpdatedAt?} the type systemDeleteConnectionType platform, editor/admin {id, expectedUpdatedAt} (required) {id, deleted}; refused (id:) if any connection of the type exists in any state systemSetTypeProvider platform, editor/admin {connectionTypeId, providerId, state, settings{integrationKey?}, expectedUpdatedAt?} the link; active demotes the type's other active link in the same transaction systemRemoveTypeProvider platform, editor/admin {connectionTypeId, providerId, expectedUpdatedAt?} {.., removed}; refused while a connection uses the link systemCheckTypeProvider platform, any boundary {connectionTypeId, providerId, integrationKey?} {ok, checks[{name, ok, detail}]} (fixed sentences only) systemListCatalogAudit platform, any boundary {limit?, cursor?} newest first, before/after per row, nextCursor

There is no provider-editing capability: providers are added in code (a registry migration, as 00002 does). systemUpsertProvider was removed on 2026-11-17.

docs.title: requestConnection
docs.text:
// request (manifest: additionalProperties false; the registry also rejects any other field, e.g. `name`, with `name: not accepted`)
{ "typeCode": "generic-api-key",        // required, 1..64
  "reason": "Read the sales API",       // required, trimmed, 1..500, plain text (a newline is a control character)
  "idempotencyKey": "k-123",            // optional, <= 128; the DT tool sends the runtime placeholder
  "host": "api.example.com",            // generic types only (a host is required for them)
  "pathPrefix": "/v2",                  // optional
  "forceNew": false }                   // boolean, or the strings "true" / "false" (a tool template can only send strings)

// answer
{ "connection": { ...Connection, "reason": "...", "metadata": {} },
  "link": { "url": "https://<connectBaseUrl>/connections/connect#s=<session>", "message": "...", "expiresAt": "<RFC3339, +60 min>" },
  "reused": false, "reusedFromRequestedAt": null }

Processing:

  1. Tenant scope required (this capability needs a tenant-scoped caller). reason and forceNew validated (reason: is required; ..., reason: is at most 500 characters, reason: must be plain text without control characters). A retired type is refused type_retired: .... The registry needs CONNECT_BASE_URL (and INTAKE_BASE_URL for form kinds): unset fails UNAVAILABLE (connect_base_url_not_configured, intake_base_url_not_configured) and stores nothing.
  2. Idempotency key hit first: the same (tenant, type, key) finds its own connection again, even with forceNew, and mints a fresh link; reused is false. If that connection is no longer pending: INVALID_ARGUMENT conflict: this idempotencyKey already produced a connection that is <state>; use a new key to request another.
  3. Reuse unless forceNew: inside one transaction holding an advisory lock on (tenant, type, host, pathPrefix, creator) (pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(...))), a pending connection of the same tenant, same user (creator_id), type, host and path prefix created within the last 60 minutes (PendingWindow.Since) is returned: reused: true, reusedFromRequestedAt = created_at, a fresh signed link for that same connection (older links stay valid until their own expiry), and link.message starts "A connection request for () made N minutes ago is still pending, so this is the link for that same connection instead of a new one. To start another connection of the same type, request again with forceNew set to true; the pending one stays as it is." The reuse keeps the first request's reason; the new reason goes only into the audit row.
  4. Otherwise insert a new pending connection with the generated name (see naming) and request_reason; forceNew always takes this path and leaves the old pending connection untouched.
  5. Write the audit row connection.link_minted (type, reused, forceNew, expiry, reason) and log connection requested.
  6. A refusal for an unknown or retired type, a missing host for a generic type, or a bad field never creates a row.

    7. setConnectionMetadata rules: keys ^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$; values plain text 1..500 characters, trimmed, newline counts as a control character; at most 20 keys per connection (enforced under a row lock: 30 racing writes leave exactly 20 keys); set and remove are exclusive per key; an unchanged key is not rewritten and writes no audit row; one connection.metadata_changed audit row per change with key names only, never values; errors NOT_FOUND, or INVALID_ARGUMENT starting set: / remove:. Nothing writes metadata yet; the intended writer is a provider on completion (account_label).

docs.title: Authorization inside the registry
docs.text:
Rule Where Component name must be connection-registry-1; req.User required; tenant scope needs a tenant id; scopes other than tenant and platform refused assertCaller (activities.go) Tenant capabilities: tenant scope, tenant from the gateway-fixed identity (never a request field) tenantOf system* reads: platform scope systemOnly system* writes: platform scope and ComponentRequest.SessionBoundary of editor or admin; first thing each does, before the payload is read catalogWriter (catalog.go) Internal capabilities (completeConnection, inspectConnection, setConnectionMetadata, recordCredentialUse): platform scope and req.User in INTERNAL_CALLERS (the STS token's sub) internalOnly requestConnection checks tenant scope only. The editor boundary for connecting is enforced by console-1's adapter (requiresBoundary: "editor"), not by the registry console connect.ts

INTERNAL_CALLERS is the comma-separated env var built from the chart value registry.internalCallers (not under nango:). In GitOps it lists janus-intake-1 and janus-outbound-policy-1. If it is empty or unset every internal call answers PERMISSION_DENIED: this capability is internal.

docs.title: Idempotency and workflow ids
docs.text:
• Gateway workflow id. When a call carries no idempotencyKey the gateway derives the workflow id (gateway-<hash>) from tenant, user, capability, boundary and a hash of the payload. Two identical calls in flight at once therefore share an id and the second fails with Workflow execution is already running (HTTP 500 from the Nexus handler). With a key, the id derives from the key. Every caller that can issue identical calls concurrently must send a fresh key per try: the console sends read-<uuid> for reads (and the browser's Idempotency-Key for writes); intake-1 sends intake-call-<32 hex> on every try of a registry call.
  • Catalog editor writes are idempotent: the call's dedupe key is the caller's idempotency key (the console sends one per intended edit), else run: + the workflow run id, never the bare workflow id (the same edit made at different times shares a workflow id and must still execute). Each write looks its call up in catalog_audit first, inside the same transaction under a pg_advisory_xact_lock of (action, key), and replays the stored result byte for byte on a hit. A key reused for a different request (request_hash mismatch) is refused INVALID_ARGUMENT idempotencyKey: ....
  • Optimistic concurrency: expectedUpdatedAt must equal the stored updated_at or the write fails FAILED_PRECONDITION (console: 409 conflict). The console always sends it when editing, never when creating (creating an existing id is a console-side 409).
  • Temporal retries: the registry workflow runs one activity with StartToCloseTimeout 10s, MaximumAttempts 3, backoff 200 ms → 2 s; failures return as a typed Response, never a workflow failure.

docs.title: Session boundary
docs.text: The STS token carries sessionBoundary (viewer, editor, admin); ComponentRequest.SessionBoundary (capability module v0.3.0, the version the registry and gateway are pinned to) delivers it to the component. The console reads it from the session and lists a write adapter for a principal only when its scope and boundary are met (the bootstrap adapters array), so a viewer sees disabled controls with the reason, and the server refuses the call (403 boundary_required) before any gateway call. Platform sessions come from the portal's platform Google groups; the highest boundary is the group's.

docs.title: Nexus callback implementation
docs.text:
gateway-1's Execute is a workflow-run Nexus operation: Temporal answers the HTTP call 201 {"token": "<operation token>"} immediately and later POSTs the result to the callback URL the caller sent as ?callback=<url>. Headers on that POST: Nexus-Operation-Token, Nexus-Operation-State (succeeded | failed | canceled). A 200 is also accepted and carries the answer directly. The caller sends Operation-Timeout: <whole seconds>s, never shorter than its own wait.

Item Go (intake-1, outbound-policy-1) TypeScript (console-1) Implementation shared/contract/nexuscallback.Receiver (Register() returns the URL, a wait function and a cancel) src/server/callback.ts Callbacks (register(), wait(), accept(), server()) Path /internal/nexus/callback/<id>.<sig> same Per-call id 43 characters (base64url of 32 random bytes) same Signature HMAC-SHA256 of the id with a key that lives in this process only (random at start) same Port own listener, NEXUS_CALLBACK_ADDR default :3001 (intake-1), 3001 (outbound-policy-1) NEXUS_CALLBACK_PORT 3001 Service janus-intake-1-callback, janus-outbound-policy-1-callback (stable names), port 3001 console-1-callback, port 3001 Body cap 1 MiB 8 MiB Replicas one pod per caller (the key and the pending map are per process); a callback delivered to another replica or after a restart is refused one replica (Recreate; the chart refuses replicaCount > 1) Errors FailedError{State}, ErrNoToken, ErrTokenMismatch (an operation that ended failed or canceled, a 201 without a token, or another operation's token) CallbackError timeout / failed / token Timeouts intake-1: 10 s per try, up to 3 tries (200 ms, 400 ms backoff), reads and the completion only on transient failures console: 20 s read, 60 s write (timeoutMs)

A valid-signature callback for an unknown or late call is acknowledged 204 and dropped. A bad signature or unknown path is refused (403/404) and counted.

What must exist for a callback to arrive (all three Janus receivers, each checked on 2026-11-17):

  1. Temporal's component.callbacks.allowedAddresses lists the Service and port (argocd-eks-stack, v2/apps/platform/wrflw/temporal-cluster-3/values/base.values.yaml): console-1-callback.ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-janus-1-ns-1.svc.cluster.local:3001, janus-intake-1-callback...:3001, janus-outbound-policy-1-callback...:3001 (AllowInsecure: true).
  2. A Cilium ingress policy from Temporal's history pods on port 3001 (console-1.allow-temporal-callback.yaml, intake-1.allow-temporal-callback.yaml, outbound-policy-1.allow-temporal-callback.yaml).
  3. Egress from the caller to the Temporal frontend 7243 (and the STS 8080) (<component>.allow-required.yaml).
  4. If the workload has an Istio ALLOW AuthorizationPolicy (only intake-1 does), it must also admit Temporal's service account on 3001: intake-1.allow-temporal-callback.authorizationpolicy.yaml (principal cluster.local/ns/ob1-tf-eks-temporal-3-ns-1/sa/ob1-acd-eks-temporal-cluster-3-sa-1, port 3001, ports and principals only because L7 rules are not enforced by ztunnel). Without it Temporal's delivery is refused with 403 and the caller sees "Nexus Callback has failed ... handler error (UNAUTHORIZED)".
  5. The namespace is STRICT mTLS (strict-mtls.peerauthentication.yaml, no port exceptions).

docs.title: Intake (intake-1)
docs.text:
HTTP backend of the connect page. Routes (all POST, application/json, session in the body, edge auth mode capability, Cache-Control: no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer):

Route Request Success Notes /v1/connections/session/inspect {session} 200 connection, type, provider, mode (form | redirect), fields[], expiresAt refuses a connection that left pending (409 already_completed) /v1/connections/credentials {session, fields{}} 201 {state: "active"} validates the closed field set (4 KiB each, no control characters), reserves the session nonce, writes a new revision to the Janus Vault with KV check-and-set, then completeConnection /v1/connections/session/connect {session} 200 {connectUrl, expiresAt} creates the Nango connect session lazily (POST /connect/sessions, tags connection_id) /v1/connections/session/status {session} 200 {state, completed, typeName, completedAt?} also answers for a connection that already completed /v1/connections/webhooks/nango Nango's event 200 signature auth, below

Errors: 401 session_invalid (forged or mismatched), 410 expired, 403 origin_not_allowed, 415, 429 rate_limited (+ Retry-After), 502 vault_unavailable / provider_unavailable, 503 registry_unavailable / provider_not_configured. A refused completion triggers a second inspectConnection: revoked → 404 connection_not_found, otherwise 409 already_completed. Rate limits (per minute, burst): IP 60/30, read 30/10, connect 10/5, credentials 10/5.

Vault write: KV v2 at janus-connections/tenants/<tenant>/connections/<id>, one key per field (key, username, password, token), check-and-set with the version this replica last stored (0 when unknown); on a refused CAS it reads the metadata version and retries once. Single use has two layers: the registry is authoritative (completing a non-pending connection is refused, and inspect runs before any write so a replay cannot overwrite an active credential) and an in-memory nonce set closes the window between inspect and completion. The registry client is internal/registry (Nexus HTTP, the callback receiver, STS workload token, STS session:viewer platform scope with STS_SCOPE_ID=janus-platform-1).
