docs.text: Env var Chart value / source Meaning LISTEN_ADDR, HEALTH_ADDR :8080, :3000 listeners LOG_LEVEL logLevel (default info) debug, info, warn, error; a typo stops the start INTAKE_SESSION_KEY_FILE secrets.sessionKey (key session-key) HMAC key that verifies intake sessions (shared with the registry) VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_CA_FILE, VAULT_K8S_ROLE, VAULT_K8S_MOUNT (kubernetes), VAULT_KV_MOUNT (janus-connections), SA_TOKEN_FILE vault.* Janus Vault login (projected token with audience vault.tokenAudience) and mount NEXUS_URL, NEXUS_ENDPOINT_ID, NEXUS_SERVICE (ConnectionServiceV1), NEXUS_CALLBACK_ADDR (:3001), NEXUS_CALLBACK_URL nexus.* registry transport; setting NEXUS_URL without the rest (incl. an origin-only callback URL) fails at start STS_TOKEN_URL, STS_PROJECTED_TOKEN_PATH, STS_SCOPE_ID, STS_RESOURCE, STS_SCOPE (session:viewer), STS_SCOPE_TYPE (platform) sts.* workload token exchange NANGO_BASE_URL, NANGO_CONNECT_URL nango.baseUrl, nango.connectUrl Nango API; connect UI origin fallback NANGO_SECRET_KEY_FILE secrets.nango key apiKey Nango API key (scoped: environment:connect_sessions:write) NANGO_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY_FILE secrets.nango key signingKey Nango webhook signing key (a different secret). Neither file falls back to the other CONNECT_ALLOWED_ORIGIN, CLIENT_IP_HEADER, CLIENT_IP_HOPS connect.* the only CORS/request origin; which header carries the client address and how many hops from the right

docs.title: Nango client and webhook verification
docs.text:
• API calls (by component): intake-1 → POST /connect/sessions (needs environment:connect_sessions:write). connection-registry-1 → GET /integrations/{key}?include[]=credentials for the editor's Check (only the scopes are kept; needs environment:integrations:read_credentials) and POST /connect/sessions for createConnection (a path the DT and console flow does not use). outbound-policy-1 → GET /connection/{ref}?provider_config_key=<key> (the access token; needs environment:connections:read_credentials; the singular path is deprecated by Nango). Scope names come from Nango's documentation and are not verified against the dashboard (see Not verified); the repository's docs/content/nango-keys.md has the per-component key table and rollout order.
  • Webhook verification (internal/nango.Verify): the X-Nango-Hmac-Sha256 header is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed with the environment's webhook signing key (Nango: Environment Settings > Webhooks > Signing key), compared in constant time. The older X-Nango-Signature is not accepted. The body is read with a 1 MiB cap before parsing. A completion event is type: auth, operation: creation, success: true with the connection id taken from the end-user tag connection_id; other events are acknowledged 200 {"ignored": true}.
  • On a refused signature the log carries hmac_header_hex_len, legacy_header_hex_len, body_bytes, content_type, content_encoding, secret_len and secret_fp (the first six hex digits of the key's SHA-256), never the key, a signature or any body text. Compare secret_fp with printf %s "$KEY" | sha256sum | cut -c1-6.

docs.title: connection-registry-1 configuration
docs.text:
Env var Meaning TASK_QUEUE default janus-cluster-1-connection-registry-1-tq LOG_LEVEL debug / info (default) / warn / error; a typo stops the start PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGSSLMODE, PGUSER_FILE, PGPASSWORD_FILE, PGMAXCONNLIFETIME database (dynamic Vault credentials re-read per connection); unset PGHOST starts the worker answering UNAVAILABLE INTAKE_BASE_URL, CONNECT_BASE_URL public bases of intake-1 (form URLs) and the connect page (requestConnection's link); https without credentials, query or fragment INTAKE_SESSION_KEY_FILE signs intake sessions INTERNAL_CALLERS from registry.internalCallers NANGO_BASE_URL, NANGO_SECRET_KEY_FILE Nango client (secretKey of its own Secret; scoped key environment:integrations:read_credentials) METRICS_ENABLED worker metrics

Chart values: database.{host,credentialsSecret,migratorCredentialsSecret}, registry.{intakeBaseUrl,connectBaseUrl,internalCallers,intakeSessionKeySecret}, nango.{baseUrl,secretKeySecret}, migration.{enabled,serviceAccount}, vso.*, logLevel.

docs.title: gateway-1
docs.text: Env: TASK_QUEUE, CAPABILITIES_DIR (the mounted manifests), METRICS_ENABLED. Manifest default executionTimeout: 30s. A manifest change rolls the pod (checksum/capabilities annotation); there is no runtime discovery. Manifests: connection-registry-1 (capabilities above), publish-1 (describePublications, registerPublication, retirePublication), vault-manager-1 (describeVaultState), outbound-policy-1 (describePolicy; the last two are phase-0 stubs that say so).

docs.title: publish-1
docs.text: Env: TASK_QUEUE, database variables, OPENFGA_URL, OPENFGA_API_TOKEN_FILE, OPENFGA_STORE_NAME (resolved to the id at start, waiting a bounded time for the bootstrap Job; a missing or duplicated store stops the process), OPENFGA_STORE_ID/OPENFGA_MODEL_ID (unset by default), PUBLISH_CALLERS (identities allowed to call), METRICS_ENABLED. registerPublication / retirePublication write the publication row and its tuples idempotently, widening publication.fga_tuples before and narrowing after the OpenFGA write.

docs.title: vault-manager-1
docs.text: Env: TASK_QUEUE, database variables, VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_CA_FILE, VAULT_K8S_ROLE, VAULT_K8S_AUTH_MOUNT, VAULT_TOKEN_FILE, VAULT_TOKEN_AUDIENCE, RECONCILE_INTERVAL (default 1 minute), VAULT_COMPONENT_ROLES (false skips the component Kubernetes-auth roles), JANUS_NAMESPACE, JANUS_INTAKE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, JANUS_OAUTH_PROVIDER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, JANUS_OUTBOUND_POLICY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT. Each pass ensures the Janus Vault's mounts (janus-connections, janus-platform), policies and component roles, then works the vault_destroy_request queue (batch 50). Fixed policy janus-connection-writer gives the intake components create and update on janus-connections/data/tenants/+/connections/+ and read on its metadata, never read, list or delete of a value. Roles: ob1_janus_intake-1_role_1, ob1_janus_oauth-provider-1_role_1, ob1_janus_outbound-policy-1_role_1, ob1_janus_vault-manager-1_role_1, ob1_janus_raft-snapshot_role_1. Policy janus-outbound-policy-1 may only update auth/token/create/janus-conn-reader; that token role may attach only janus-conn-*-read policies, has no default policy and lives at most 15 minutes (the just-in-time read path used by outbound enforcement; not exercised yet).

docs.title: oauth-provider-1
docs.text: Env: LISTEN_ADDR, HEALTH_ADDR, PUBLIC_BASE_URL, INTAKE_SESSION_KEY_FILE, VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_CA_FILE, VAULT_K8S_ROLE, VAULT_K8S_MOUNT, VAULT_KV_MOUNT, SA_TOKEN_FILE, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE. Built, not wired to a registered internal OAuth provider: intake-1 answers 501 provider_not_supported for such a type.

docs.title: openfga-bootstrap-1
docs.text:
Env: OPENFGA_URL (required), OPENFGA_STORE_NAME (default janus-cluster-1), OPENFGA_API_TOKEN_FILE, OPENFGA_CREATE_STORE (the sync Job true, the hourly drift CronJob false), OPENFGA_BOOTSTRAP_MESH (wait for the Istio sidecar and ask it to quit). One run: read the key; wait for the sidecar and GET /healthz; list stores and take the one named exactly OPENFGA_STORE_NAME (two with the name fails); create only when allowed; compare the store's latest model with Git's as canonical JSON and write a new model only when it differs (written / unchanged); retries on transport, 5xx and 429 (4 attempts), never on 401/403; keys and bodies are never logged. The Job is an ArgoCD Sync hook (wave 0). The model source is components/publish-1/authz/janus.fga, with generated internal/model/janus.model.json and a drift test; run make openfga-model to regenerate.

Model (schema 1.1): user, tenant, janus_dt_1 (owning_tenant), janus_automation_1 (dt, running), janus_activity_1 (automation, runnable_in), janus_run_1, janus_connection_1 (owning_tenant, user_activity, creator, dt_user, dt_manager; can_use = user_activity or dt_user or dt_manager, can_revoke = creator or dt_manager). No tuple is static: every tuple is written by publish-1 at publish or supplied as a contextual tuple from the run token. OpenFGA preshared keys have no roles (any holder can do anything): one shared key today, with per-consumer VSO secrets so it can be split later. Details: docs/content/openfga-operations.md.

docs.title: outbound-policy-1 (built, listener off)
docs.text: Env: EXT_AUTHZ_ENABLED (must be true to serve; default off), EXT_AUTHZ_ADDR, RULES_DIR, CONNECTIONS_FILE, RUN_TOKEN_AUDIENCE, STS_ISSUER, STS_JWKS_URL, OPENFGA_URL, OPENFGA_STORE_NAME/OPENFGA_STORE_ID/OPENFGA_MODEL_ID, OPENFGA_TOKEN_FILE, VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_MOUNT, VAULT_TOKEN_FILE, VAULT_TOKEN_ROLE, NANGO_BASE_URL, NANGO_SECRET_KEY_FILE, AUDIT_NEXUS_URL (the audit sink; decisions go to the registry's recordCredentialUse through Nexus with its own callback on NEXUS_CALLBACK_ADDR, 3001), TASK_QUEUE, METRICS_ENABLED. Nothing in this repository enforces outbound calls yet; see the outbound enforcement thread for the open work.

docs.title: console-1
docs.text:
Fastify server serving a React app; one session cookie (key sessionSecret, from the Janus-owned KV path .../janus-cluster-1-console-1/session, read once at start). Environment (set by the chart): CONSOLE_PORT, CONSOLE_PUBLIC_URL, CONSOLE_PORTAL_URL, CONSOLE_ACCEPTED_SCOPES (system,tenant), CONSOLE_LOG_LEVEL (chart default warn; dev debug), CONSOLE_STS_ISSUER, CONSOLE_STS_JWKS_URL, CONSOLE_STS_AUDIENCE, CONSOLE_HANDOFF_REDEEM_URL, CONSOLE_HANDOFF_APP_ID, CONSOLE_HANDOFF_RESOURCE, CONSOLE_HANDOFF_TOKEN_PATH, CONSOLE_SESSION_SECRET_FILE, NEXUS_URL, NEXUS_SERVICE, NEXUS_ENDPOINT_ID (the server-assigned endpoint id from the TemporalNexusEndpoint connection Secret, key id), NEXUS_CALLBACK_PORT, NEXUS_CALLBACK_URL. No database and no other secret.

Routes (the console's own API; all behind the console-kit session; unknown query parameters 400; a tenant session gets 403 from /api/system/* and a platform session 403 from tenant routes without calling the gateway):

Route Scope Boundary GET /api/connection-types[/:code], GET /api/connections[/:id], GET /api/audit, GET /api/publications tenant any POST /api/connections/request {typeCode, reason, host?, pathPrefix?, forceNew?} + Idempotency-Key (required) tenant editor GET /api/system/types, /providers, /usage system any GET /api/system/audit?limit=&cursor= system viewer (explicit) PUT /api/system/types/:id, PUT .../state, DELETE /api/system/types/:id (body {expectedUpdatedAt}) system editor PUT / DELETE /api/system/types/:id/providers/:providerId, POST .../check ({} or {integrationKey}) system editor /healthz, /auth/callback, /auth/logout (204), /api/bootstrap, the static app console-kit

Server rules worth knowing: reads send read-<uuid> as the gateway idempotency key; a request body with unknown fields is refused; the connect route returns only the connection's id, name, typeCode, state, host, pathPrefix, reason, createdAt, metadata, the link {url, message, expiresAt}, reused and reusedFromRequestedAt (never a provider, provider reference or Vault path); the link is never logged, never cached (no-store) and held only in component state until the dialog closes; only an https link (or http on localhost) without credentials is offered; the registry's error text never reaches the browser (the console's own sentences, field messages on a 400). The web app expires the session by its expiresAt (timer capped and re-armed, re-checked on visibilitychange/focus), shows a two-minute notice, and offers Sign out (POST /auth/logout, then the portal URL).

docs.title: Vault paths and policies
docs.text:
Vault Mount / path Written by Read by Content Janus Vault (janus-vault-cluster-1) KV v2 janus-connections/tenants/<tenant>/connections/<id> intake-1 (and oauth-provider-1) via role ob1_janus_intake-1_role_1, policy janus-connection-writer outbound-policy-1 through a 15-minute child token (janus-conn-reader, per-connection read policies); not exercised yet tenant credential fields, one KV version per revision Janus Vault janus-platform vault-manager-1 provider keys (reserved) Platform Vault (vault-cluster-2), app-kv-secrets-1, base v1/de-v2/ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-janus-1-ns-1/ connection-registry-1/intake-session-key (key), connection-registry-1/nango (secretKey), janus-cluster-1-intake-1/nango (secretKey = API key, webhookSigningKey = signing key), janus-cluster-1-outbound-policy-1/nango (secretKey), janus-cluster-1-console-1/session (sessionSecret) the owner VSO into Kubernetes Secrets service secrets

intake-1-nango (VSO VaultStaticSecret in resources/base/intake-nango.vss.yaml) maps apiKey ← secretKey, signingKey ← get .Secrets "webhookSigningKey" (an empty value, not a literal, when the field is missing), and keeps secret ← secretKey only while the previous chart runs; remove secret and secrets.nangoWebhook once the new chart is everywhere. The janus Vault's own bootstrap (initialization, recovery keys, break-glass) is in docs/content/janus-vault-operations.md and deploy/janus-vault-bootstrap/. The root token is documented as revoked; custody of recovery keys is the owner's.

docs.title: Chart and GitOps wiring
docs.text:
Umbrella chart charts/janus-cluster-1 (published as janus-cluster-1-repo-1 to OCI on ECR): top-level values keys global, temporal, config, gateway-1, connection-registry-1, publish-1, outbound-policy-1, vault-manager-1, intake-1, oauth-provider-1, openfga-bootstrap-1, console-1, janus-catalog-1. Temporal resources (namespace, connection, Nexus endpoint and its connection Secret) are created by the umbrella through Crossplane. config.logLevel configures the Temporal worker library only; intake-1 and the registry read their own logLevel.

GitOps (ob1_mn_gh_de-v2_gitops_repo_1, charts/apps/janus-cluster-1/): app.yaml (ArgoCD Application janus-cluster-1-app, project apps-janus-cluster-1-acd-proj-1; Kargo owns targetRevision), values/default.values.yaml (written by Kargo), values/base.values.yaml, values/profiles/{dev,stage,prod}.values.yaml, values/env/{dev-1,stage-1,prod-2}.values.yaml, resources/base/ (VSO secrets intake-nango, intake-session-key, outbound-policy-nango, vault-auth). Layers apply in that order, later wins. In the dev profile intake-1 and the registry run at debug.

ArgoCD projects (ob1_mn_gh_argocd-critical-stack_repo_1, v2/env/_base/bootstrap/projects/applications/): apps-janus-cluster-1-acd-proj-1 (the Janus namespace, the Temporal namespace and Nexus endpoint kinds), apps-janus-supporting-1-acd-proj-1 (Janus Vault and OpenFGA namespaces). apps-de-v2-services-acd-proj-1 must list ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-janus-1-ns-1 as a destination: the backend-services-cluster-1 chart's api-gateway-1 renders a ReferenceGrant in that namespace so the gateway can route /v1/connections/* to intake-1; without the destination ArgoCD refuses the resource and the whole app does not sync (fixed in argocd-critical-stack PR 197).

Edge routing (backend-services-cluster-1, chart api-gateway-1): contracts/intake declares inspectConnectionSession, /credentials, /session/connect, /session/status (auth capability: the signed session in the body) and POST /v1/connections/webhooks/nango (signature auth); all five route to backend intake-1 (Service intake-1, namespace ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-janus-1-ns-1, port 80 → pod 8080) and are listed as unauthenticated in the gateway's AuthorizationPolicy (so no bearer token is needed). The edge replies for a denied path are rewritten to 401 application/problem+json ("Sign in to continue"): a 403 from Istio RBAC and a missing token look identical at the edge.

Network and mesh policy (ob1_mn_github_k8s-security_gitops_repo_1, v1/objects/netpol/manifests/de-v2-janus-1-ns-1/): namespace default deny; ingress/ console-1.allow-istio-ingress-gateway, console-1.allow-temporal-callback, intake-1.allow-api-gateway-1 (+ .authorizationpolicy: principal cluster.local/ns/ob1-tf-eks-api-gateway-ns-1/sa/api-gateway-1-istio, port 8080), intake-1.allow-temporal-callback (+ .authorizationpolicy), outbound-policy-1.allow-temporal-callback, outbound-policy-1.allow-outbound-gateway-1, outbound-gateway-1.allow-workers, namespace-wide.allow-prometheus-envoy-stats; egress/ per-component *.allow-required (registry, console, intake, oauth-provider, publish, vault-manager, outbound-policy, outbound-gateway, gateway), janus-components.allow-janus-vault, janus-components.allow-janus-openfga-1, temporal-workers.allow-external-payload-store-and-vault, namespace-wide.allow-required, namespace-wide.deny-missing-label; strict-mtls.peerauthentication.yaml. Pods are matched by the label budybot.io/netpol: janus-<component>; Gatekeeper budy-netpol-identity lists the allowed identities. The generated inventory/ must be regenerated in the same commit (python3 tools/policy-inventory/policy_inventory.py --write).

Environments: dev-1 (main), stage-1 (release/stage), prod-2 (release/prod), one AWS account each. The owner reports stage and prod running older charts than dev (0.1.18 and 0.1.17 on 2026-11-17); they apply pending migrations, including the destructive 00008, when their chart reaches it.

docs.title: CI/CD and release
docs.text:
Shared pipeline pinned at @v1, driven by .github/components.json.

  • Pull request (ci.yml → app-cluster-ci.yml): detect, changeset (a .changeset/*.md file or label no-changeset, package names must equal catalog packages, a dry run of changeset version), validate-chart, check-go per Go module (vet, test, build; the registry's store tests run against Postgres), check-node for console-1, catalog-chart (scripts/lint-catalog-chart.sh: the Tool and Skill resources; setConnectionMetadata and the other internal capabilities are forbidden in any tool), and the aggregate ci-required. A superseded run shows cancelled and the aggregate reports failure: it is not a real failure.
  • Release (release.yml, on push to main): a merged changeset opens the Release PR changeset-release/janus-cluster-1, which may change only package.json, CHANGELOG.md and .changeset/**. Merging it builds and pushes the changed images (<component>-<version>-<sha7>), tags shared/contract/v<version>, creates <component>/v<version> tags, and opens the chart-release PR (automation/chart-release/janus-cluster-1, the only thing that bumps the umbrella chart; CI owns chart versions, never hand-bump). A chart-only change needs the label no-changeset; after it merges CI opens the chart PR from the shared resolve-chart-release + chart-release-pr. Merging the chart PR publishes the chart and opens a CHANGELOG-only PR in de-v2 (kargo_managed: true).
  • Promotion: Kargo discovers the chart and promotes dev → dev-bake (1 h) → stage → stage-bake (4 h) → prod → prod-verify (15 min); bake stages check restarts, 5xx and ArgoCD health.
  • Local: make test, make lint-catalog-chart, make openfga-model, npm run changeset. Commit the root package-lock.json (changesets needs it to see the workspaces); console-kit comes from GitHub Packages with min-release-age=7, so a new kit version needs its lockfiles regenerated through a disposable workflow when offline.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Structured slog lines (text format through the process default logger for Go; JSON for the console). IDs, outcomes and fixed-word causes only: never a session, link, credential, Vault path contents, webhook body or signature, client address, request path or header, or the text of a dependency's error (tests assert this for intake, the registry and the console).

Component LOG_LEVEL Info Debug Warn Error intake-1 env LOG_LEVEL, default info startup (hosts and ids only, once), connection_completed session_inspected, session_status, provider_session_created, credential_written, webhook_received, webhook_ignored, callback_delivered request_refused (with reason), rate_limited, vault_cas_conflict, completion_refused, webhook_refused, webhook_unknown_connection, webhook_completion_refused, callback_refused provider_session_failed, provider_not_configured, vault_write_failed, registry_unavailable (with cause), webhook_refused for secret_not_configured connection-registry-1 env LOG_LEVEL, default info connection requested, connection completed, connection revoked, vault destruction queued catalog write, connection metadata changed connection request refused, connection create refused, connection completion refused, connection revoke refused (code + fixed refusal text), nango connect session failed, nango integration check failed an internal failure (code=INTERNAL) console-1 CONSOLE_LOG_LEVEL, chart default warn connection requested (outcome created/reused/forced) registry call timings and statuses connection request refused, registry call failed

Every intake line has event and request. The request id is the edge's X-Request-Id when it matches ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{8,64}$, otherwise a fresh 16-hex id; it is answered in the same header and sent to the gateway on every registry try, so intake's lines, the gateway's and Temporal's share it. The registry's request field is the idempotency key the gateway passed, else run:<workflow run id> (the capability request carries no console or edge request id). registry_unavailable carries a fixed-word cause: no_identity_token, gateway_unreachable, gateway_timeout, gateway_status_<code>, answer_unreadable, no_callback (the wait ended with nothing), operation_failed (the callback said failed or canceled), callback_token_mismatch, no_operation_token. A refused identity (401/403) is logged separately ("the registry refused this service's identity") and carries no cause.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Suite What it covers How it runs shared/contract validation helpers, intake session sign/verify, capability name lists vs manifests, the callback receiver, LooseBool go test connection-registry-1/internal/activities every capability against an in-memory fake repository: identity checks, naming (host-aware bases, numbering, truncation, unicode), reuse and forceNew, key hits, reason rules, metadata rules and the 20-key limit, the catalog editor (replay, stale writes, retired and delete rules), logging (no link, session or reason in a line) go test -race connection-registry-1/internal/store the PostgreSQL repository and every migration (up, down, up again; 00007 renumbering; 00008 with seeded revisions and grants: the destroy queue holds the right path and versions, the immutability trigger is back and still blocks deletes, an editor-renamed type is left alone, metadata cascades); concurrency (30 racing metadata writes) needs TEST_DATABASE_URL (a scratch PostgreSQL 16); skipped without it; CI provides one internal/capabilities each manifest schema accepts and refuses the payloads it should (capabilitytest.Verify) go test intake-1 every route and failure mode with a recognisable secret, session and token asserting none reaches a log line or an error body; the registry client against a fake Temporal (201 + callback before and after the answer, failed/canceled/mismatched token, retries and distinct per-try keys, causes); config and app wiring; the Nango client and Verify go test console-1 server routes (scope and boundary, write mapping, error sentences, the connect route and the link-never-logged check), the shared rule modules, static-render tests of the pages and dialogs, the session timer rules; about 330 tests vitest, tsc --noEmit, vite build openfga-bootstrap-1 the bootstrap run against a fake OpenFGA; the model drift test (the .fga source vs the embedded JSON) go test Not covered browser behaviour of the console (focus, the native dialogs, clipboard, CSS truncation) is not exercised by the HTML-render tests; the catalog Helm lint needs helm and runs in CI; outbound enforcement has no end-to-end test see runbooks

docs.title: Confirm a connect flow (dev)
docs.text:
1. As a tenant user with an editor session open the console, Connection types → Connect on a type, enter a reason. Expect the answer with a link; a second Connect within the hour returns the same pending connection with the reuse notice; Start another creates a numbered second one.
  2. Open the link: the connect page loads (session/inspect 200 in intake's debug log as session_inspected). For an API-key type enter the key (credential_written, connection_completed via=form, the connection shows active). For a Nango type the page sends you to Nango's connect UI; after approval Nango's webhook (webhook_received, connection_completed via=webhook) moves it to active.
  3. Check Temporal: the gateway workflow for each call shows the child ConnectionRegistryWorkflowV1 completing, and the Nexus callback state Succeeded.

docs.title: Failures seen while bringing Janus up (cause → fix)
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Connect page session/inspect returns 401 application/problem+json "Sign in to continue", intake has no logs the gateway did not have the intake routes: apps-de-v2-services-acd-proj-1 lacked the Janus namespace as a destination, so the api-gateway-1 ReferenceGrant failed and the app did not sync (no intake-1 HTTPRoute; the gateway policy kept the old open-path list) add ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-janus-1-ns-1 to the project's destinations (argocd-critical-stack PR 197); check the Application's sync result Gateway workflow returns PERMISSION_DENIED: this capability is internal INTERNAL_CALLERS unset in the registry because internalCallers sat under nango: in the GitOps values put it under connection-registry-1.registry.internalCallers Workflow completes but intake shows registry_unavailable / the page waits; Temporal shows "Nexus Callback has failed ... handler error (UNAUTHORIZED)" an Istio ALLOW policy on intake-1 listed only the API gateway and denied Temporal's delivery to port 3001 (403) the Temporal-callback AuthorizationPolicy (k8s-security PR 629); any new ALLOW policy on a callback receiver needs the same rule cause=gateway_status_500 with the gateway log "Workflow execution is already running" two identical gateway calls without an idempotency key shared a workflow id (a retry of a call still running, or concurrent polls) send a fresh idempotencyKey per try (done in console reads and intake) Nango webhook webhook_refused reason=invalid_signature while the connect session works the webhook was verified with the API key; Nango signs with the separate webhook signing key store the signing key in webhookSigningKey and use the two-file configuration; compare secret_fp UNAVAILABLE connect_base_url_not_configured / intake_base_url_not_configured the registry has no public base URLs set registry.connectBaseUrl / intakeBaseUrl in the environment values New pod in CreateContainerConfigError after a chart upgrade the chart reads a Secret key the Secret lacks (for example apiKey / signingKey before the VSO template added them) upgrade the GitOps resources first (keep the legacy key while the old chart runs), then the chart Console "service not answering" 503 historical: Execute answers 201 and the console treated it as unavailable the callback listener, allowlist and policies above

docs.title: Not verified
docs.text:
• Live cluster state. Nothing here was read from a running cluster; policy, sync and rollout statements come from the repositories on 2026-11-17. The k8s-security policies, the ArgoCD project change and the registry internalCallers fix were merged by the owner during the session, whose dev results (the API-key connect flow completing) are the owner's report.
  • Stage and prod. The owner states they run older charts (0.1.18 and 0.1.17); the tier profiles read in the repository show the chart switched off outside dev, which does not match, so the actual state of those branches was not confirmed.
  • Nango scope names (environment:connect_sessions:write, integrations:read / read_credentials, connections:read / read_credentials, connections:delete) come from Nango's public documentation found by search, because docs.nango.dev could not be opened from the session; confirm in the dashboard when creating each key. Whether the integration Check strictly needs read_credentials was not tested.
  • Shared-kit behaviour (budy-common-modules): the gateway's workflow-id derivation, the edge 401 rewriting and the STS verification are described from this repository's docs and the observed behaviour, not from the kit's source.
  • Image and chart versions are not stated here; they move with each release (changesets). The Release PR for the 2026-11-17 changes (registry 0.5 → next minor, contract, gateway-1, intake-1, console-1) had not been released when this was written.
  • Kargo stage durations are copied from the repository's AGENTS.md, not re-read from the Kargo project.
  • Gatekeeper budy-netpol-identity entries and the OPA rules were not re-read in this pass.

docs.title: console-1: the tenant console
docs.text: The Karkhana dashboard of one tenant, opened from the platform portal at karkhana.<env>.orangebox.ai. Built the same way as the dt-consulting-services-1 console (Node, React and @budybot/console-kit, tenant scope, one sealed host-only cookie), so it is a signed-in shell today: the one page, Sandboxes, stays empty until sandbox-manager-1 creates sandboxes. The point of building it first is the path (host, ingress, portal route, STS handoff, network policy, Vault session key), which is the same whatever the pages show.

docs.title: How a session reaches it
docs.text:
portal (nexusTarget route, tenant scope) -> STS: tenant session, aud = urn:budy:nexus:ob1-nexus-karkhana-cluster-1-endpoint-1:KarkhanaServiceV1
   -> handoff -> console-1 /auth/callback -> sealed host-only cookie (console-kit)
reads: console-1 -> its own API (/api/sandboxes), tenant taken from the token
  • Route type. The portal route karkhana-console-1 is a nexusTarget (endpoint ob1-nexus-karkhana-cluster-1-endpoint-1, service KarkhanaServiceV1). The route id is the STS handoff app id (auth-cluster-1 handoffRedeemerPolicies, bound to the console's ServiceAccount).
  • Scopes. CONSOLE_ACCEPTED_SCOPES=tenant, no minimum boundary: any tenant session may read. There are no writes yet.
  • Open point. The STS resolves the operations of a urn:budy:nexus: audience from OpenFGA. The dt-consulting-services-1 cluster publishes an authorization model for its service; whether KarkhanaServiceV1 needs one before the portal can mint the session is not checked yet.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Host karkhana.<env>.orangebox.ai, OIDC-protected ALB ingress to the shared Istio gateway, HTTPRoute to Service console-1 port 80 (argocd-eks-stack gtw/ingress) Route id / handoff app id karkhana-console-1 Namespace ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-karkhana-1-ns-1 (Istio ambient) Network Cilium and Istio together: the gateway reaches the pod over HBONE (:15008) and an Istio ALLOW names the gateway's principal and port 3000; the console reaches STS the same way (k8s-security AGENTS.md, "Istio ambient") Vault role ob1_tf_vault_karkhana-console-1_role_1; the session key (a random string of at least 32 characters, key sessionSecret) at app-kv-secrets-1 v1/de-v2/ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-karkhana-1-ns-1/karkhana-cluster-1-console-1/session, written by hand per environment Chart console-1, off by default; GitOps turns it on in dev first

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Sandboxes read from the sandbox store (ob1-karkhana-db-1) once sandbox-manager-1 writes to it, and credits and usage follow. Both need a read role in Vault and a database ingress rule, added with the manager.

docs.text: name: karkhana-cluster-1 kind: service description: Karkhana (workshop): the sandbox service. docs.title: karkhana-cluster-1
docs.text:
karkhana-cluster-1 is the Karkhana cluster. Karkhana is the Hindi and Urdu word for a workshop or factory: the place where things are made, here the sandboxes Digital Teammates and platform services work in. A caller asks for a sandbox of a named type; Karkhana records the request, and an operator runs the sandbox as a pod with a persistent workspace in the tenant's own namespace, under its own identity.

The design, the contract and the data model are in Sandboxes. The tenant console is in Console.

Status: built, being brought up in dev (checked 2026-11-13 against each repository's main). Released: the karkhana-cluster-1 chart 0.1.3 (gateway-1, sandbox-manager-1, console-1) and the operator chart sandbox-service-1-repo-1 0.3.6 (sandbox-operator-1 0.4.0, the first release of the new operator). Dev still pins karkhana-cluster-1 chart 0.1.1, so sandbox-manager-1 is not promoted to dev yet; stage and prod have none of it switched on. Not done: GitLab access from sandboxes, the sandbox-1 workload session kind (de-v2 #2414, open), an end-to-end test on a cluster. The list, with what each environment needs, is in Sandboxes: Status.

docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text:
A caller asks KarkhanaServiceV1 for a sandbox of a named type. sandbox-manager-1 checks the caller and writes one row of desired state to Postgres. sandbox-operator-1 watches those rows and makes Kubernetes match them: a pod with a persistent workspace in the tenant's namespace, under its own ServiceAccount. The operator writes back status, an event trail and usage. There is no custom resource per sandbox, no Service and no ingress: nothing calls into a sandbox.

caller ── STS token ──▶ gateway-1 ──▶ sandbox-manager-1 ──▶ Postgres (schema sandbox)
                                                              ▲   │ LISTEN/NOTIFY + resync
                                              status, usage   │   ▼
                                                        sandbox-operator-1 ──▶ pod, PVC, ServiceAccount, Secret
                                                                                (tenant namespace)

docs.title: 2. Decisions
docs.text: # Decision D1 Desired state lives in Postgres, written only by sandbox-manager-1. The operator reconciles from it. Temporal carries the request to the manager and nothing else: no lifecycle workflow. D2 The only custom resource is SandboxType (karkhana.budy/v1alpha1, cluster-scoped): the catalog of what a sandbox can be. D3 Sandboxes run in the tenant's namespace. The operator resolves it from the UserOrg whose spec.userOrgShortName is the tenant (status.tenantNamespace.name) and refuses a namespace that is not labelled platform.budy.ob1.ai/managed-by: user-org or is terminating. The manager has no Kubernetes access. D4 Tenant and requester come from the verified STS token the gateway passes (tenant scope only; platform-scoped callers are refused), never from the payload. The billing entity is the token's glassboxId, or the tenant when the token carries none (section 9). D5 Each sandbox has its own ServiceAccount and its own short-lived platform user, homed in the tenant (section 8). A sandbox never holds more than its requester and its type allow. D6 A sandbox has a persistent workspace volume. Pausing deletes the pod and keeps the volume; resuming starts a pod in the same zone. D7 Zone and region are recorded from the first schedule. A resume never moves a sandbox to another zone. D8 Network reach is a property of the type: networkProfile becomes the pod's budybot.io/netpol label and one cluster-wide policy per profile grants the destinations. D9 The operator is the only writer of Kubernetes objects. Its ClusterRole is fenced by an admission policy to tenant namespaces and to objects it labels (with one exception for pods/exec, section 6). D10 Usage is metered by the operator in the platform's standard record (usage metering standard). Karkhana does not price or enforce. D11 Only holders of a role listed in the type's allowedRoles, in an editor session, may use it. Today that is the dt-consulting-services coder (svcrole-dtcs-coder-1). Only that service role may call KarkhanaServiceV1 at all (authz-config entities/services/nexus-topology.yaml).

docs.title: 3. Components
docs.text:
Component Repository Runs in Does gateway-1 karkhana-cluster-1 ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-karkhana-1-ns-1 Verifies the STS token, validates the payload against the capability schema, dispatches. sandbox-manager-1 karkhana-cluster-1 (components/sandbox-manager-1, sub-chart sandbox-manager-1 of the umbrella chart karkhana-cluster-1-repo-1) same Authorization, limits, writes desired state, reads status. Owns the database migrations (a Job with the admin credentials). Temporal worker, task queue karkhana-cluster-1-sandbox-manager-1-tq. sandbox-operator-1 ob1_mn_gh_sandbox-service-1_repo-1 (chart sandbox-service-1-repo-1) ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-sandbox-1-ns-1 Reconciles Postgres rows into Kubernetes objects; status, events, usage; cleanup; validates SandboxType objects. sandbox-runner-1 ob1_mn_gh_sandbox-shell-1_repo-1 (cmd/sandbox-runner-1, in every image type, for example claude-code-1) the sandbox pod Process 1 of the sandbox: runs commands detached, writes files, keeps the sandbox's STS tokens fresh, clones the git source on first start when configured.

The row types, state names and capability payloads are Go types in the karkhana contract module (github.com/Budybot/karkhana-cluster-1_repo-1/shared/contract). The operator does not import that module yet: it keeps a mirror in internal/model (name for name, field for field) to be replaced by an import. The mirror's file_1 row does not carry request_key and ordinal, which only the manager reads.

docs.title: 4. Capabilities (sandbox-manager-1)
docs.text:
The manifest is charts/gateway-1/files/capabilities/sandbox-manager-1.yaml (workflow SandboxManagerWorkflowV1, default execution timeout 30 s); the manager's activities and the manifest must offer exactly the nine capabilities below.

All are tenant scope. All check that the caller holds a role in the type's allowedRoles on the tenant, in an editor session (see Authorization). A sandbox belongs to its requester: every capability that names a sandbox or a command also requires that the caller is that sandbox's requester in that tenant, and answers "not found" otherwise. There is no administrative access to another requester's sandbox.

Capability Input Result requestSandbox type, idempotencyKey, ttlSeconds?, zone?, git? {projectPath, branch}, labels? sandboxId, phase, created. The same key from the same requester with the same type returns the existing sandbox (created false). The same key with another type, or a key another requester of the tenant used, is a conflict. getSandbox sandboxId sandboxId, type, desiredState, phase, generation, observedGeneration, ttlSeconds, runningSeconds, zone, region, expiresAt, lastCommandAt, lastError, git, labels, createdAt, updatedAt. listSandboxes phase?, limit? (default 50, at most 200) The caller's sandboxes in the tenant, newest first. A sandbox is listed when its type is served and the caller holds a role for it, or when its type was retired. The eligibility is part of the SQL query, so the limit counts eligible rows only. pauseSandbox / resumeSandbox / deleteSandbox sandboxId sandboxId, desiredState, phase, generation. Repeating a request changes nothing, except that a resume of an idle-paused sandbox (phase paused or pausing, desired state still running) is a change. A deleted sandbox cannot be paused or resumed (conflict). deleteSandbox frees the sandbox's place against the type's limits; the workspace is removed. runCommand sandboxId, script, env?, timeoutSeconds?, idempotencyKey commandId, state, created. Refused unless the sandbox's desired state is running. The same key in the same sandbox returns the same command. Commands of one sandbox run one at a time, in the order queued. getCommand commandId commandId, sandboxId, state (queued, running, succeeded, failed, timed_out, cancelled), exitCode, outputTail (64 KiB at most), logPath (in the workspace), timeoutSeconds, cancelRequested, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt. putFiles sandboxId, files[] {path, content, mode?} sandboxId, files[] {fileId, path, state}. The files are queued; the operator writes them.

Payload limits (the manifest schema and the manager both enforce them):

Field Limit idempotencyKey 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits and . _ : / @ = -, starting with a letter or digit. ttlSeconds Positive, at most the type's maxTTLSeconds; 0 or absent means the type's defaultTTLSeconds. zone An availability zone such as us-west-2b. git.projectPath A GitLab project path: at least two segments of letters, digits, _, -, ., each starting with a letter, digit or _, none ending in ., .git or .atom, no ..; at most 255 characters. git.branch Valid by the rules of git check-ref-format --branch (no control characters, space or ~ ^ : ? * [ \, no leading - or /, no //, .., @{, trailing ., component starting with . or ending in .lock, not @); at most 255 characters. labels At most 16; key 1 to 63 characters (letters, digits, . _ / -), value at most 128 printable characters. script At most 64 KiB, UTF-8 text without NUL. env At most 64 entries, name [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* of at most 128 characters, value at most 4096 bytes, 32 KiB in total, names starting SANDBOX_ reserved. Non-secret only: it is stored with the command and readable with it. timeoutSeconds 1 to 86400; default 3600. putFiles 1 to 64 files, 256 KiB of content in total; path relative, clean, at most 1024 characters, inside the workspace and not under .sandbox/, no duplicates; mode a string of octal permission bits from 0400 to 0777 (for example "0644", the default), no setuid, setgid or sticky bit. Accepted for any sandbox that is not deleted, including a paused one; the files are written when the pod is running.

Limits enforced by the manager before a row is written: the type's limits.maxPerTenant and limits.maxPerRequester (sandboxes of that type whose desired state is not deleted; counted and inserted under a per-tenant advisory lock), and ttlSeconds no greater than the type's maximum.

putFiles queues its files once per request. The manager's own key for a request is the workflow id, run id and activity id; it is stored in file_1.request_key with the file's ordinal, so when the manager retries the activity it finds the rows and queues nothing new. putFiles takes no caller key: a caller that repeats the request queues the files again.

Authorization. The type's catalog entry maps each allowed role to an OpenFGA relation on tenant:<t> (for svcrole-dtcs-coder-1, active_svcrole_dtcs_coder_1, which is the coder grant and an editor session). The caller passes when it holds any one of the relations, checked with go/authz against the read-only OpenFGA proxy, with the session of its token. The coder grant is conditional (non_expired_grant, for workload sessions), so every check carries current_time (UTC, RFC 3339, to the second); the same holds for the token broker. A check that cannot be answered is refused, never allowed. The manager reads the catalog (per type: allowedRoles with their relations, limits, lifetime) from a file rendered from the chart's catalog values and mounted at /etc/sandbox-manager/catalog.json; it cannot read SandboxType objects, so the catalog values and the SandboxType resources must be kept in step by hand.

Retired types. A sandbox whose type has left the catalog stays reachable by its requester for getSandbox, getCommand, listSandboxes, pauseSandbox and deleteSandbox (ownership is enough); resumeSandbox, runCommand and putFiles are refused.

No capability cancels a command yet: command_1.cancel_requested exists, the manager may set it, and the operator honours it, but no capability sets it.

docs.title: 5. SandboxType
docs.text:
The CRD is in the operator chart (crds/karkhana.budy_sandboxtypes.yaml, short name sbxtype). The deployed instance is platform-crs v1/stacks/de-v2-sandbox-type/claude-coder-1.yaml:

apiVersion: karkhana.budy/v1alpha1
kind: SandboxType
metadata:
  name: claude-coder-1
spec:
  description: Claude Code for the dt-consulting-services coder
  image: 745404749629.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ob1-ecr-repo-v2/ob1_tf_aws_ecr_sandbox-shell-1_repo-1:claude-code-1-0.1.0
  workspace: {path: /workspace, size: 20Gi, storageClassName: sandbox-gp3-1}
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: "1", memory: 2Gi}
    limits: {cpu: "2", memory: 4Gi}
  lifetime:
    defaultTTLSeconds: 14400      # 4 hours
    maxTTLSeconds: 28800          # 8 hours
    idleTimeoutSeconds: 1800      # pause after 30 minutes without a running command
    pausedRetentionSeconds: 604800  # delete a paused sandbox after 7 days
  placement:
    nodeSelector: {budy.io/nodepool: "true", budy.io/compute-type: standard}
    tolerations: [{key: budy.io/nodepool-required, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
  networkProfile: sandbox-coder-1
  secrets:
    - name: claude-oauth-token
      secretRef: {name: claude-code-oauth-1, key: token}   # a Secret in the operator's namespace (VSO)
      env: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
  identity:
    kind: sandbox-1
    roles: [svcrole-dtcs-coder-1]
    audiences: ["urn:budy:nexus:ob1-nexus-gitjib-cluster-1-endpoint-1:GitjibBrokerV1"]
  allowedRoles: [svcrole-dtcs-coder-1]
  limits: {maxPerTenant: 10, maxPerRequester: 10}

Schema notes: a secrets entry sets exactly one of env (an environment variable) or file (an absolute path, mounted read-only, mode 0400); at most 16 entries. networkProfile matches sandbox-<name>-<n>. requests for cpu and memory are required, because usage is metered from them.

The TTL bounds a sandbox's total running time; time spent paused does not count, and a paused sandbox is removed after pausedRetentionSeconds. The idle timeout is measured from the later of the last command and the start of the run, and a sandbox with a queued or running command is never idle. Every field is validated by the CRD schema, and the operator's SandboxType controller sets a Validated condition for the spec's generation after the checks a schema cannot make: requests positive and not above limits, a positive workspace size, default TTL not above the maximum, unique secret names, environment names and files, no SANDBOX_ environment name, no file under /run/budy, /tmp, /var/run/secrets/budy or the workspace, maxPerRequester not above maxPerTenant. The operator refuses to start a sandbox of a type that is missing or not validated (phase failed, reason sandbox type); pause and delete still work. Types are deployed from platform-crs.

docs.title: 6. What the operator creates
docs.text:
All in the tenant namespace, all named from the sandbox id (sbx- and 20 lower-case base32 characters, [a-z2-7]):

Object Name Notes ServiceAccount <id>-sa-1 automountServiceAccountToken: false. The pod mounts one projected token, audience auth.budy.internal, at /var/run/secrets/budy/sts/token (lifetime sts.sandboxTokenExpirationSeconds, 3600 by default, at least 600). PersistentVolumeClaim <id>-pvc-1 ReadWriteOnce; size and class from the type. Kept across pauses, deleted with the sandbox. Secret <id>-secret-1 Created only when the type has secrets: a copy of the values they name, keyed by the entry name. Deleted on pause and on delete. Pod <id>-pod-1 One container sandbox, the type's image, command sandbox-runner-1 init. uid and gid 1000 (fsGroup 1000), non-root, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, read-only root, seccomp RuntimeDefault, restart policy Always, termination grace 30 s, no service links. Volumes: the workspace at the type's path, emptyDir /run/budy (64 Mi) and /tmp (1 Gi), the projected token. Ready when sandbox-runner-1 ready answers. Node selector and tolerations from the type; a required node affinity for the recorded zone (or the requested one) when there is one.

Environment of the container: SANDBOX_ID, SANDBOX_TENANT, SANDBOX_TYPE, SANDBOX_WORKSPACE; when the operator has an STS URL, SANDBOX_STS_URL, SANDBOX_STS_AUDIENCES (the type's identity audiences, as JSON), SANDBOX_STS_SESSION (editor) and SANDBOX_K8S_TOKEN_FILE; when the request has a git source and the operator has a git URL, SANDBOX_GIT_URL, SANDBOX_GIT_PROJECT, SANDBOX_GIT_BRANCH and SANDBOX_GIT_AUDIENCE (the operator's git.audience, else the type's first audience); then the type's secrets.

Labels on every object: app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: sandbox-operator-1, karkhana.budy/sandbox-id, karkhana.budy/sandbox-type. The pod also carries budybot.io/netpol: <networkProfile> and budy.io/user-org-short-name: <tenant> (the tenant namespace denies egress to pods without it).

docs.title: Operator behaviour
docs.text:
• Ownership. When a create finds the object already there, the operator adopts it only if it carries all three labels (managed-by, sandbox id, sandbox type). Otherwise the sandbox fails with reason name conflict, the object is left untouched, and the periodic resync looks again (no backoff). The Secret is written with a JSON patch whose test operations require the labels, so the API server checks ownership atomically; the operator never reads Secrets in tenant namespaces. Teardown and the sweep never delete an object without the labels, and a Secret delete carries the UID recorded when it was created.
  • Phase changes. A phase change and its event_1 row are written in one transaction. A failed step records phase failed with the reason in last_error and is retried with the controller's backoff; the move out of failed happens when a step succeeds.
  • Runs. A run opens when the pod is ready (start time: the pod's Ready transition) and closes when the pod stops. The measured totals stay in memory until the close has succeeded, so a failed close finds them on the retry. The meterer updates the cumulative totals of open runs only. Measured usage of a run is counted only while the run is open: it starts from zero when the run opens and is re-attached to the open run after an operator restart.
  • Provision timeout. A pod not ready 10 minutes after creation is deleted and the sandbox fails (pod not ready, with the scheduling or container reason).
  • Concurrency. One active replica (leader election by a Lease); four sandboxes reconciled in parallel.

docs.title: Operator permissions
docs.text:
• A ClusterRole with: pods (create, delete, get, list, watch), pods/exec (create), persistentvolumeclaims and serviceaccounts (create, delete, get, list, watch), secrets (create, patch, delete only: no read outside its own namespace), sandboxtypes (get, list, watch) and sandboxtypes/status (get, update, patch), userorgs (get, list, watch), namespaces and nodes (get, list, watch), persistentvolumes (get, to read the CSI volume handle), and metrics.k8s.io pods (get, list).
  • A ValidatingAdmissionPolicy sandbox-operator-1-fence, matched to the operator's ServiceAccount: create, update and delete of pods, persistentvolumeclaims, serviceaccounts and secrets are admitted only in a namespace labelled platform.budy.ob1.ai/managed-by: user-org and only on an object labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: sandbox-operator-1 (an update also needs the label on the stored object). pods/exec is a CONNECT request whose object is the exec options, not the pod, so the pod's labels cannot be checked: it is admitted only in such a namespace and only for a pod named <sandbox id>-pod-1.
  • A Role in its own namespace: Secrets (get, list, watch: the ones the types name), its leader-election Lease, and Events.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: The caller's command is a row. The operator starts it in the pod through sandbox-runner-1 exec (a short pods/exec, 30 s at most, SPDY transport by default), which runs it detached and writes its output and exit code under <workspace>/.sandbox/commands/<commandId>/. The operator polls with sandbox-runner-1 status and copies the state, the exit code and the output tail to the row; a command that ends by itself records a command event. A command therefore survives an operator restart, and a long run holds no stream open. Commands run in seq order, one at a time. A command the runner does not know after a pod replacement ends failed; one the pod restart interrupted carries a note. When a sandbox is deleted, queued commands end cancelled and a running one failed. Files from putFiles are written with sandbox-runner-1 put while the pod is running, and their content is removed from the database once written or failed.

docs.title: 7. Lifecycle
docs.text:
Desired state (sandbox_1.desired_state): running, paused, deleted. Observed phase (sandbox_status_1.phase):

pending → provisioning → running ⇄ pausing → paused ⇄ resuming → running
   any ── desired deleted, TTL reached or paused retention reached ──▶ deleting → deleted
   failed: a step could not complete; the reason is in last_error and the operator retries with backoff
  • Provisioning: resolve and verify the namespace, check the type, create the workload session (section 8) and wait until it is active, create ServiceAccount, PVC and Secret, then the pod. If the request names a zone the pod is required there; otherwise the scheduler chooses. When the pod is scheduled the operator records region and zone from the node and never changes them. When the pod is ready the run opens, expires_at is set to the run's start plus the remaining running budget, and the phase is running. Without an identity service URL the sandbox starts without an identity and without STS environment, and an identity event says so.
  • Pause: by request (desired_state paused), or by the operator when no command has run for idleTimeoutSeconds (the desired state stays running; observed_generation is held at the generation seen when the pause began). The pod and the Secret are deleted, the run closes (stop reason paused or idle) and the identity is released. The volume stays.
  • Resume: the same steps as provisioning with the existing volume and a node affinity for the recorded zone. An idle-paused sandbox resumes when the manager writes a newer generation (resumeSandbox) or a command is queued. A pod that cannot be scheduled in the zone is not moved: after the provision timeout the sandbox is failed.
  • Interruption: a pod lost to a node (spot reclaim, drain) is recreated in the recorded zone; the run that ended is closed (interrupted), an error event pod lost is written, the phase goes back to provisioning and a new run opens. A pod that ended Failed or Succeeded (evicted, finished) is deleted and recreated.
  • Expiry: the running budget (ttl_seconds, the closed runs plus the open one) is used up: the sandbox is deleted (stop reason expired). A paused sandbox is deleted pausedRetentionSeconds after paused_at (stop reason deleted).
  • Delete: the pod is removed, the run closed, the commands finished (queued ones cancelled, a running one failed), the identity released, then the Secret, ServiceAccount and PVC are removed; the row is kept for the record and its usage stays.
  • Cleanup: every object and every volume the operator creates, and the workload session, is a row in resource_1. A sweep every 10 minutes compares the rows with the labelled pods, volumes and ServiceAccounts in the cluster, both ways: labelled objects of a deleted or unknown sandbox older than 10 minutes are deleted; a row whose object is gone is released; the Secret of a deleted or paused sandbox is deleted by its row (Secrets cannot be listed); and an object carrying the label but no row is reported once as a cleanup event. Objects without the sandbox-id label are never touched.

The operator learns of changes by LISTEN on the channel sandbox_1 (a trigger notifies with the sandbox id on every insert or update of sandbox_1, every insert of command_1 or update of its cancel_requested, and every insert of file_1), by watches on the pods and volumes it labels, and by a full resync of every sandbox that is not deleted, every 60 seconds and after every reconnect of the listener, which is also how it recovers after a restart. Each sandbox row has a generation the manager increments and the operator echoes as observed_generation.

docs.title: 8. Identity
docs.text:
A sandbox acts as itself, not as its requester and not with a token handed to it.

  1. On start the operator asks authz-manager-1 (POST /v1/workload-sessions, authenticated with the operator's projected ServiceAccount token whose audience is authz-manager-1, identity.tokenAudience) for a workload session of kind sandbox-1: the tenant, the namespace, the ServiceAccount, the requester, the roles the type lists, the glassboxId, an expiry and the sandbox id as the reference. The expiry is the remaining running budget plus 5 minutes of grace. It polls GET /v1/workload-sessions/{id} until the state is active.
  2. authz-manager-1 creates a user of the workload-session UserType homed in that tenant whose only identity is that ServiceAccount, and grants it the roles with that expiry (a conditional grant, non_expired_grant, so OpenFGA ends it by itself). A role is granted only if the kind's configuration allows it and the requester holds it on the tenant now and until the expiry; the namespace must be the tenant's; the ServiceAccount must be bound to no other user. The user has no access to any other tenant. A session whose requester later loses a role, or whose tenant is retired, is ended by the maintenance task.
  3. In the pod, sandbox-runner-1 exchanges the projected Kubernetes token (audience auth.budy.internal) at the STS (POST /v2/oauth2/token, token exchange, tenant scope, session editor) for STS tokens for the audiences the type lists, writes them under /run/budy/tokens/ (an index.json maps each audience to its file) and renews them at two thirds of their lifetime, with exponential backoff from 1 s to 60 s on failure. Tools read them from there. The runner's git credential helper hands the token of SANDBOX_GIT_AUDIENCE to git for the host of SANDBOX_GIT_URL; once a GitLab proxy exists, GitLab access uses that STS token through gitjib's token broker and no GitLab credential reaches the sandbox. That path is not deployed yet (Status).
  4. On pause and on delete the operator releases the session (a resume creates a new one for the same reference). If the operator is down, the expiry ends it.

The workload session is a general authz-manager-1 capability: sandbox-1 is one entry of its configuration (config.workloadSessionKinds: the callers that may create, read and release, the roles a session may carry, its maximum lifetime from creation, and the namespaces). The entry for sandbox-1 is: caller the operator's ServiceAccount (system:serviceaccount:ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-sandbox-1-ns-1:sandbox-operator-1), roles [svcrole-dtcs-coder-1], maxLifetime: 8h5m (the type's maximum TTL of 8 hours plus the operator's 5-minute grace), namespaces ["$tenant"]. It is written in de-v2 #2414 (open), for dev only. authz-manager-1 refuses a workload-session UserType that has creators or is tenant-managed. A create for a kind and reference whose earlier session is past its expiry but not yet swept ends that session and creates the replacement. The operator's service user sandbox-operator-1 holds the requester relation on the create and release operations (authz-config bundles/authz-manager-policy.yaml).

docs.title: 9. Billing entity and usage
docs.text:
• glassboxId is a standard STS claim: the entity that pays for what a session does. It is a digital teammate of the tenant (the default for a teammate's own session) or the tenant itself. A service acting in a tenant names it when it exchanges, and the STS checks that it belongs to the tenant. For a workload session it is fixed: authz-manager-1 records it as a glassbox tuple on the session's user (the tenant, or a digital teammate of it that is neither admin nor owner) and the STS stamps that value on every session it mints for that user. An OpenFGA model without user#glassbox (OpenFGA relation_not_found) means "no fixed billing entity" and the default applies; any other OpenFGA error fails closed.
  • The manager stores the caller's glassboxId on the sandbox, or the tenant when the token carries none; the workload session carries it, so the sandbox's own sessions are stamped with it too. gitjib's token broker uses the claim to pick the teammate: it is matched against a DigitalTeammate's spec.name (the generated teammate id), and the tenant id leaves the teammate to the request.
  • The operator writes usage_1 rows with service karkhana-cluster-1, resource reference sandbox/<id> and attributes type, zone and region:
Meter Unit Written for a window when sandbox.cpu-request-seconds seconds a pod held its CPU request: the request in cores times the seconds a run overlapped the window sandbox.memory-request-gib-seconds gib-seconds the same, for the memory request in GiB sandbox.storage-gib-seconds gib-seconds the volume existed, also while the sandbox is paused (from the volume's resource_1 row) sandbox.cpu-used-seconds, sandbox.memory-used-gib-seconds seconds, gib-seconds metrics.k8s.io answered and a sample fell in the window

Windows are five minutes, aligned to the clock (:00, :05, ...) in UTC, and a window is written once it has closed, at the next check (the operator checks every 30 seconds, usage.interval, which is also the metrics sampling interval). The idempotency key is sandbox/<id>/<meter>/<window start, RFC 3339 UTC>; an existing key is skipped. At start the operator writes the windows closed while it was down, up to 288 windows per sandbox per pass, and it keeps writing for a sandbox for 2 hours after its last run or volume. Used meters are sampled in memory, so a restart loses the measured usage of the windows still open; the request and storage meters are recomputed from run_1 and resource_1. run_1 holds one row per run (from a pod start to its stop) with the same totals, refreshed while the run is open. - Glassbox reads usage_1 with the schema's read-only role. Rating and enforcement are Glassbox's.

docs.title: 10. Data (database ob1-karkhana-db-1, schema sandbox)
docs.text:
Table Writer Content sandbox_1 manager id, tenant, requester, glassbox_id, type, idempotency_key (unique per tenant), desired_state, ttl_seconds, requested_zone, git, labels, generation, created_at, updated_at sandbox_status_1 operator sandbox_id, phase, observed_generation, namespace, region, zone, pod, service_account, workload_session_id, running_seconds (the closed runs), expires_at, paused_at, last_command_at, last_error, updated_at command_1 manager inserts and sets cancel_requested; operator completes id, seq, sandbox_id, script, env, timeout_seconds, idempotency_key (unique per sandbox), state, cancel_requested, exit_code, output_tail, log_path, created_at, started_at, finished_at. The operator writes state, exit_code, output_tail, log_path, started_at and finished_at. file_1 manager inserts, operator completes id, seq, sandbox_id, request_key and ordinal (the manager's own identity for one putFiles execution, derived from its workflow run and step, and the file's place in it; unique per sandbox when the key is set), path, mode, content (removed once the operator has finished the file), state, error, created_at, written_at run_1 operator id, sandbox_id, started_at, stopped_at, stop_reason (paused, idle, expired, deleted, interrupted, failed), node, zone, cpu_request_millis, memory_request_bytes, storage_bytes, and the cumulative meters cpu_request_seconds, memory_request_gib_seconds, cpu_used_seconds, memory_used_gib_seconds (the last two null without metrics) usage_1 operator the standard usage record resource_1 operator id, sandbox_id, kind (Pod, PersistentVolumeClaim, ServiceAccount, Secret, WorkloadSession), namespace, name, uid, external_id (the EBS volume), region, zone, size_bytes, state (active, released), created_at, released_at event_1 operator id, sandbox_id, at, kind (phase, error, cleanup, identity, command), from_phase, to_phase, reason, detail

Roles: sandbox-manager-1 uses ob1-karkhana-db-1-sandbox-rw-role; the operator uses ob1-karkhana-db-1-sandbox-operator-rw-role; readers use ob1-karkhana-db-1-sandbox-ro-role. These are per-schema roles, not the database's three standard roles: the platform's database grants job creates them and the schema (the database's entry in standard-db-custom-grants-1, argocd-eks-stack) and gives Vault the right to issue credentials in them, and each workload's Vault catalog entry names its role. The migration (00001_init.sql) runs as the admin role, creates no role, and fails if the manager or operator role is missing. It then revokes everything from the manager and operator roles on the eight tables and grants exactly:

Role Grants manager SELECT on all eight tables; INSERT and UPDATE on sandbox_1; INSERT on command_1 and UPDATE of cancel_requested; INSERT on file_1; the sequences of command_1 and file_1 operator SELECT on all eight tables; INSERT and UPDATE on sandbox_status_1, run_1, resource_1, event_1; UPDATE of state, exit_code, output_tail, log_path, started_at, finished_at on command_1; UPDATE of content, state, error, written_at on file_1; INSERT on usage_1; the sequence of event_1 read-only SELECT (default privileges)

No role can DELETE. The trigger function sandbox.notify_sandbox_1 sends the sandbox id on the channel sandbox_1.

docs.title: 11. Network
docs.text:
Profile Destinations sandbox-coder-1 DNS; the STS (sts-service, over HBONE); the npm proxy (npm-proxy-1, over HBONE); api.anthropic.com and platform.claude.com on 443. Nothing else, and no ingress. It denies the kube-apiserver, the node and other nodes, and the instance metadata address. There is no rule for GitLab yet: no GitLab proxy exists (Status).

A profile is a CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy in k8s-security (egress-tenant-sandbox-coder-1-allow-required, under v1/objects/rbac/cluster/manifests/tenant-sandbox-netpol/) that selects the label in namespaces managed by a UserOrg. Tenant namespaces are Istio ambient, so a call to an in-mesh service leaves the pod as HBONE and the destination's own policy limits tenant callers to one port. The label value sandbox-coder-1 is reserved by an OPA constraint to pods labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: sandbox-operator-1. Ingress to a sandbox is denied by the namespace; the operator reaches it with pods/exec, which does not use the pod network.

The operator's own policy allows the kube-apiserver, Postgres (CNPG in dev and stage, RDS in prod) and the authz-manager-1 API; the manager's allows Temporal, the read-only OpenFGA proxy and Postgres.

docs.title: 12. How dt-consulting-services is meant to use it
docs.text:
Planned: delivery-lead-1 (phase 2 of dt-consulting-services-1; not built) would run as the coder service user and exchange into the engagement's tenant, naming the requesting teammate as glassboxId. Then:

  1. requestSandbox {type: claude-coder-1, idempotencyKey: <engagement id>, git: {projectPath, branch}}.
  2. getSandbox until running.
  3. putFiles with the PRD and the HLD.
  4. runCommand with the Claude Code invocation; getCommand until it ends; repeat for each round of the compile and CI loop.
  5. pauseSandbox while a review is pending, resumeSandbox to continue, deleteSandbox when the engagement closes.

The git source needs the GitLab path in Status; until then, put the files with putFiles.

docs.title: 13. Not in this design
docs.text:
• Archiving a paused workspace to a snapshot (the cluster has no snapshot controller).
  • Sandbox types other than claude-coder-1.
  • Callers other than the coder service role.
  • Cancelling a command through a capability.

docs.title: nainai console
docs.text:
The admin and support UI for the DT Dynamo worker fleet that operator-1 manages. It is the first console built on the Platform Console Standard; the runbook for adding another is the wiki skill scaffold-platform-console.

Status (October 2026): deployed. A user signed in through the platform portal, opened the 9i page and saw the workers and their deployment states. The Rollouts and Templates pages exist but have not been checked end to end.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Lets platform admins and support see, in one place, the worker deployments operator-1 manages: which image each runs, which build is current and which is the target, whether the resource is ready, and the Temporal worker controller's view of each rollout.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text: Component console-1 in nainai-cluster-1_repo-1 (non-Nexus, Node component), image and chart released with the cluster Scope System scope only (scopeType=platform tokens). Its data sources use the pod's credentials, so a tenant token gets 403 Hosts nainai.dev-1.orangebox.ai, nainai.stage-1.orangebox.ai, nainai.prod-2.orangebox.ai. The same hosts carry the operator's public /webhook/ecr route, which is evaluated first (group.order); the UI route is behind the ALB's Google OIDC Sign-in Platform UI route nainai-console-1 (app id = route id, resource = https://nainai.<env>.orangebox.ai), STS handoff redeemed by the console's service account Data k8s list adapters on nainai.ob1.ai DTDynamoDeployment and DTWorkerTemplate, temporal.io WorkerDeployment, and events. Views are projections that pick fields by name Kubernetes access ClusterRole ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-nainai-1-ns-1-console-1: get, list on those kinds and events; no secrets, no pods/exec Session key Vault KV v1/de-v2/ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-nainai-1-ns-1/nainai-cluster-1-console-1/session, key sessionSecret, synced by VSO

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
• Fleet: one row per worker (name, namespace, image tag, current and target build, ready reason, rollout state) with a detail panel for conditions and events.
  • Rollouts: the Temporal worker controller's current and target version of each worker deployment.
  • Templates: DTWorkerTemplate resources (cluster scoped).

Lists request up to 500 rows and say when they are cut. Paging with a continuation token is in @budybot/console-kit (0.2.0) and is not adopted here yet.

docs.title: Where it is wired
docs.text: Repository What nainai-cluster-1_repo-1 components/console-1, charts/console-1, catalog entry budy-common-modules @budybot/console-kit vault-gitops role ob1_tf_vault_nainai-console-1_role_1, default KV policy k8s-security network policies, netpol identity, ReferenceGrant, gateway egress, nainai-shared-vso-1 allowed namespaces argocd-critical-stack nainai AppProject cluster-resource whitelist argocd-eks-stack OIDC-protected Ingress and HTTPRoute de-v2 STS redeemer policy, audiences, client resources; nainai app values de-v2 (frontend-cluster-1 values) platform-ui-1 route (routeDefaults and per-environment routes) and form-action origin

docs.title: Open items
docs.text:
• Adopt usePagedList from console-kit 0.2.0.
  • Temporal versions panel and connector: not built; add Temporal credentials when Temporal authentication ships.
  • The next phase is the console's own roadmap (the V2 build of the 9i controller UI), tracked separately.

docs.title: nainai-cluster-1
docs.text:
nainai-cluster-1 manages the deployments of DT Dynamo Workers. It loads updates, starts and restarts workers, and coordinates transitions while older workflows are still running on the previous version.

Status (17 November 2026): the gateway is released; operator-1, the Crossplane provider that deploys DT Dynamo workers, is built and enabled in dev-1 (de-v2 charts/apps/nainai-cluster-1). Its design is in the repository's docs/operator-1.md; this page summarises it. The deployer component sketched below under Proposed shape is not built, and no deploy command is planned (see How a worker is deployed).

docs.title: How a worker is deployed
docs.text:
A DT Dynamo worker deploys itself when CI pushes its image. Nothing calls nainai to deploy or roll back a worker.

teammate's GitLab fork, protected default branch
  └─ CI build-image job ──▶ push dynamo-worker-<x.y.z>-<sha7> to <env account>/v1/dt-root-ns/v1/<org>/<dt>/dynamo-worker-<n>
ECR push event ──▶ EventBridge rule (environment account) ──▶ API destination ──▶ operator-1 /webhook/ecr   (5-minute poll as fallback)
operator-1 ──▶ reconcile DTDynamoDeployment ──▶ WorkerDeployment on the newest tag matching the template's pattern
temporal-worker-controller ──▶ the new version rolls out; running workflows finish on the version they started
Who chooses the image operator-1: the most recently pushed tag in the worker's own ECR repository that matches a regex. No tag is accepted as input (operator decision 8) How a push arrives ECR → EventBridge → HTTPS webhook on the operator, authenticated by a shared token whose SHA-256 the operator holds; a 5-minute poll catches missed events (decisions 9 and 10) Who creates the worker resource The DigitalTeammate Crossplane composition composes one DynamoWorker per worker, which creates the tenant ECR repository, the DTDynamoDeployment and the Temporal Connection What a publish does dt-consulting-services' Mission registry only observes which version runs (a to-do in its saga); it never asks nainai to deploy or roll back Rolling back Push an earlier commit through the same pipeline (a revert merge in the fork)

docs.title: Boundary (proposed)
docs.text:
Owns Does not own The decision and sequencing of when a Dynamo Worker version starts, restarts and drains The code or packages a worker runs (see gitjib-cluster-1) Transition coordination while older workflows are still running The Temporal server, Kubernetes cluster and Worker Controller The cluster's Nexus contract for requesting deployments and reading transition state Tenant lifecycle (budy-platform-operator-1) and DT provisioning (dt-manager-1)

The "older workflows still running" requirement is exactly what Temporal Worker Deployment Versioning with Pinned behavior provides (executions finish on the version they started). Whether nainai drives that mechanism for Dynamo Workers or wraps it is an open question below.

docs.title: Proposed shape
docs.text:
Repository type Nexus-first: gateway + components (the reference instance of the standard) Gateway gateway: Nexus service DeploymentServiceV1 (decided October 2026) with DescribeCapabilities First component operator-1 (built; see How a worker is deployed). The deployer drafted here earlier, with verbs loadUpdate, startWorker, restartWorker, getTransitionStatus, is not built and no deploy command is planned: a push deploys. A read-only status capability may come later for the Mission registry's observe step Likely platform access Kubernetes API (namespaced RBAC) or the platform operator CRDs; decided in k8s-security, not in this repo

Bootstrap target (gateway-only first pass): gateway container, empty capability registry, umbrella chart, CI green, one image published, dev smoke test (DescribeCapabilities through the Nexus endpoint, one denied-tenant call). Components, and the capability smoke test, follow one at a time. See the standard's definition of done.

docs.title: Names (derived from the standard)
docs.text: Kubernetes namespace ob1-tf-eks-de-v2-nainai-1-ns-1 Nexus endpoint ob1-nexus-nainai-cluster-1-endpoint-1 Task queues nainai-cluster-1-gateway-tq, nainai-cluster-1-deployer-tq Umbrella chart nainai-cluster-1-repo-1 Image repository ob1-ecr-repo-v2/ob1_tf_aws_ecr_nainai-cluster-1_repo-1 Helm repository ob1-helm-chart-repo-v1/nainai-cluster-1-repo-1

docs.title: Callers and callees (assumed, unconfirmed)
docs.text:
• Callers: none for deployment (a push deploys). A read of a worker's current version may be added for the Mission registry's observe step.
  • Update source: the worker's image, built by its GitLab fork's CI with credentials from gitjib's token broker.
  • Callees: Kubernetes API or budy-platform-operator-1 CRDs; Temporal for deployment state.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. Definition. Answered (November 2026): a Dynamo worker is a Temporal worker, one per DT workbench, running deterministic workflows. See the glossary.
  2. Relationship to the platform operator. budy-platform-operator-1 reconciles BudyWorkerPool and BudyWorker per userOrg. Does nainai create or modify those, replace part of that behavior, or manage a different class of worker?
  3. Update source and trigger. Answered (November 2026): an image tag pushed by the worker repository's CI; the ECR push event triggers the load (operator decisions 8 and 9). It is not a Nexus call: see How a worker is deployed.
  4. Who calls it. Which services are Nexus callers, and what identity and tenancy do they present?
  5. Transition policy. Rollout and sunset behavior per worker (ramp steps, scale-down and delete delays); where it is configured; who may override it.
  6. Failure and rollback. What happens when a started worker fails readiness mid-transition; is rollback a new call or automatic?
  7. Kubernetes permissions. Does it need cluster-scoped access, or only namespaced access in tenant namespaces? Needed before the k8s-security onboarding PR.
