  • Platform Console Standard: the consoles the portal launches.
  • Network Policy & mTLS.
  • Application Cluster CI/CD Standard.

docs.title: Usage metering standard
docs.text: How a platform service records what a tenant consumed, so that Glassbox can turn it into credits and decide what happens when they run out. The first producer is Karkhana (sandboxes).

docs.title: Three jobs, three owners
docs.text: Job Owner What it is Metering each service Appending immutable records of quantities consumed. No prices, no credits, no decisions. Rating Glassbox Turning quantities into credits with a price book Glassbox owns. Prices change without touching a service. Enforcement Glassbox, through authorization Writing the fact "this billing entity may or may not consume" where the STS and authorization checks read it. A service never checks a balance itself.

docs.title: The billing entity: glassboxId
docs.text: Every STS session carries a glassboxId claim: the entity that pays for what the session does. It is a digital teammate of the session's tenant (the default for a teammate's own session) or the tenant itself. A service acting in a tenant on someone's behalf names the entity when it exchanges, and the STS refuses one that does not belong to the tenant. Gateways pass it to components as GlassboxID next to the tenant and the user. A service records it and does not choose it. One fallback exists today: Karkhana's sandbox-manager-1 bills the tenant when a token carries no glassboxId (the STS stamps one on every tenant session, so this is a safeguard).

docs.title: The usage record
docs.text:
One row per meter per window per resource.

Field Type Meaning id uuid The record. idempotency_key text, unique <resource_ref>/<meter>/<window_start> (window start as RFC 3339 UTC, for example sandbox/sbx-.../sandbox.cpu-request-seconds/2026-11-13T10:05:00Z): writing the same window twice is a no-op. A correction appends #c<n> (see the rules). glassbox_id text The billing entity, from the token. tenant text The tenant, from the token. service text The producing service, for example karkhana-cluster-1. meter text What was measured: <domain>.<quantity>-<unit> in lower case, for example sandbox.cpu-request-seconds. quantity numeric How much, in the meter's unit, within the window. Never cumulative. unit text seconds, gib-seconds, count, tokens, ... window_start, window_end timestamptz The period the quantity covers. Windows of one resource and meter do not overlap. Karkhana's windows are five minutes long, aligned to the clock in UTC, and written once closed. resource_ref text What consumed it, for example sandbox/<id>. attributes jsonb Dimensions rating may need (Karkhana writes type, zone and region). Never personal data. recorded_at timestamptz When the row was written.

docs.title: Rules for a producer
docs.text:
• Append only. A record is never updated or deleted by the producer. A correction is a new record for the same resource, meter and window whose quantity is the signed difference, whose idempotency key is the corrected record's key followed by #c<n> (n counts corrections of that record from 1), and whose attributes carry correctionOf (the corrected record's id) and reason (Karkhana's operator writes no corrections today). The rule that windows do not overlap applies to records that are not corrections; the consumed quantity of a window is the sum of its record and its corrections.
  • Windowed, not on completion. A long-running resource reports every few minutes (five by default), so a crash loses at most one window and Glassbox sees consumption as it happens.
  • Measure what was reserved and, where possible, what was used. They are different meters (...-request-seconds, ...-used-seconds); rating chooses.
  • Idempotent. The idempotency key makes a retried write safe.
  • A new meter is a documented meter. Each service lists its meters, units and attributes in its own design page.
  • Read access. The records live in the service's own database, in a table named usage_<n>, readable by a read-only role that Glassbox holds. A service that cannot offer that exposes the same records through a capability.

docs.title: What a producer does not do
docs.text: It does not hold a balance, price anything, refuse a request for lack of credit, or call Glassbox on the request path.

docs.title: Budy 2 FAQ
docs.text: This FAQ accompanies the Budy 2 Press Release. It answers the questions we expect from customers and the internal team; the Product Vision defines the durable principles behind those answers.

docs.title: What is Budy 2?
docs.text: Budy 2 is a Digital Teammate: a long-running AI counterpart that users can teach, delegate to, and grow with over time. It combines persistent context, approved tools and permissions, visible work, and dependable execution so a user can move meaningful work forward without personally orchestrating every thread, tool, and handoff.

docs.title: Is Budy 2 a chatbot?
docs.text: No. A user may communicate with Budy in chat when that is useful, but chat is only one interface. Budy is a persistent workspace where users can see active work, outputs, decisions, questions, context, permissions, and progress.

docs.title: How is Budy different from ChatGPT, Claude, or a basic AI workflow?
docs.text:
Those products are extremely useful, but they often leave the user as the orchestrator: supervising separate chats and tools, carrying context between them, and turning an impressive output into an operating process. Budy is designed for an enduring working relationship. It retains useful context, can be taught a working style, connects to approved tools, takes work forward over time, and makes its actions and status visible. It is also designed so that non-technical builders do not need to become workflow engineers to access that capability.

The difference becomes clear after the initial LLM “wow.” An analysis, dashboard, or prototype can look transformative until someone tries to implement it reliably in the real world. Budy is built to close that implementation gap—not simply to generate a more impressive answer.

docs.title: Does Budy only respond to individual requests?
docs.text: No. Budy has an enduring role and set of responsibilities that its owner teaches and refines over time. It can receive individual requests, but it does not treat each request as an isolated assignment. It uses its understanding of the owner’s goals, working style, active work, and prior decisions to take work forward coherently.

docs.title: Does Budy improve its own work over time?
docs.text: Yes, within the boundaries its owner has set. Budy reflects on completed work and recurring patterns: for example, how it could have made the prior week more efficient or completed a similar project faster, better, or at lower cost next time. It should surface meaningful improvements and ask when changing direction, scope, or authority requires the owner’s judgment.

docs.title: Who is Budy for?
docs.text: Budy is for high-agency, non-technical builders. They are analytical, creative, and biased toward action. They may be founders, owner-operators, or leaders in functions such as sales, operations, finance, or marketing. They know their work and can identify what would be valuable; they need a capable system to help them build and execute.

docs.title: Who is Budy not for?
docs.text: Budy is not intended to be a cheap, casual AI subscription for every knowledge worker. It is also not designed for customers who want a consulting firm to define every use case or a hidden human service to operate the product for them. Budy is most valuable when its owner wants to actively teach, delegate to, and grow a powerful working system.

docs.title: Is Budy an industry-specific product?
docs.text: No. Budy is an agnostic platform, not an AI feature built for a single vertical. We may learn from and serve customers in particular industries, but our focus is a shared user disposition rather than a vertical sales playbook.

docs.title: What happens in the first day?
docs.text: The first-day experience should establish enough context, access, and direction for Budy to complete or advance a meaningful piece of work. The exact outcome differs by customer. The important promise is not a generic demo; it is a credible realization that Budy understands something important about the user’s work and can become a source of compounding leverage.

docs.title: Does Budy require a salesperson, consultant, or human operator?
docs.text: No customer interaction with one is required. Budy is product-led: users should be able to discover the product, purchase an evaluation tier, onboard, and achieve initial value through Budy itself. We aim for an experience that feels white-glove through sophisticated AI, compute, and product design. Budy is designed to deliver that care and reliability through the product itself.

docs.title: Why call the experience white-glove if there is no human touch?
docs.text: White-glove describes the quality of the experience: thoughtful onboarding, contextual guidance, proactive help, exceptional first-use value, and attention to detail. Budy itself delivers this experience through extensive use of models and compute. It is not a promise of customer-facing human concierge service.

docs.title: What is the Explore tier?
docs.text: Explore is a paid evaluation tier, expected to be $200–$500 per month and provide roughly one-tenth of the capacity of Part-Time. It lets a serious prospective customer buy with a credit card, use Budy on real work, and decide whether to buy a full-capacity Budy. We may accept break-even or modestly negative economics on this tier because its role is to make the product’s potential tangible.

docs.title: Is Explore a free trial or a freemium plan?
docs.text: Neither. It is a paid evaluation tier. “Freemium” suggests a free, indefinitely useful product with paid upgrades; “free trial” suggests a time-limited preview. Explore is a meaningful, paid way to experience Budy on real work before deciding to buy the product; Part-Time is the starting point for owning Budy, not merely an Explore upgrade.

docs.title: What will Budy cost?
docs.text: The expected core plans are Part-Time at $5,000/month, Full-Time at $10,000/month, and Heavy / Max at $20,000+/month. The plans differ primarily by capacity: Full-Time is roughly 2× Part-Time capacity and Heavy / Max roughly 4× or more. Final package boundaries and the final highest-tier name are still to be defined. The pricing principle is firm: Budy is premium because persistent context, reliable execution, secure access, and an exceptional AI-delivered experience require material capability and compute.

docs.title: Why is Budy priced at this level?
docs.text: The product is designed to create substantial leverage for people with meaningful scope and budget. We will not strip out the intelligence, reliability, security, or onboarding experience required to fit a commodity subscription price. The relevant comparison is not a general AI chat subscription; it is the value of a persistent, capable teammate that can move important work forward.

docs.title: How does Budy learn context without learning the wrong thing?
docs.text: Budy should retain history as permitted and promote information into usable context only when it has a clear purpose and sufficient confidence. Users must be able to inspect, correct, and guide the context Budy uses. We prefer deliberate, accurate learning over a large but unreliable memory.

docs.title: Can Budy take actions in other systems?
docs.text: Yes, only when the owner explicitly grants the required access and Budy operates within the approved scope. Budy makes permissions, intended actions, and resulting work understandable. Like a good employee, it acts when it has clarity and the decision is low-impact or reversible; it asks for clarification or authorization when an action is ambiguous, consequential, or difficult to undo.

docs.title: How is Budy safe and accountable?
docs.text: Budy always identifies itself as Budy and does not impersonate a user or another person. Access is scoped, actions are visible, and Budy uses impact and reversibility to determine when it can act independently and when it should ask. Internal Agent Success review can add a further reliability safeguard; it is not positioned as a customer approval promise. Internally, we also separate reasoning from predictable execution so that a broad idea cannot silently become an unbounded action.

docs.title: Will Budy work with a team?
docs.text:
Yes. Budy can share outputs, coordinate work, and interact with collaborators where the owner chooses. But the owner’s direct relationship with Budy comes first; a team rollout is an expansion path, not a requirement to receive value.

This is especially valuable for people who have not adopted systems, processes, chatbots, or copilots in the past. Budy should not require them to become AI operators. It should let them participate through the familiar experience of working with a teammate that has a role, takes work forward, and communicates when needed.

docs.title: What should we measure to know Budy is working?
docs.text: We care most about time to first meaningful outcome, repeat delegation, growth in the useful work owners teach Budy to do, trust in its execution, retention, and expansion. We do not treat generic activity or task volume as proof of value.

docs.title: Introducing Budy 2, the Digital Teammate for People Who Build
docs.text:
A premium, long-running AI teammate for high-agency professionals who want to teach, delegate, and make meaningful work move forward.

August 2026 — Today we are introducing Budy 2, a new kind of personal computer for work. Budy 2 is a Digital Teammate: a persistent AI counterpart that professionals can teach, delegate to, and grow with over time.

AI has already made it easier to write, research, analyze, and experiment. But for most professionals, it does not remove the burden of orchestration. They still supervise separate chats and tools, decide which thread matters, carry context between them, turn an impressive output into a working process, and keep the work moving.

Many have felt the initial AI “wow”: an analysis or dashboard makes it seem that a problem or process has been solved—or will no longer be a problem. Then comes the attempt to implement it in the real world, and the realization that the output is not yet an operating system for getting work done. Budy 2 is the answer to that gap. It is not another AI agent or a better prompt interface; it is a fundamentally different product architecture for turning AI capability into sustained business impact.

Budy 2 is built for a different experience. It keeps context, learns how its owner works, understands its role and responsibilities—not just one-time requests—and takes work forward within clear boundaries. It reflects on completed work: how it could have made the prior week more efficient, or completed a project faster, better, or at lower cost next time. Its owner can see what Budy is working on, what it has learned, and what it has completed. Instead of another chat window, Budy is a long-running teammate with a visible workspace and a growing understanding of the work that matters.

“We are not trying to turn every professional into an AI workflow engineer,” said [Founder Name], [Title] at Budy. “We are giving people who already see what needs to be built a new kind of computer—one they can teach, trust, and use to create far more leverage.”

Budy 2 is for high-agency, non-technical builders: founders, owner-operators, and functional leaders who are analytical, creative, and biased toward action. They may not code, but they know their work deeply and can recognize an opportunity when they see one. Budy does not prescribe a narrow set of use cases for them. It helps them get started, shows them what is possible, and gives them the tools to decide what is valuable.

It also makes AI more usable for the people around them. Many people who have avoided systems, processes, chatbots, or copilots are not resisting technology itself; they are resisting becoming its operator. Budy works through the familiar model of a teammate: it has a role, takes work forward, communicates when needed, and helps people participate without asking them to manage a maze of tools and threads.

docs.title: A first-day experience designed to change expectations
docs.text:
The promise of Budy 2 begins on the first day. Budy helps establish goals and working context, securely connects to the tools an owner chooses, and guides the user toward a meaningful first project. It is designed to create the feeling that early personal computers created for people who had only experimented with technology before: this is not just interesting—this changes what I can do.

The experience is deliberately white-glove, but delivered through Budy itself. We use advanced models and compute generously to make onboarding, learning, quality, and time to value feel unusually personal. Customers do not need a consulting engagement or human operator to make Budy work. Budy is designed to deliver that care and reliability through the product itself.

docs.title: Premium capability, priced to keep the promise
docs.text:
Budy 2 is not a $20 chatbot subscription. Reliable, persistent work requires strong models, secure access, visible controls, and an experience that earns trust. Budy is priced for customers with meaningful work and the authority to invest in compounding leverage.

People can begin with Explore, a paid evaluation tier expected to cost $200–$500 per month and provide roughly one-tenth of the capacity of a Part-Time Budy. Explore is designed to let a serious prospective customer use a credit card, reach a real outcome, and decide whether to buy Budy—not merely upgrade a lightweight plan. It is not a limited free trial or a freemium funnel.

Full Budy 2 plans begin with Part-Time at $5,000 per month, followed by Full-Time at $10,000 per month and Heavy / Max at $20,000+ per month. The plans differ by capacity: Full-Time provides roughly 2× Part-Time capacity, while Heavy / Max provides roughly 4× or more. docs.title: A Digital Teammate, not another AI agent
docs.text:
Budy 2 is general-purpose rather than industry-specific. It always acts as Budy—not as the owner or another person—and it operates only within permissions the owner has approved. Like a good remote employee, Budy acts where the decision is clear and the impact is limited or reversible, and asks when the stakes or ambiguity require it. The product makes work, context, access, decisions, and pending questions visible so that users can build trust through use rather than blind faith.

Chat may be one way to work with Budy. It is not the whole product. Budy 2 is a workspace, a persistent context, a set of tools, and an accountable long-running relationship with AI.

docs.title: Read this after the launch narrative
docs.text:
The recommended reading order is:

  1. Budy 2 Press Release — the product we want the world to understand and want.
  2. Budy 2 FAQ — the questions, trade-offs, and implications behind that launch narrative.
  3. This document — the durable choices that should guide our decisions after launch.

docs.title: The Vision: a New Personal Computer for Work
docs.text:
Budy 2 is a Digital Teammate: a new kind of personal computer for work. It is a long-running, capable AI counterpart that a professional can teach, delegate to, and grow with over time.

Today’s AI products are powerful, but most leave the user as the orchestrator. The user must supervise separate chats and tools, decide which thread matters, carry context between them, turn an impressive output into a working process, and keep the work moving. Basic AI workflows can help, but they are difficult for non-technical people to build and too unreliable to become a trusted part of meaningful work.

We believe there is a better model. A Budy has enduring context, a working identity, tools, memory, permissions, and a visible operating state. It can be taught how its owner works, take work forward within agreed boundaries, and improve through the relationship. It is not a chatbot, an assistant feature inside someone else’s platform, or a pre-packaged vertical agent. It is an agnostic platform for doing work.

The personal-computer analogy matters. Personal computers did not tell every person exactly what to make; they gave capable people an accessible, general-purpose tool and let them create value in ways the maker could not predict. Budy should do the same for work.

Many people have had the same experience with modern AI: an analysis, dashboard, or prototype produces a genuine “wow”—perhaps it even appears to make existing software unnecessary—then the promise fades when they try to implement it in the real world. The hard part is not generating a compelling answer. It is turning that answer into reliable, ongoing work. Budy 2 is built to close that gap. It is not a slightly better AI agent or another way to prompt an LLM; it is a fundamentally different architecture for creating business impact after the initial wow.

docs.title: Who Budy 2 Is For
docs.text:
We are not building for an industry, a job title, or every knowledge worker. We are building for a disposition: the high-agency, non-technical builder.

These people are analytical, creative, and strongly biased toward action. They see what needs to get done and enjoy figuring out how to make it happen. They may not write code or build AI workflows, but they have experimented with AI and understand its potential. They do not need us to prescribe every use case or decide what value means for them. They need to be inspired, equipped, and able to build.

They can be startup founders, owner-operators of service businesses, functional leaders, or executives in low-bureaucracy companies. A CMO, CFO, sales leader, or operations leader may all be a strong fit. Their teams can be small or large. What matters is that they can move quickly, have meaningful work to improve, and have authority to invest in a powerful solution.

This is intentionally a narrow intersection:

  • non-technical enough that building reliable AI systems alone is not realistic;
  • builder-minded enough to recognize and create value with a flexible platform;
  • action-oriented enough to teach, direct, and refine a Budy; and
  • sufficiently resourced to pay for a premium, reliable experience.

This focus is a product choice, not merely a marketing choice. A broad, cheap, generic product would force us to compromise on reliability, experience, and the depth of value we can deliver.

docs.title: The Job Budy Is Hired to Do
docs.text:
Our user’s central need is simple:

“Give me a capable, persistent teammate that understands my world, lets me teach it how I work, and reliably takes work forward without making me re-explain everything.”

Budy should create a first-day realization: this already moves meaningful work forward, and I can see how much further it can grow with me. The experience should feel like the moment an early computer user first encountered a computer that was genuinely usable and extensible—not another novelty to experiment with, but a new source of leverage.

We do not define every use case, every workflow, or every measure of value for the user. We provide a safe, legible, capable system; examples that spark ideas; and a way for users to teach Budy what matters. Some uses will have direct ROI and some will be personally or strategically valuable in ways only the user can judge. That is the point of a general-purpose tool.

docs.title: 1. Persistent, Personal, and Long-Running
docs.text:
Budy builds useful working context over time. It should know the owner’s goals, preferences, environment, past decisions, and active work without asking them to reconstruct that context every session. Context is valuable only when it is accurate, inspectable, and operationally useful; Budy must learn deliberately rather than accumulate noise.

Budy also has an enduring role and responsibilities. It should not treat work as a series of isolated requests: it uses what it has learned to connect tasks, notice recurring patterns, and reflect on how it could make future work faster, better, or more efficient. Meaningful changes to direction, scope, or authority remain the owner’s decision.

docs.title: 2. Tools for Builders, Not Prescriptions for Buyers
docs.text: We help users see what is possible and make it easy to begin. We do not require a sales or solutions team to determine what every customer should build. Budy earns adoption by helping its owner discover, teach, and extend valuable work themselves.

docs.title: 3. Powerful, but Legible
docs.text: The owner must be able to see what Budy is doing, what it has produced, what it needs, what it believes it knows, and where it needs approval. Chat can be a useful entry point, but it is not the product. The product needs a workspace where work, context, activity, decisions, access, and progress are visible.

docs.title: 4. Reliability Is the Product
docs.text: Users will delegate meaningful work only when Budy is dependable. We choose predictable execution, disciplined handoffs, clear escalation, and quality over superficial feature breadth or low cost. A Budy that does less reliably is more valuable than one that promises everything and cannot be trusted.

docs.title: 5. Safe, Scoped, and Accountable
docs.text: Budy always acts as Budy; it does not impersonate its owner or another person. Access and write permissions are explicit, scoped, and visible. Budy operates like a good employee: it takes decisions where it has clarity and where the impact is limited or readily reversible; it seeks clarification when a decision is ambiguous, consequential, or difficult to undo. It maintains an understandable trail of its work and never treats broad access as a default.

docs.title: 6. AI-Delivered White-Glove Experience
docs.text: The experience must feel unusually personal, thoughtful, and high-touch without requiring customer interaction with a salesperson, consultant, or human operator. We will use models, compute, and product intelligence liberally where they improve onboarding, teaching, guidance, quality, and time to value. Internal Agent Success review may support reliability where appropriate, but it is an operational safeguard—not the customer-facing product or a substitute for Budy's judgment.

docs.title: 7. Inspire, Then Compound
docs.text: The first session must produce a credible “wow”: Budy understands enough context and completes enough meaningful work to earn continued attention. From there, the relationship compounds. Each taught preference, approved action, and completed project should make Budy more useful and expand what its owner believes is possible.

docs.title: 8. Premium by Design
docs.text: We will not compromise the experience to fit a commodity AI subscription. Persistent context, dependable work, secure access, sophisticated models, and an exceptional first-use experience have a real cost. Budy is deliberately for people with high-leverage work and the budget to invest in it.

docs.title: 9. Adoption Should Feel Natural
docs.text: People who have historically avoided systems, processes, chatbots, and copilots do not adopt them merely because they are capable. Too often, those tools ask the person to become the operator: to maintain the process, supervise the threads, and translate outputs into action. Budy should instead fit the familiar model of working with a teammate. When it is done right, people begin using AI and more disciplined ways of working almost immediately because it feels like the way work should always have been done.

docs.title: Discover and Evaluate
docs.text: Users should be able to understand Budy, see credible examples, buy an evaluation tier with a credit card, and reach a meaningful result without a sales-led implementation process. Explore should feel like trying a powerful new computer in a store, through a friend, or at a library: enough real use to decide whether they need one of their own. The product and website must make both the promise and the intended user unmistakably clear.

docs.title: Set Up and Teach
docs.text: Onboarding is not a configuration burden handed to the user. Budy should actively help establish goals, gather relevant context, connect tools securely, suggest a valuable first project, and explain what it is learning. It should make sophisticated capability accessible without pretending the user is a workflow engineer.

docs.title: Delegate and Observe
docs.text: The owner can assign work, give feedback, and redirect Budy through the interface that is most natural for the moment. Budy then makes its work visible in a dedicated workspace: active work, completed outputs, decisions, questions, permissions, context, and next steps. Reports and notifications should drive decisions, not become an additional dashboard to maintain.

docs.title: Grow Beyond the First Win
docs.text: Budy should make it easy to add projects, tools, knowledge, and collaborators as trust grows. It can work with teams, but team collaboration is an extension of an owner’s relationship with Budy—not a prerequisite for receiving value. This matters especially for collaborators who have not adopted systems, processes, chatbots, or copilots in the past: Budy should make their participation feel like working with a teammate, not learning another system to operate.

docs.title: Commercial and Go-to-Market Principles
docs.text:
Our model is product-led acquisition and activation, not an industry-first sales motion. We will win by making a precise user feel immediately understood and by letting the product demonstrate exceptional value.

Product-led does not mean cheap, free, or low-touch in experience. It means that the product—not a salesperson, consultant, or human operator—is responsible for making the promise real.

We expect a paid Explore tier in the $200–$500/month range, with roughly one-tenth of the capacity of the Part-Time tier. It is a serious evaluation experience, not a freemium giveaway or a lower version of the product: a user with authority to spend $60k–$180k annually should be able to try Budy with a credit card, see real value quickly, and decide whether to buy their own full-capacity Budy. Explore may operate at break-even or a small loss because it is designed to prove the product’s potential.

The core offerings are premium monthly tiers:

Tier Indicative price Intended role Part-Time $5k/month The entry point for buying Budy: a full Budy with capacity for focused, high-leverage ongoing work Full-Time $10k/month A full Budy with roughly 2× Part-Time capacity Heavy / Max $20k+/month A full Budy at roughly 4× Part-Time capacity or higher

These names and prices are directional until the package boundaries are defined; “Heavy” or “Max” remains to be selected as the customer-facing name for the highest tier. A tenant may hold multiple Budy subscriptions, but each Budy remains a separate, evolving Digital Teammate with its own identity and capacity. The enduring principle is that Budy’s price must sustain the experience and the compute required to make it trustworthy.

docs.title: What We Will Not Be
docs.text:
• An industry-specific AI solution with a separate sales playbook for every vertical.
  • A low-cost chatbot or a collection of disposable prompts.
  • A consulting-led service that tells customers which use cases they should value.
  • An opaque agent that acts without boundaries, visibility, or accountability.
  • A human-operated service presented as autonomous software.

docs.title: How We Know We Are Succeeding
docs.text:
We will measure whether the right users reach value and deepen their relationship with Budy:

  • time to first meaningful outcome, especially on day one;
  • repeat delegation and continued use after the initial novelty;
  • the number and quality of new ways owners teach Budy to help;
  • trust signals: approvals, appropriate autonomy, and low need for corrective intervention;
  • retention, expansion, and willingness to recommend Budy to other high-agency builders; and
  • reliability and quality of completed work.

We will not confuse task volume, generic engagement, or a neatly calculated ROI claim with success. The true test is whether Budy becomes a source of compounding leverage that its owner would not want to give up.

docs.title: Appendix: Internal Architecture Principles
docs.text:
The user experiences one coherent Budy. Internally, we may separate reasoning and planning from predictable execution in order to protect reliability, cost, and safety.

  • Thinking Mode reasons about goals, context, learning, and how work should be approached. It has minimal direct execution capability by design.
  • Muscle Memory Mode performs defined, repeatable work predictably within the permissions and approach it has been given.

The handoff between these modes is a high-scrutiny boundary. It must turn intention into dependable execution without silently broadening scope, permissions, or authority. This architecture is a means to the product promise—not the product story itself.
